// config/build_workflows.dag -- Workflow spec and meta target types.
//
// Consolidates workflow and meta target type definitions used by the
// build system. Data declarations for core workflows and meta targets
// live in build_targets.dag; this module provides the types and any
// additional workflow metadata.

module config.build_workflows

// ── Workflow specification types ───────────────────────────────────────

type WorkflowKind = Tool | Pipeline | Workflow | Meta

type WorkflowSpec {
  name: String
  kind: WorkflowKind
  description: String
  dsl_module: String?
  entry_func: String?
  has_dry_run: Bool
}

// ── Meta target types ──────────────────────────────────────────────────

type MetaTarget {
  name: String
  description: String
  has_check: Bool
  has_fix: Bool
  command: String
  check_command: String?
  fix_command: String?
  command_prefix: String?
  resource_needs: List<ResourceNeed>
  fix_prerequisites: List<String>
}

type ResourceNeed {
  resource: String
  mode: String
}

// ── Workflow catalog ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
// Each DSL-invocable tool is a workflow spec. This data drives
// codegen (CLI entrypoints), makegen (Makefile targets), and
// the tool registry.

data workflow_specs: List<WorkflowSpec> = [
  { name: "bootstrap",      kind: Tool, description: "Generate bootstrap artifacts (.gitignore, clippy.toml)",
    dsl_module: "tools/bootstrap", entry_func: "bootstrap", has_dry_run: true },
  { name: "codegen",        kind: Tool, description: "Generate CLI entrypoints (DAG upsert)",
    dsl_module: "tools/codegen", entry_func: "codegen", has_dry_run: true },
  { name: "deps",           kind: Tool, description: "Manage workspace dependency configuration",
    dsl_module: "tools/deps", entry_func: "deps", has_dry_run: true },
  { name: "gist",           kind: Tool, description: "Create gist snapshot of workspace",
    dsl_module: "tools/gist", entry_func: "gist", has_dry_run: true },
  { name: "gist-diff",      kind: Tool, description: "Gist snapshot with diff against previous",
    dsl_module: "tools/gist", entry_func: "gist_diff", has_dry_run: true },
  { name: "gist-recent",    kind: Tool, description: "List recent gist snapshots",
    dsl_module: "tools/gist", entry_func: "gist_recent", has_dry_run: true },
  { name: "makegen",        kind: Tool, description: "Generate Makefile from tool registry",
    dsl_module: "tools/makegen", entry_func: "makegen", has_dry_run: true },
  { name: "pragma",         kind: Tool, description: "Generate pragma lint configuration",
    dsl_module: "tools/pragma", entry_func: "pragma", has_dry_run: true },
  { name: "testgen",        kind: Tool, description: "Generate tests from DAG structures and MockSpecs",
    dsl_module: "tools/testgen", entry_func: "testgen", has_dry_run: true },
  { name: "ci",             kind: Pipeline, description: "Run CI via workflow planner",
    dsl_module: None, entry_func: None, has_dry_run: false },
  { name: "test-all",       kind: Pipeline, description: "Run all tests via workflow planner",
    dsl_module: None, entry_func: None, has_dry_run: false }
]

```
// config/ci.dag -- Our CI configuration.
//
// Composes Layer 1 (extdeps) with our repo's CI requirements.
// Static configuration data declarations — things that don't change
// at runtime. Dynamic values (secrets, tool command) come from the
// extern bridge in tools/cigen.dag.
//
// Follows the config/build_targets.dag pattern: source of truth for
// generated CI artifacts.

module config.ci

import extdeps.github_actions {
  EnvVar, Permission, RunnerImage, Trigger, Checkout, Cache,
  ubuntu_latest
}
import extdeps.gitlab_ci { CacheConfig }

// ── Trigger ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

data ci_trigger: Trigger = {
  push_branches: ["main"],
  pr_branches: ["main"]
}

// ── Runner ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

data ci_runner: RunnerImage = ubuntu_latest

data ci_timeout_minutes: Int = 30

// ── Permissions ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────

data ci_permissions: List<Permission> = [
  { scope: "contents", level: "read" },
  { scope: "id-token", level: "write" }
]

// ── Environment ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────

data ci_env: List<EnvVar> = [
  { key: "CARGO_TERM_COLOR", value: "always" },
  { key: "RUSTFLAGS", value: "-D warnings" }
]

// ── Cache ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

data ci_cache_paths: List<String> = [
  "~/.cargo/bin/",
  "~/.cargo/registry/index/",
  "~/.cargo/registry/cache/",
  "~/.cargo/git/db/"
]

// ── Checkout ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

data ci_checkout: Checkout = {
  fetch_depth: 1,
  submodules: null
}

// ── Workflow identity ───────────────────────────────────────────────

data ci_workflow_name: String = "ci"
data ci_generator: String = "gunbc-codegen"
data ci_regen_command: String = "cargo run -p gunbc-app --bin gunbc-codegen -- cigen"

# dsl/config/clippy_policy.dag
```
// config/clippy_policy.dag -- Clippy enforcement policy (derived).
//
// Composes: extdeps/clippy.dag (what clippy can configure)
//         + config/arch_rules.dag (our invariants + exemptions)
//         + config/clippy_disallowed.dag (what we disallow)
//         → concrete clippy.toml content, allowlist, lint policy.
//
// All derivation is pure DSL. Data flows from arch_rules + clippy_disallowed
// into the derive_* functions via explicit parameters.

module config.clippy_policy

import extdeps.clippy {
  ClippySpec,
  DisallowedMethodEntry,
  DisallowedTypeEntry,
  ClippyTomlConfig,
  spec
}

import config.arch_rules {
  AllowlistPattern,
  BoundaryRule,
  Exemption,
  DeadCodeAllowance,
  allowlist_patterns,
  boundary_rules,
  exemptions,
  dead_code_allowances,
  pragma_allow_lints,
  large_error_threshold
}

import config.clippy_disallowed {
  DisallowedMethodGroup,
  DisallowedTypeGroup,
  disallowed_method_groups,
  disallowed_type_groups
}

// ── Derivation output types ─────────────────────────────────────────

type AllowlistEntry {
  pattern: String
  rationale: String
}

type LintPolicyOutput {
  allow_dead_code: List<String>
  allow_lints: List<String>
}

// ── Rendering helpers ───────────────────────────────────────────────

fn render_method_entry(entry: DisallowedMethodEntry) -> String {
  "    { path = \"{entry.path}\", reason = \"{entry.reason}\" },"
}

fn render_type_entry(entry: DisallowedTypeEntry) -> String {
  "    { path = \"{entry.path}\", reason = \"{entry.reason}\" },"
}

fn render_method_group(group: DisallowedMethodGroup) -> String {
  let comments = group.comments |> map(c => "    # {c}") |> join("\n")
  let entries = group.entries |> map(e => render_method_entry(entry: e)) |> join("\n")
  "{comments}\n{entries}"
}

fn render_type_group(group: DisallowedTypeGroup) -> String {
  let comments = group.comments |> map(c => "    # {c}") |> join("\n")
  let entries = group.entries |> map(e => render_type_entry(entry: e)) |> join("\n")
  "{comments}\n{entries}"
}

fn scope_label(scope: ExemptionScope) -> String {
  match scope {
    WholePackage(pkg) => pkg.name,
    PackagePrefix(pp) => pp.prefix + "*",
    PackageFile(pf) => pf.package_name + "/" + pf.path,
    PackagePathPrefix(pp) => pp.package_name + "/" + pp.prefix + "*"
  }
}

fn render_exceptions_list(exs: List<Exemption>) -> String {
  exs |> map(e => "#   - " + scope_label(scope: e.scope) + " (" + e.rationale + ")") |> join("\n")
}

// ── Derivation functions ────────────────────────────────────────────

fn derive_clippy_toml(
  threshold: Int,
  crate_exemptions: List<Exemption>,
  method_groups: List<DisallowedMethodGroup>,
  type_groups: List<DisallowedTypeGroup>
) -> String {
  let header = "# Generated by gunbc-clippy\n# DO NOT EDIT - regenerate with: cargo run -p gunbc-app --bin gunbc-pragma"
  let desc = "# Clippy configuration for gunbc\n#\n# BuilderError is intentionally large (144 bytes) to contain diagnostic info.\n# Increase the threshold to allow it in Result types.\nlarge-error-threshold = {threshold}"
  let exceptions = render_exceptions_list(exs: crate_exemptions)
  let invariants = "# This configuration enforces system invariants:\n#\n# I6. NO ESCAPE HATCHES\n#     The system cannot be bypassed. If I/O must go through transport,\n#     there's no function to call to skip it.\n#\n# I7. NO FALLBACKS\n#     Operations either succeed or fail. No silent degradation.\n#     Don't use .unwrap_or_default() to hide errors.\n#\n# I8. NO WARNINGS\n#     Run with: cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings\n#     Warnings are errors. If something is wrong, the build fails.\n#\n# APPROVED EXCEPTIONS (must have documented reason):\n{exceptions}\n#\n# To add an exception: #[allow(clippy::disallowed_methods)] with comment."
  let methods = method_groups |> map(g => render_method_group(group: g)) |> join("\n    \n")
  let types = type_groups |> map(g => render_type_group(group: g)) |> join("\n    \n")
  "{header}\n\n{desc}\n\n{invariants}\n\ndisallowed-methods = [\n{methods}\n]\n\ndisallowed-types = [\n{types}\n]\n"
}

fn derive_disallowed_methods_allowlist(patterns: List<AllowlistPattern>) -> String {
  let header = "# Generated by gunbc-pragma\n# DO NOT EDIT - regenerate with: cargo run -p gunbc-app --bin gunbc-pragma\n"
  let desc = "# Allowed path prefixes for #[allow(clippy::disallowed_methods)] and #[allow(clippy::disallowed_types)].\n# Format: prefix (repo-relative)\n# Note: any path containing \"/tests/\" is always allowed.\n#\n"
  let entries = patterns |> map(p => "# {p.rationale}\n{p.pattern}\n") |> join("")
  "{header}{desc}{entries}"
}

fn derive_pragma_lint_policy(dead_code: List<DeadCodeAllowance>, allow_lints: List<String>) -> String {
  let dead_code_paths = dead_code |> map(d => d.fallback_path) |> join("\n")
  let lint_names = allow_lints |> join("\n")
  "# Generated by gunbc-pragma\n# DO NOT EDIT - regenerate with: cargo run -p gunbc-app --bin gunbc-pragma\n\n[allow.dead_code]\n{dead_code_paths}\n\n[allow.lints]\n{lint_names}\n"
}
```

# dsl/config/test_policy.dag
```
// config/test_policy.dag -- Repo-specific test classification policy.
//
// Classification logic lives in std/fidelity.dag (classify_transports),
// evaluated at compile time via evaluate_fn_body(). This file provides
// repo-specific policy knobs: budget thresholds and budget checking.
//
// Like build_policy.dag is this repo's build choices, test_policy.dag is
// this repo's test classification choices.

module config.test_policy

import std.types { FermiDepth }

// Default CI budget (skip tests more expensive than this)
data default_ci_budget: FermiDepth = Xl

// Default local budget (skip expensive tests locally)
data default_local_budget: FermiDepth = S

// --- Budget comparison -----------------------------------------------

fn depth_ordinal(depth: String) -> Int {
  match depth {
    "XS" => 0
    "S"  => 1
    "M"  => 2
    "L"  => 3
    "XL" => 4
    _    => 5
  }
}

// Check if a depth string is within a budget string.
fn within_budget(depth: String, budget: String) -> Bool {
  depth_ordinal(depth: depth) <= depth_ordinal(depth: budget)
}

// config/workspace.dag -- Workspace crate declarations.
//
// Single source of truth for the gunbc workspace structure. Each crate
// is declared with its path, crate name, and layer classification.
// A CI drift test verifies this data matches the actual Cargo.toml.

module config.workspace

// ── Types ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

type CrateLayer = Core | Compiler | Library | Tool | Repo

type CrateSpec {
  path: String
  name: String
  layer: CrateLayer
}

// ── Workspace members ──────────────────────────────────────────────────

data workspace_crates: List<CrateSpec> = [
  // Core crates (handwritten foundation)
  { path: "core/infra",                     name: "gunbc-infra",                  layer: Core },
  { path: "core/ir",                        name: "gunbc-ir",                     layer: Core },
  { path: "core/exec",                      name: "gunbc-exec",                   layer: Core },
  { path: "core/resolve",                   name: "gunbc-resolve",                layer: Core },
  { path: "core/workflow",                  name: "gunbc-workflow",               layer: Core },
  { path: "core/cli",                       name: "gunbc-cli",                    layer: Core },
  { path: "core/codegen",                   name: "gunbc-codegen",                layer: Core },
  { path: "core/test",                      name: "gunbc-test",                   layer: Core },
  { path: "core/testgen-registry",          name: "gunbc-testgen-registry",       layer: Core },
  { path: "core/testgen-registry-macros",   name: "gunbc-testgen-registry-macros", layer: Core },
  { path: "core/delegate-macros",           name: "gunbc-delegate-macros",        layer: Core },
  // DSL compiler (daglang)
  { path: "core/daglang/daglang-syntax",    name: "daglang-syntax",              layer: Compiler },
  { path: "core/daglang/daglang-contract",  name: "daglang-contract",            layer: Compiler },
  { path: "core/daglang/daglang-resolve",   name: "daglang-resolve",             layer: Compiler },
  { path: "core/daglang/daglang-typecheck", name: "daglang-typecheck",           layer: Compiler },
  { path: "core/daglang/daglang-lower",     name: "daglang-lower",               layer: Compiler },
  { path: "core/daglang/daglang-derive",    name: "daglang-derive",              layer: Compiler },
  { path: "core/daglang/daglang-emit",      name: "daglang-emit",                layer: Compiler },
  { path: "core/daglang/daglang-driver",    name: "daglang-driver",              layer: Compiler },
  { path: "core/daglang/daglang-cli",       name: "daglang-cli",                 layer: Compiler },
  // Library crates (DAG op libraries)
  { path: "lib/primitives",                 name: "gunbc-primitives",             layer: Library },
  { path: "lib/blob",                       name: "gunbc-lib-blob",              layer: Library },
  { path: "lib/cloud-ops",                  name: "gunbc-lib-cloud-ops",         layer: Library },
  { path: "lib/aws-ops",                    name: "gunbc-lib-aws-ops",           layer: Library },
  { path: "lib/llm-ops",                    name: "gunbc-lib-llm-ops",           layer: Library },
  { path: "lib/review",                     name: "gunbc-lib-review",            layer: Library },
  { path: "lib/design-ops",                 name: "gunbc-design-ops",            layer: Library },
  { path: "lib/transport",                  name: "gunbc-lib-transport",         layer: Library },
  { path: "lib/gcp-ops",                    name: "gunbc-lib-gcp-ops",           layer: Library },
  // General tool definitions (reusable by any project)
  { path: "lib/tools/deps",                 name: "gunbc-deps",                  layer: Tool },
  { path: "lib/tools/clippy",               name: "gunbc-clippy",                layer: Tool },
  // Repo-specific configuration (gunbc's own DAGs)
  { path: "gunbc-app",                      name: "gunbc-app",                   layer: Repo }
]

# dsl/examples/abstract_services.dag
```
// examples/abstract_services.dag -- EXPLORATION: Abstract service modeling.
//
// STATUS: Forward-looking proposal. Not yet part of the spec.
//
// PROBLEM: Current service declarations are concrete -- every service has
// hard-coded transport annotations (@rest, @shell). This means:
//   1. You can't swap implementations (test vs staging vs production)
//   2. You can't compose services (higher-level from lower-level)
//   3. You can't write funcs against an abstract contract
//   4. You can't bind the implementation at deploy time
//
// PROPOSAL: Three-layer model:
//   interface  -- abstract contract (what operations, what types, what properties)
//   service    -- concrete implementation (how operations are fulfilled)
//   bind       -- deployment-time wiring (which implementation to use where)
//
// This is dependency injection at the language level.

module examples.abstract_services

import std.types { FilePath }


// =========================================================================
// LAYER 1: Interfaces (Abstract Contracts)
// =========================================================================
//
// An interface defines WHAT a service provides, not HOW.
// Think: Go interface, Rust trait, Java interface.
//
// Key properties:
//   - Pure declarations (no transport, no endpoints)
//   - Behavioral contracts (@contract) for verification
//   - Composable (interfaces can extend other interfaces)

// --- Storage interface ---------------------------------------------------
// Any key-value storage backend: GCS, S3, local filesystem, Redis, etc.

interface Storage {
  operation Get(key: String) -> { value: Bytes?, found: Bool }
    idempotent
    readonly

  operation Put(key: String, value: Bytes) -> { ok: Bool }
    idempotent
    readonly

  operation Delete(key: String) -> { ok: Bool }
    idempotent
    readonly

  operation List(prefix: String) -> { keys: List<String> }
    idempotent
    readonly

  // Behavioral contracts -- the compiler uses these for:
  //   1. Test generation (verify implementations obey the contract)
  //   2. Static analysis (reason about program behavior)
  //   3. Documentation
}

// --- LLM interface -------------------------------------------------------
// Any language model backend: OpenAI, Gemini, Claude, local llama.cpp, etc.

interface LLM {
  type Message {
    role: String          // "system" | "user" | "assistant"
    content: String
  }

  type Usage {
    prompt_tokens: Int
    completion_tokens: Int
    total_tokens: Int
  }

  operation Complete(
    messages: List<Message>,
    temperature: Float = 0.3,
    max_tokens: Int?
  ) -> { content: String, usage: Usage }

  operation Embed(text: String) -> { embedding: List<Float>, dimensions: Int }

  // Contracts
}

// --- Queue interface -----------------------------------------------------
// Any pub/sub backend: Pub/Sub, SQS, Kafka, in-memory channel, etc.

interface AbstractQueue<T> {
  operation Publish(message: T) -> { message_id: String }
  operation Pull(max_messages: Int = 1) -> { messages: List<{ id: String, body: T }> }
  operation Ack(message_id: String) -> { ok: Bool }
}

// --- Interface composition -----------------------------------------------
// Interfaces can extend other interfaces.

interface DurableStorage : Storage {
  operation Snapshot(key: String) -> { version: String }

  operation Restore(key: String, version: String) -> { ok: Bool }
}


// =========================================================================
// LAYER 2: Services (Concrete Implementations)
// =========================================================================
//
// A service implements an interface with specific transport and endpoints.
// The `service X : InterfaceName` syntax means X fulfills InterfaceName.
//
// The compiler verifies that every operation in the interface is implemented
// and that the types match.

// --- GCS implements Storage ----------------------------------------------

service gcs.Storage : Storage {

  config {
    bucket: String          // bound at deploy time
    project_id: String
  }

  operation Get {
    input { key: String }
    output { value: Bytes?, found: Bool }
  }

  operation Put {
    input { key: String, value: Bytes }
    output { ok: Bool }
  }

  operation Delete {
    input { key: String }
    output { ok: Bool }
  }

  operation List {
    input { prefix: String }
    output { keys: List<String> }
  }
}

// --- S3 implements Storage -----------------------------------------------

service aws.S3 : Storage {

  config {
    bucket: String
    region: String = "us-east-1"
  }

  operation Get {
    input { key: String }
    output { value: Bytes?, found: Bool }
  }

  operation Put {
    input { key: String, value: Bytes }
    output { ok: Bool }
  }

  operation Delete {
    input { key: String }
    output { ok: Bool }
  }

  operation List {
    input { prefix: String }
    output { keys: List<String> }
  }
}

// --- Local filesystem implements Storage ---------------------------------
// For testing and local development.

service local.FileStore : Storage {
  config {
    base_dir: FilePath = "/tmp/dag-store"
  }

  operation Get {
    input { key: String }
    output { value: Bytes?, found: Bool }
  }

  operation Put {
    input { key: String, value: Bytes }
    output { ok: Bool }
  }

  operation Delete {
    input { key: String }
    output { ok: Bool }
  }

  operation List {
    input { prefix: String }
    output { keys: List<String> }
  }
}

// --- OpenAI implements LLM -----------------------------------------------

service openai.ChatGPT : LLM {

  config {
    model: String = "gpt-4"
    organization: String?
  }

  operation Complete {
    input {
      messages: List<Message>,
      temperature: Float = 0.3,
      max_tokens: Int?
    }
    output { content: String, usage: Usage }
  }

  operation Embed {
    input { text: String }
    output { embedding: List<Float>, dimensions: Int }
  }
}

// --- Vertex AI implements LLM --------------------------------------------

service gcp.VertexAI : LLM {

  config {
    project_id: String
    region: String = "us-central1"
    model: String = "gemini-pro"
  }

  operation Complete {
    input {
      messages: List<Message>,
      temperature: Float = 0.3,
      max_tokens: Int?
    }
    output { content: String, usage: Usage }
  }

  operation Embed {
    input { text: String }
    output { embedding: List<Float>, dimensions: Int }
  }
}


// =========================================================================
// LAYER 3: Writing funcs against interfaces
// =========================================================================
//
// Funcs declare dependency on INTERFACES, not concrete services.
// The compiler threads the interface through the func's node graph.
// Which concrete service fulfills the interface is decided at deploy time.

// A func that works with ANY storage backend
func save_artifact(key: String, content: Bytes) -> { ok: Bool }
  uses store: Storage                    // abstract -- not gcs, not s3, not local
{
  existing = store.Get(key: key)
  result = match existing.found {
    true  => store.Put(key: "{key}.v2", value: content)
    false => store.Put(key: key, value: content)
  }
  return { ok: result.ok }
}

// A func that works with ANY LLM backend
func review_code(diff: String, system_prompt: String?) -> { review: String }
  uses llm: LLM                         // abstract -- not openai, not vertex
{
  messages = [
    { role: "system", content: system_prompt ?? "You are a code reviewer." },
    { role: "user", content: "Review this diff:\n\n{diff}" }
  ]
  result = llm.Complete(messages: messages, temperature: 0.3, max_tokens: None)
  return { review: result.content }
}

// Composing multiple abstract services
func review_and_store(diff: String) -> { review: String, stored: Bool }
  uses llm: LLM
  uses store: Storage
{
  review = review_code(diff: diff, system_prompt: None)
  stored = save_artifact(
    key: "reviews/{hash(diff)}.md",
    content: review.review |> to_bytes()
  )
  return { review: review.review, stored: stored.ok }
}


// =========================================================================
// WHAT THIS ENABLES
// =========================================================================
//
// 1. TESTING: The compiler auto-generates tests against Storage/LLM
//    contracts. `review_code` can be tested with a mock LLM that
//    verifies the contract (non-empty response for non-empty messages).
//
// 2. PORTABILITY: The same func works on GCS, S3, or local filesystem.
//    No code changes, just different deploy bindings.
//
// 3. COMPOSITION: Services compose through interfaces. A `CachedStorage`
//    could implement Storage by wrapping another Storage + a Cache.
//
// 4. SCALING: New backends (Azure Blob, MinIO, etc.) just implement
//    the Storage interface. All existing funcs work automatically.
//
// 5. GRADUAL MIGRATION: Start with local.FileStore for development,
//    switch to gcs.Storage for production, without touching func code.
//
// The binding happens in deploy blocks (see deployment.dag).
```

# dsl/examples/deployment.dag
```
// examples/deployment.dag -- Multi-cloud infra composition.
//
// Shows the full holistic binding across providers:
//   1. Abstract interfaces let business logic target capabilities, not providers
//   2. Provider-specific resources implement the interfaces
//   3. Provider selection happens at compile time via environment config
//   4. Cross-provider composition works naturally
//   5. Integration tests generate for any provider
//
// Reading order:
//   infra/core.dag       -- Abstract interfaces (ObjectStorage, Compute, etc.)
//   infra/spec.dag       -- Provider-neutral spec types
//   infra/gcp/           -- GCP implementations
//   infra/aws/           -- AWS implementations
//   infra/azure/         -- Azure implementations
//   (this file)          -- Composition examples

module examples.deployment

import infra.core { ObjectStorage, Compute, SecretStore, Identity, Queue, CloudConfig, InfraEnvironment, Environment }
import infra.spec { ReconcileResult }

// --- Provider resources ---
import infra.gcp.resources { GcsBucket, CloudRunService, ManagedSecret, GcpServiceAccount, WifProvider, PubSubTopic }
import infra.gcp.config as gcp_config
import infra.aws.resources { S3Bucket, LambdaFunction, AwsSecret, AwsIamRole, SqsQueue }
import infra.aws.config as aws_config
import infra.azure.resources { BlobContainer, ContainerApp, KeyVaultSecret, AzureManagedIdentity, ServiceBusQueue }
import infra.azure.config as azure_config

import std.types { NonEmptyStr, CommitSha, Url }


// =========================================================================
// 1. ABSTRACT INTERFACE -- Provider-agnostic business logic
// =========================================================================
//
// Business logic writes against ObjectStorage. It does NOT know whether
// the backend is GCS, S3, or Azure Blob -- that's resolved at compile time.

func store_artifact(key: NonEmptyStr, content: Bytes) -> { ok: Bool }
  uses store: ObjectStorage
{
  result = store.write(key: key, content: content)
  return { ok: result.ok }
}

func read_artifact(key: NonEmptyStr) -> { content: Bytes, found: Bool }
  uses store: ObjectStorage
{
  result = store.read(key: key)
  return { content: result.content, found: result.found }
}

// Compiler resolves `ObjectStorage` to the concrete provider based on
// the environment config at build time:
//   gunbc build --env=gcp-dev  -> ObjectStorage = GcsBucket
//   gunbc build --env=aws-dev  -> ObjectStorage = S3Bucket
//   gunbc build --env=azure    -> ObjectStorage = BlobContainer


// =========================================================================
// 2. PROVIDER-SPECIFIC -- Direct resource usage (GCP)
// =========================================================================
//
// You can also use concrete resources directly when you need
// provider-specific features (e.g., GCS storage classes, S3 versioning).

func store_artifact_gcp(content: String, key: NonEmptyStr) -> { ok: Bool }
  uses bucket: GcsBucket(name: "gunbc-artifacts", project_id: "gunbai-auto")
{
  result = bucket.write(key: key, content: content |> to_bytes())
  return { ok: result.ok }
}


// =========================================================================
// 3. CROSS-PROVIDER COMPOSITION
// =========================================================================
//
// A func that uses resources from DIFFERENT providers.
// The compiler provisions each resource via the correct provider API.

func cross_cloud_pipeline(
  content: Bytes,
  notification: String
) -> { stored_gcp: Bool, stored_aws: Bool, notified: Bool }
  uses gcs: GcsBucket(name: "gunbc-primary", project_id: "gunbai-auto")
  uses s3: S3Bucket(name: "gunbc-backup", region: "us-east-1")
  uses queue: SqsQueue(name: "gunbc-notifications", region: "us-east-1")
{
  // Write to GCS (primary)
  gcp_result = gcs.write(key: "data/latest.bin", content: content)

  // Replicate to S3 (backup)
  aws_result = s3.write(key: "data/latest.bin", content: content)

  // Notify via SQS
  notify = queue.publish(message: notification) [after gcp_result, after aws_result]

  return {
    stored_gcp: gcp_result.ok,
    stored_aws: aws_result.ok,
    notified: notify.ok
  }
}

// Compiler generates:
//   1. Acquire GcsBucket via GCP APIs (check -> create -> resolve)
//   2. Acquire S3Bucket via AWS APIs (HeadBucket -> CreateBucket)
//   3. Acquire SqsQueue via AWS APIs (GetQueueUrl -> CreateQueue)
//   4. gcs.write and s3.write run in parallel (independent)
//   5. queue.publish runs after both writes complete
//   6. Each provider's auth chain is resolved independently


// =========================================================================
// 5. PROVIDER SELECTION VIA CONFIG
// =========================================================================
//
// Same business logic, different provider per environment.
// The environment config determines which concrete resource backs
// each abstract interface.

fn storage_for_env(env: InfraEnvironment) -> ObjectStorage {
  match env.cloud {
    GcpConfig { project, ... } =>
      GcsBucket(name: "gunbc-artifacts", project_id: project)
    AwsConfig { region, ... } =>
      S3Bucket(name: "gunbc-artifacts", region: region)
    AzureConfig { ... } =>
      BlobContainer(account_name: "gunbcartifacts", name: "artifacts")
  }
}

fn compute_for_env(env: InfraEnvironment) -> Compute {
  match env.cloud {
    GcpConfig { project, region, ... } =>
      CloudRunService(
        name: "gunbc-api", project_id: project, region: region,
        image: "gcr.io/{project_id}/gunbc-api:latest"
      )
    AwsConfig { region, ... } =>
      LambdaFunction(
        name: "gunbc-api", region: region,
        role_arn: "arn:aws:iam::*:role/gunbc-lambda",
        code_s3_bucket: "gunbc-deploy", code_s3_key: "lambda/api.zip"
      )
    AzureConfig { subscription_id, resource_group, location, ... } =>
      ContainerApp(
        name: "gunbc-api",
        subscription_id: subscription_id,
        resource_group: resource_group,
        location: location,
        image: "gunbcregistry.azurecr.io/api:latest"
      )
  }
}

// Usage: build-time resolution
//   gunbc build --env=gcp-dev    -> storage_for_env(gcp_config.gcp_dev_config())
//   gunbc build --env=aws-prod   -> storage_for_env(aws_config.aws_prod_config())


// =========================================================================
// 6. FULL MULTI-CLOUD DEPLOYMENT
// =========================================================================
//
// Deploy a complete application stack to any cloud provider.
// The func composes compute + storage + secrets + identity.

func deploy_api(env: InfraEnvironment) -> { url: Url, ready: Bool }
  uses compute: Compute
  uses store: ObjectStorage
  uses secrets: SecretStore
  uses identity: Identity
{
  // Identity: acquire service identity
  token = identity.assume(
    scopes: ["https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"],
    lifetime_seconds: 3600
  )

  // Secrets: read API credentials
  api_key = secrets.read_value()

  // Compute: deploy the service
  deployed = compute.deploy(
    image: "gunbc-api:latest",
    env: { "STORAGE_BACKEND": "abstract", "API_KEY_SECRET": "ref:secrets" }
  ) [after token, after api_key]

  // Storage: verify bucket/container is ready
  url = compute.get_url() [after deployed]

  return { url: url.url, ready: deployed.ok }
}


// =========================================================================
// 7. GCP-SPECIFIC FULL BOOTSTRAP (concrete)
// =========================================================================

func infra_bootstrap_gcp() -> { ready: Bool }
  uses wif: WifProvider(
    project_number: "314501921854",
    pool_id: "github-pool",
    provider_id: "github",
    issuer_uri: "https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com",
    attribute_mapping: {
      "google.subject": "assertion.sub",
      "attribute.repository": "assertion.repository"
    },
    attribute_condition: "assertion.repository_owner == 'org-name'"
  )
  uses deployer_sa: GcpServiceAccount(
    name: "gunbai-deployer",
    project_id: "gunbai-auto",
    display_name: "GitHub Actions Deployer",
    roles: ["roles/iam.serviceAccountAdmin", "roles/secretmanager.admin"]
  )
  uses github_token: ManagedSecret(
    project_id: "gunbai-secrets",
    secret_id: "github-token",
    prefix: "dev-"
  )
  uses artifacts_bucket: GcsBucket(name: "gunbc-artifacts", project_id: "gunbai-auto")
  uses notifications: PubSubTopic(name: "gunbc-events", project_id: "gunbai-auto")
{
  // All resources acquired. Compiler orders:
  //   WIF -> ServiceAccount -> Secret -> Bucket, PubSub (parallel)
  return { ready: true }
}


// =========================================================================
// 8. AWS-SPECIFIC FULL BOOTSTRAP (concrete)
// =========================================================================

func infra_bootstrap_aws() -> { ready: Bool }
  uses role: AwsIamRole(
    name: "gunbc-deployer",
    assume_role_policy: {
      "Version": "2012-10-17",
      "Statement": [{
        "Effect": "Allow",
        "Principal": { "Federated": "arn:aws:iam::*:oidc-provider/token.actions.githubusercontent.com" },
        "Action": "sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity",
        "Condition": { "StringEquals": { "token.actions.githubusercontent.com:aud": "sts.amazonaws.com" } }
      }]
    },
    managed_policy_arns: [
      "arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/AmazonS3FullAccess",
      "arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/SecretsManagerReadWrite"
    ]
  )
  uses api_key: AwsSecret(name: "gunbc/github-token", region: "us-east-1")
  uses artifacts: S3Bucket(name: "gunbc-artifacts", region: "us-east-1")
  uses notifications: SqsQueue(name: "gunbc-events", region: "us-east-1")
{
  return { ready: true }
}


// =========================================================================
// 9. INTEGRATION TEST GENERATION (multi-cloud)
// =========================================================================
//
// For `store_artifact` using ObjectStorage, the compiler generates tests
// for EACH provider implementation:
//
// --- Per-provider DryRun (cost XS) ---
//   GcsBucket: mock GCP APIs, verify DAG completes
//   S3Bucket: mock AWS APIs, verify DAG completes
//   BlobContainer: mock Azure APIs, verify DAG completes
//
// --- Contract verification (cost S) ---
//   For each provider: write(k,v) then read(k) => found: true, content: v
//   Tests that the @contract from ObjectStorage holds for all implementations
//
// --- Cross-provider scenario (cost M) ---
//   cross_cloud_pipeline: mock GCP + AWS APIs, verify parallel writes
//   and sequential notification

func store_and_verify(key: NonEmptyStr, content: Bytes) -> { stored: Bool, verified: Bool }
  uses store: ObjectStorage
{
  write_result = store.write(key: key, content: content)
  read_result = store.read(key: key) [after write_result]
  verified = read_result.found && read_result.content == content
  return { stored: write_result.ok, verified: verified }
}


// =========================================================================
// 10. ENVIRONMENT CONFIGS (all providers)
// =========================================================================

// Provider-specific dev storage helpers intentionally omitted until
// named-config record typing for concrete resource constructors lands.

// Build command selects the provider:
//   gunbc build --env=gcp-dev     -> GcsBucket with gcp_dev_storage()
//   gunbc build --env=aws-dev     -> S3Bucket with aws_dev_storage()
//   gunbc build --env=azure-dev   -> BlobContainer with azure_dev_storage()
```

// examples/integration_tests.dag -- Test generation for infra-backed funcs.
//
// Shows what the compiler generates for funcs that use infra resources.
// The key insight: infra resources have @mock_response annotations in
// their acquire blocks, plus testgen already knows the probe-observer
// model. Combining these gives us multi-tier integration tests for free.
//
// Tiers (from cheapest to most expensive):
//   1. Hermetic unit (mocked transport, structural validity)
//   2. Contract (per-node correctness with mock probes/observers)
//   3. Scenario (guard paths: resource exists / missing / stale)
//   4. Resource hygiene (lifecycle invariants)
//   5. Live integration (real GCP APIs, gated by cost + secrets)
//   6. End-to-end (full pipeline with real infra)

module examples.integration_tests

import infra.gcp.resources { GcsBucket, ManagedSecret, CloudRunService }
import infra.spec { EnvironmentConfig }


// =========================================================================
// SOURCE FUNC (the thing we're testing)
// =========================================================================

func upload_artifact(key: NonEmptyStr, content: Bytes) -> { url: Url, stored: Bool }
  uses bucket: GcsBucket(name: "gunbc-artifacts", project_id: "gunbai-auto")
{
  write = bucket.write(key: key, content: content)
  url = "gs://gunbc-artifacts/{key}" as Url
  return { url: url, stored: write.ok }
}


// =========================================================================
// TIER 1: HERMETIC UNIT (compiler generates automatically)

// Generated test structure:

//   @test(tier: Unit, cost: XS, hermetic: true)

//     // Probes: entry inputs

//
//     // All transport mocked using @mock_response from GcsBucket.acquire:
//     mock(GcsBucket.acquire.check, status: 404)
//     mock(GcsBucket.acquire.create, status: 200, body: { name: "gunbc-artifacts" })
//     mock(GcsBucket.acquire.resolve, status: 200, body: { name: "gunbc-artifacts" })
//     mock(bucket.write, status: 200, body: { ok: true })
//

//

//
// What the compiler knows to generate this:
//   - Input types from func signature -> probe generation
//   - @mock_response from GcsBucket resource -> transport mocks
//   - Output types from func signature -> observer assertions
//   - Seed policy: key/content are semantic carriers -> must be seeded


// =========================================================================
// TIER 2: NODE CONTRACTS (compiler generates per-node)
// =========================================================================
//
// For each node in the expanded DAG, the compiler generates a focused test.
// This includes the acquire nodes from the resource.

//
// When a service implements an interface with @contract annotations,

// =========================================================================
// CONTENT ENCODING COVERAGE (from content-indexed file types)
// =========================================================================
//
// When a func uses Filesystem.read on paths from an unclassified source
// (like git.Core.LsFiles), the content encoding type system creates new
// test obligations. This models BOTH sides of the I/O equation:
//   Producer side: git.Core.LsFiles() → List<FilePath>  (mixed content)
//   Consumer side: fs.read(TextFilePath) → String        (text only)
//
// The gap ⟦FilePath⟧ \ ⟦TextFilePath⟧ = ⟦BinaryFilePath⟧ is the set of
// paths that would crash fs.read. The classify_files / read_text_files
// patterns bridge this gap, and the compiler generates tests to verify
// the bridge works.
//
// SOURCE FUNC (using read_text_files to handle mixed content):
//
//   func snapshot_files(paths: List<FilePath>) -> { markdown: String, skipped: Int }
//     uses fs: Filesystem(mode: Read)
//   {
//     result = read_text_files(paths: paths)
//     markdown = render(files: result.files)
//     return { markdown: markdown, skipped: result.skipped |> length() }
//   }
//
//
// --- Compile-time: what the OLD code looked like (before content types) ---
//
//   func snapshot_files_BROKEN(paths: List<FilePath>) -> { markdown: String }
//     uses fs: Filesystem(mode: Read)
//   {
//     contents = for file in paths {
//       fs.read(path: file)        // COMPILE ERROR: ⟦FilePath⟧ ⊄ ⟦TextFilePath⟧
//     }                             // fs.read requires TextFilePath, got FilePath
//   }
//
// The compiler rejects this because Filesystem.read takes TextFilePath
// and `paths` is List<FilePath> (unclassified). The developer must insert
// an explicit classification step (classify_files or read_text_files).
//
//
// --- Generated: Encoding Branch Scenarios (Bucket C extension) ---
//
// The classify_files pattern contains a coproduct branch:
//   encoding != Binary → TextFilePath
//   encoding == Binary → BinaryFilePath
//
// The compiler generates scenarios for each branch of the partition,
// using @file_types to produce realistic mock file lists:
//
//   @test(tier: Scenario, cost: S, hermetic: true, scenario: "all_text_files")
//   func test_snapshot_all_text() {
//     mock(git.Core.LsFiles, { files: ["src/main.rs", "Cargo.toml"] })
//     mock(fs.probe, [
//       { classification: { path: "src/main.rs", encoding: UTF8, size: 100, mime: "text/x-rust" } },
//       { classification: { path: "Cargo.toml", encoding: UTF8, size: 50, mime: "text/plain" } }
//     ])
//     mock(fs.read, [
//       { content: "fn main() {}" },
//       { content: "[package]\nname = \"test\"" }
//     ])
//
//     result = execute(snapshot_files, { paths: ["src/main.rs", "Cargo.toml"] })
//     assert result.skipped == 0
//     assert result.markdown is String
//   }
//
//   @test(tier: Scenario, cost: S, hermetic: true, scenario: "mixed_content")
//   func test_snapshot_mixed_files() {
//     // Mock: LsFiles returns text AND binary files
//     // Generated from @file_types: ".rs" → text, ".pdf" → binary
//     mock(git.Core.LsFiles, { files: ["src/main.rs", "docs/spec.pdf", "README.md"] })
//     mock(fs.probe, [
//       { classification: { path: "src/main.rs", encoding: UTF8, size: 100, mime: "text/x-rust" } },
//       { classification: { path: "docs/spec.pdf", encoding: Binary, size: 50000, mime: "application/pdf" } },
//       { classification: { path: "README.md", encoding: UTF8, size: 200, mime: "text/markdown" } }
//     ])
//     mock(fs.read, [
//       { content: "fn main() {}" },
//       { content: "# README" }
//     ])
//     // Note: fs.read is called only for text files (2 calls, not 3)
//
//     result = execute(snapshot_files, { paths: ["src/main.rs", "docs/spec.pdf", "README.md"] })
//     assert result.skipped == 1              // docs/spec.pdf was skipped
//     assert result.markdown is String
//     assert "spec.pdf" not_in result.markdown // binary file excluded from output
//   }
//
//   @test(tier: Scenario, cost: S, hermetic: true, scenario: "all_binary_files")
//   func test_snapshot_all_binary() {
//     mock(git.Core.LsFiles, { files: ["image.png", "data.wasm"] })
//     mock(fs.probe, [
//       { classification: { path: "image.png", encoding: Binary, size: 2048, mime: "image/png" } },
//       { classification: { path: "data.wasm", encoding: Binary, size: 8192, mime: "application/wasm" } }
//     ])
//     // fs.read never called (no text files)
//
//     result = execute(snapshot_files, { paths: ["image.png", "data.wasm"] })
//     assert result.skipped == 2
//     assert node_call_count(fs.read) == 0    // no text reads attempted
//   }
//
//
// --- Generated: Domain Compatibility Check (Bucket D extension) ---
//
// The compiler verifies that every Filesystem.read node is preceded by
// a classification step when the path source is unclassified:
//
//   @test(tier: Hygiene, cost: XS, hermetic: true)
//   func test_snapshot_encoding_hygiene() {
//     dag = compile(snapshot_files)
//
//     // Verify: classify_files appears before any fs.read node
//     assert dag.node_order(classify_files) < dag.node_order(fs.read)
//
//     // Verify: fs.read input paths are all TextFilePath (post-classification)
//     for read_node in dag.nodes_of_type(fs.read) {
//       assert read_node.input("path").type == TextFilePath
//     }
//
//     // Verify: the coproduct branch (text vs binary) is fully handled
//     assert dag.coproduct_coverage(ContentEncoding) == { Text, Binary }
//   }
//
//
// --- Generated: Real Repo Integration (Tier 5 extension) ---
//
// Uses the actual filesystem to verify content classification works
// with real file diversity. Cheap: local-only, no network calls.
//
//   @test(tier: Integration, cost: S, hermetic: false)
//   func test_snapshot_real_file_diversity() {
//     // Real git ls-files against the actual repo
//     files = git.Core.LsFiles()
//
//     // Classify all files
//     classified = classify_files(paths: files.files)
//
//     // Verify: known binary extensions are classified as Binary
//     for path in classified.binary {
//       assert path ends_with_one_of @file_types.binary
//     }
//
//     // Verify: text files are actually readable as String
//     for path in classified.text {
//       content = fs.read(path: path)
//       assert content.content is String    // valid UTF-8
//     }
//
//     // Verify: at least one binary file exists (repo-specific).
//     // This assertion is generated from repo scan at compile time.
//     // If the repo contains "docs/design/v4/ac.pdf", the compiler
//     // knows binary files exist and generates this assertion.
//     assert classified.binary |> length() > 0
//   }
//
// KEY INSIGHT: The content encoding type system turns an invisible
// runtime crash into three layers of defense:
//   1. Compile-time: type error if classification step is missing
//   2. Scenario tests: generated from coproduct branches (text vs binary)
//   3. Repo integration: generated from @file_types + actual file scan


// =========================================================================
// TEST MATRIX SUMMARY
// =========================================================================
//
// For a single func `upload_artifact` using GcsBucket:
//
// Tier      | Count | Cost | Hermetic | What it tests
// ----------|-------|------|----------|-------------------------------
// Unit      | 1     | XS   | Yes      | DAG completes with mocks
// Contract  | 3     | S    | Yes      | Per-node input/output
// Scenario  | 3     | S    | Yes      | Guard paths (exists/missing/fail)
// Hygiene   | 1     | XS   | Yes      | Resource lifecycle invariants
// Integr.   | 1     | M    | No       | Live GCP acquire + write + verify
// E2E       | 0     | -    | -        | (composed at pipeline level)
//
// For a func using Filesystem + unclassified paths (e.g., gist_snapshot):
//
// Tier      | Count | Cost | Hermetic | What it tests
// ----------|-------|------|----------|-------------------------------
// Unit      | 1     | XS   | Yes      | DAG completes with text-only mock
// Scenario  | 3     | S    | Yes      | all-text / mixed / all-binary file lists
// Hygiene   | 1     | XS   | Yes      | classify before read, coproduct coverage
// Repo      | 1     | S    | No       | Real file diversity from actual repo
//
// Total hermetic: 8 + 5 tests, all generated automatically from:
//   - func signature (probes + observers)
//   - resource @mock_response annotations (transport mocks)
//   - resource acquire guards (scenario paths)
//   - resource model invariants (hygiene)
//   - content encoding coproduct branches (encoding scenarios)
//   - @file_types extension rules (mock diversity)
//
// Total live: 1 + 1 tests, gated by cost + env vars.
// Contract tests: generated from interface @contract annotations.
//
// All of this is derived from the DAG structure. No hand-written tests.

# dsl/examples/rich_types.dag
```
// examples/rich_types.dag -- Richer type system proposals.
//
// STATUS: Forward-looking proposal. Not yet part of the spec.
//
// FOUNDATION: Every type denotes a set of values, subtyping is set
// inclusion, and coercion safety is decidable at compile time.
// See dsl-design.md §4.1 "Type-Theoretic Foundations" for the axioms.
//
// This file extends the base model (std/types.dag) with richer constructs.
// Each section annotates which axioms / set-theoretic levels apply.
//
// TYPE ALGEBRA LEVELS (from dsl-design.md):
//   L0: Primitives     -- ⟦Int⟧ = ℤ, ⟦String⟧ = Σ*, etc.
//   L1: Refinements    -- ⟦T @pred(P)⟧ = {x ∈ ⟦T⟧ | P(x)}  (subset comprehension)
//   L2: Brands         -- ⟦T @brand(N)⟧ ⊂ ⟦T⟧, disjoint across brands
//   L3: Records        -- ⟦{a:A, b:B}⟧ = ⟦A⟧ × ⟦B⟧  (labeled product)
//   L4: Sums           -- ⟦A | B⟧ = ⟦A⟧ ⊔ ⟦B⟧  (tagged disjoint union)
//   L5: Optionals      -- ⟦T?⟧ = ⟦T⟧ ∪ {none}
//   L6: Collections    -- ⟦List<T>⟧ = ⋃ₙ ⟦T⟧ⁿ
//   L7: Generics       -- type constructors F : Type → Type  (parametric)
//   L8: Bounds         -- ⟦Serializable⟧ = {T | T has to_json, from_json}
//   L9: Invariants     -- ⟦{..., @invariant: P}⟧ ⊂ ⟦{...}⟧  (dependent refinement)
//
// RECOMMENDATION: The DSL should own type definitions fully because:
//   - Types are the contract language between services, funcs, and infra
//   - The compiler needs types for testgen, mock generation, validation
//   - Cross-module type sharing requires a module system (DSL has this)
//   - Refinement types + generics enable powerful automatic test generation
//   - Types flow through deploy boundaries (serialization format selection)

module examples.rich_types

import infra.core { ObjectStorage }
import std.types { Timestamp }


// =========================================================================
// GENERIC TYPES  (Level 7: Parametric Polymorphism)
// =========================================================================
//
// A generic type is a type constructor F : Type → Type.
// Application instantiates: ⟦Result<Int, String>⟧ = ({Ok} × ⟦Int⟧) ⊔ ({Err} × ⟦String⟧)
//
// Generic subtyping is covariant:
//   If A <: B then Result<A, E> <: Result<B, E>
//   If A <: B then Page<A> <: Page<B>  (via List covariance)
//
// The DSL already uses List<T> and Map<K, V> as built-ins.
// The question: can users DEFINE new generic types?

// Result type -- the universal error-handling type.
type Result<T, E>
  = Ok { value: T }
  | Err { error: E }

// Convenience alias
type ApiResult<T> = Result<T, ApiError>

type ApiError {
  code: HttpStatus
  message: String
  details: Json?
}

// Page of results -- generic over the item type
type Page<T> {
  items: List<T>
  next_cursor: String?
  total_count: Int?
}

// Validated wrapper -- carries proof of validation
type Validated<T> {
  value: T
  validated_at: Timestamp
  validator: String
}

// Either -- one of two types
type Either<L, R>
  = Left { value: L }
  | Right { value: R }


// =========================================================================
// SUM TYPES WITH PAYLOADS  (Level 4: Disjoint Union / Coproduct)
// =========================================================================
//
// ⟦A | B⟧ = ⟦A⟧ ⊔ ⟦B⟧  -- tagged disjoint union
//
// With payloads:
//   ⟦DeployEvent⟧ = ({BuildStarted} × ⟦CommitSha⟧ × ⟦String⟧)
//                  ⊔ ({BuildSucceeded} × ⟦CommitSha⟧ × ⟦Int⟧ × ⟦List<String>⟧)
//                  ⊔ ({BuildFailed} × ⟦CommitSha⟧ × ⟦String⟧²)
//                  ⊔ ({Deployed} × ⟦CommitSha⟧ × ⟦String⟧ × ⟦Url⟧)
//                  ⊔ ({RolledBack} × ⟦CommitSha⟧ × ⟦String⟧ × ⟦CommitSha⟧)
//
// Tags ensure disjointness even when payload types overlap.
// Pattern matching must be exhaustive (covers the full ⊔).
//
// Current enums are simple (CloudRuntime = GitHubActions | Metadata | LocalDev).
// Real-world modeling needs payloads on variants.

type DeployEvent
  = BuildStarted { commit: CommitSha, branch: String }
  | BuildSucceeded { commit: CommitSha, duration_ms: Int, artifacts: List<String> }
  | BuildFailed { commit: CommitSha, error: String, stage: String }
  | Deployed { commit: CommitSha, target: String, url: Url }
  | RolledBack { commit: CommitSha, reason: String, rolled_to: CommitSha }

// Transport descriptor -- what the compiler resolves for each service call
type Transport
  = Http { method: String, url: Url, headers: Map<String, String> }
  | Shell { command: List<String>, env: Map<String, String>? }
  | Grpc { service_name: String, method: String, endpoint: Url }
  | InProcess { handler: String }


// =========================================================================
// TYPE BOUNDS / INTERFACES  (Level 8: Constrained Quantification)
// =========================================================================
//
// An interface defines a SET OF TYPES:
//   ⟦Serializable⟧ = {T ∈ Type | T has to_json : T → Json
//                                  and from_json : Json → Result<T, String>}
//
// If interface A extends B, then ⟦A⟧ ⊆ ⟦B⟧ (fewer types satisfy stricter bounds).
// Multiple bounds are intersection: <T: A + B> means T ∈ ⟦A⟧ ∩ ⟦B⟧.
//
// Auto-derivation: if all fields of a record implement Serializable,
// the record auto-derives Serializable (products of serializable = serializable).
//
// Type bounds let you write generic funcs that work with any type
// satisfying a contract.

interface Serializable {
  fn to_json(self) -> Json
  fn from_json(json: Json) -> Result<Self, String>
}

interface Comparable {
  fn compare(self, other: Self) -> Int
}

interface Hashable {
  fn hash(self) -> Int
}

interface Display {
  fn display(self) -> String
}

// Built-in types automatically implement appropriate interfaces:
//   String : Serializable, Comparable, Hashable, Display
//   Int    : Serializable, Comparable, Hashable, Display
//   Records with all Serializable fields auto-derive Serializable.


// =========================================================================
// BOUNDED GENERICS  (Level 7 + Level 8: Parametric + Constrained)
// =========================================================================
//
// Bounded quantification: fn f<T: Bound>(x: T) -> R
// This is: ∀T ∈ ⟦Bound⟧. T → R
//
// Parametricity: a generic fn cannot inspect T's structure.
// It must work uniformly for all T in the bound set.
// (In set-theoretic terms: f is a natural transformation.)

fn serialize<T: Serializable>(value: T) -> Json {
  value |> to_json()
}

fn sort_by_field<T, K: Comparable>(items: List<T>, key_fn: fn(T) -> K) -> List<T> {
  items |> sort_by(item => key_fn(item))
}

// Generic func: store any serializable value
func store_value<T: Serializable>(key: String, value: T) -> { ok: Bool }
  uses store: ObjectStorage
{
  bytes = serialize(value: value) |> to_bytes()
  result = store.write(key: key, content: bytes)
  return { ok: result.ok }
}

// Generic func: load and deserialize
func load_value<T: Serializable>(key: String) -> { value: Result<T, String> }
  uses store: ObjectStorage
{
  raw = store.read(key: key)
  result = match raw.found {
    true  => Err(error: "Deserialization example omitted in this corpus")
    false => Err(error: "Key not found: {key}")
  }
  return { value: result }
}


// =========================================================================
// BRANDED TYPES  (Level 2: Nominal Disjointness)
// =========================================================================
//
// ⟦T @brand("N")⟧ ⊂ ⟦T⟧              (subtype of base)
// ⟦T @brand("N")⟧ ∩ ⟦T @brand("M")⟧ = ∅  when N ≠ M  (disjoint)
//
// Same carrier set, different type identity (newtype pattern).
// Zero runtime cost -- brands are phantom compile-time tags.
//
// Brands compose with refinements:
//   ⟦Milliseconds⟧ = {n ∈ ℤ | n ≥ 0} ∩ {branded "Milliseconds"}
//   Milliseconds <: Int ✓,  Seconds <: Int ✓,  Milliseconds <: Seconds ✗

type UserId = String where brand("UserId")
type TeamId = String where brand("TeamId")
// Compiler prevents: let team: TeamId = some_user_id  // type error!
// Set-theoretically: ⟦UserId⟧ ∩ ⟦TeamId⟧ = ∅, but both ⊂ ⟦String⟧

type Milliseconds = Int where brand("Milliseconds"), range(min: 0)
type Seconds      = Int where brand("Seconds"), range(min: 0)
// Prevents: let timeout: Seconds = duration_ms  // type error!
// ⟦Milliseconds⟧ = {n ∈ ℤ | n ≥ 0, branded "Milliseconds"}
// ⟦Seconds⟧      = {n ∈ ℤ | n ≥ 0, branded "Seconds"}
// Disjoint despite identical carrier and predicates.


// =========================================================================
// CROSS-FIELD INVARIANTS  (Level 9: Dependent Refinement)
// =========================================================================
//
// ⟦DateRange⟧ = {(s, e) ∈ ⟦Date⟧ × ⟦Date⟧ | s ≤ e}
//             ⊂ ⟦{start: Date, end: Date}⟧    (strict subset of the product)
//
// The invariant is a predicate on the product -- subset comprehension
// over a Cartesian product. Decidable predicates only (no Turing-complete
// type-level computation). Preserves P9 (totality).

type DateRange {
  start: String where pattern("^\\d{4}-\\d{2}-\\d{2}$")
  end: String where pattern("^\\d{4}-\\d{2}-\\d{2}$")
}


// =========================================================================
// COMPOSITE EXAMPLE  (all levels combined)
// =========================================================================
//
// ReviewArtifact<M> combines:
//   L7: Generic type constructor (parameterized over M)
//   L8: Bounded generic (M: Serializable)
//   L3: Record (labeled product of fields)
//   L1: Refinement (id: uuid format, created_at: ISO pattern)
//   L2: Brand (author: UserId -- nominal, not just String)
//   L4: Sum type (status: ReviewStatus with payloads)
//   L9: (potential) Cross-field invariant could enforce created_at < completed_at
//
// The compiler decomposes this into nested set operations:
//   ⟦ReviewArtifact<M>⟧ = ⟦uuid⟧ × ⟦ISO⟧ × ⟦UserId⟧ × ⟦M⟧ × ⟦NonEmptyStr⟧ × ⟦ReviewStatus⟧
//   where M ∈ ⟦Serializable⟧
//
// Subtyping works at every level:
//   ReviewArtifact<SpecificMeta> <: ReviewArtifact<Json>
//     (if SpecificMeta <: Json and M is covariant)

type ReviewArtifact<M: Serializable> {
  id: String where format(uuid)
  created_at: Timestamp
  author: UserId
  metadata: M
  content: NonEmptyStr
  status: ReviewStatus
}

type ReviewStatus
  = Pending
  | InProgress { reviewer: UserId, started_at: Timestamp }
  | Completed { reviewer: UserId, score: Int where range(min: 1, max: 5) }
  | Rejected { reason: String }

func submit_review<M: Serializable>(
  artifact: ReviewArtifact<M>,
  reviewer: UserId
) -> { result: ReviewArtifact<M> }
  uses store: ObjectStorage
{
  updated = artifact with {
    status: InProgress(reviewer: reviewer, started_at: now())
  }
  stored = store_value(key: "reviews/{artifact.id}", value: updated)
  return { result: updated }
}


// =========================================================================
// PHASING RECOMMENDATION
// =========================================================================
//
// Phase 1 (DONE): L0-L1, L3-L6 -- Primitives, refinements, records, simple
//   enums, optionals, collections. The foundational set-theoretic model
//   (Axioms 1-4, three-level coercion) is fully operational.
//
// Phase 2: L2, L4 extended -- Branded types (nominal disjointness),
//   sum types with payloads. Extends the lattice with brand partitions
//   and tagged disjoint unions. No new axioms needed.
//
// Phase 3: L7, L8 -- Generics (type constructors), type bounds (constrained
//   quantification). Adds parametric polymorphism. Covariance rules follow
//   from Axiom 2 (subset inclusion) applied to type constructors.
//
// Phase 4: L9 -- Cross-field invariants (dependent refinement on products).
//   Most expressive extension. Requires decidable predicate evaluation
//   at compile time.
//
// KEY INVARIANT: The IR represents the FULL type model (all levels, full
// cardinality algebra, full predicate lattice) from day one. The surface
// syntax grows incrementally, but the underlying set-theoretic model is
// complete. Every surface construct desugars to the same Dag<TypeOp>
// representation, preserving the algebraic laws at every phase.
//
// See dsl-design.md §4.1 "Type-Theoretic Foundations" for the complete
// axiom system and coercion theorem.
```

// extdeps/cargo.dag -- "What is Cargo?"
//
// Rust's build system and package manager: packages, targets, profiles,
// features, and command behaviors.
//
// Consumers:
//   services/cargo.dag        — shell transport wiring
//   config/build_commands.dag — build command composition
//   tools/build.dag           — build workflow

module extdeps.cargo

import std.behavioral {
  OperationBehavior, SideEffects, Determinism, Confidence, PrerequisiteKind, Severity
}

// ── Package model ─────────────────────────────────────────────────

type CargoPackage {
  name: String
  version: String
  edition: String
  path: String
}

// ── Targets ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────

type CargoTarget
  = Lib
  | Bin { name: String }
  | CargoTest { name: String }
  | Example { name: String }
  | Bench { name: String }

// ── Profiles ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
// Cargo allows arbitrary user-defined profiles in Cargo.toml
// (e.g., [profile.ci-optimized]). Use String to avoid a closed-world
// enum that cannot represent valid workspaces.

type CargoProfile = String

data canonical_profiles: List<String> = ["dev", "release", "test", "bench"]

// ── Features ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────

type CargoFeature {
  name: String
  dependencies: List<String>
}

// ── Test harness ──────────────────────────────────────────────────

type TestHarness = Harness | NoHarness

// ── Commands ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────

type CargoCommand = CargoBuild | CargoTest | CargoClippy | CargoDoc | CargoRun | CargoCheck | CargoBench | CargoPublish

// ── Constants ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────

data default_edition: String = "2021"

data default_profile: CargoProfile = "dev"

// ── Operation behaviors ───────────────────────────────────────────

type CargoOperationBehavior {
  operation: String
  behavior: OperationBehavior
}

data operation_behaviors: List<CargoOperationBehavior> = [
  {
    operation: "build",
    behavior: {
      side_effects: WritesState,
      idempotent: true,
      idempotency_keys: ["target", "profile", "features"],
      determinism: Deterministic,
      failure_modes: [{ name: "CompileError", condition: "source_error", http_status: null, recoverable: false, retry_safe: true }],
      edge_cases: [{ description: "incremental compilation may cache stale artifacts", trigger: "source_rename", severity: Medium }],
      confidence: Documented,
      prerequisites: [{ description: "rust toolchain installed", kind: Tooling }],
      assumptions: ["Cargo.lock is present and up-to-date"],
      unknowns: []
    }
  },
  {
    operation: "test",
    behavior: {
      side_effects: WritesState,
      idempotent: true,
      idempotency_keys: ["target", "profile"],
      determinism: Deterministic,
      failure_modes: [
        { name: "TestFailure", condition: "assertion_failed", http_status: null, recoverable: false, retry_safe: true },
        { name: "CompileError", condition: "source_error", http_status: null, recoverable: false, retry_safe: true }
      ],
      edge_cases: [],
      confidence: Documented,
      prerequisites: [{ description: "rust toolchain installed", kind: Tooling }],
      assumptions: [],
      unknowns: []
    }
  },
  {
    operation: "clippy",
    behavior: {
      side_effects: ReadOnly,
      idempotent: true,
      idempotency_keys: null,
      determinism: Deterministic,
      failure_modes: [{ name: "LintDenied", condition: "deny_lint_triggered", http_status: null, recoverable: false, retry_safe: true }],
      edge_cases: [],
      confidence: Documented,
      prerequisites: [{ description: "clippy component installed", kind: Tooling }],
      assumptions: [],
      unknowns: []
    }
  },
  {
    operation: "publish",
    behavior: {
      side_effects: WritesExternal,
      idempotent: false,
      idempotency_keys: null,
      determinism: Deterministic,
      failure_modes: [
        { name: "VersionExists", condition: "version_already_published", http_status: null, recoverable: false, retry_safe: false },
        { name: "AuthError", condition: "invalid_token", http_status: null, recoverable: false, retry_safe: false }
      ],
      edge_cases: [{ description: "published crates cannot be unpublished, only yanked", trigger: "publish_complete", severity: High }],
      confidence: Documented,
      prerequisites: [{ description: "crates.io API token", kind: Credential }],
      assumptions: [],
      unknowns: []
    }
  }
]

```
// extdeps/clippy.dag -- "What is clippy?"
//
// Stable domain model of clippy as a lint tool. Facts about clippy's
// spec, categories, and configuration surface. No policy decisions.
//
// Consumers:
//   tools/clippy.dag     — invocation (ensure/install/lint)
//   config/clippy_policy.dag — enforcement config (disallowed methods)
//   config/arch_rules.dag    — invariant definitions reference lint actions

module extdeps.clippy

// ── Identity ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

type ClippySpec {
  id: String
  config_file: String
  integration: String
}

data spec: ClippySpec = {
  id: "clippy",
  config_file: "clippy.toml",
  integration: "cargo clippy"
}

// ── Lint categories ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
// Facts from clippy documentation. These are properties of clippy
// itself, not our choices about which to enable.

type LintLevel = Deny | Warn | Allow

type ClippyCategory {
  name: String
  default_level: LintLevel
  description: String
}

data categories: List<ClippyCategory> = [
  { name: "correctness",  default_level: Deny,  description: "Code that is outright wrong or useless" },
  { name: "suspicious",   default_level: Warn,  description: "Code that is most likely wrong or useless" },
  { name: "style",        default_level: Warn,  description: "Code that should be written in a more idiomatic way" },
  { name: "complexity",   default_level: Warn,  description: "Code that does something simple but in a complex way" },
  { name: "perf",         default_level: Warn,  description: "Code that can be written to run faster" },
  { name: "pedantic",     default_level: Allow, description: "Lints which are rather strict or have occasional false positives" },
  { name: "restriction",  default_level: Allow, description: "Lints which prevent the use of language and library features" },
  { name: "nursery",      default_level: Allow, description: "New lints that are still under development" },
  { name: "cargo",        default_level: Allow, description: "Lints for the cargo manifest" }
]

// ── Configuration surface ───────────────────────────────────────────
// What clippy.toml can configure.

type DisallowedMethodEntry {
  path: String
  reason: String
}

type DisallowedTypeEntry {
  path: String
  reason: String
}

// clippy.toml structure.

// extdeps/cloud/aws/iam.dag -- "What is AWS IAM?"
//
// AWS IAM resource model: roles, policies, trust relationships,
// managed policies.
//
// Consumers:
//   infra/aws/resources.dag    — IAM resource impl
//   cloud/aws/credential.dag   — AssumeRole chain

module extdeps.cloud.aws.iam

import extdeps.cloud.aws.core { Arn }
import std.behavioral {
  OperationBehavior, SideEffects, Determinism, Confidence, PrerequisiteKind, Severity
}

// ── Roles ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

type AwsRole {
  arn: String
  name: String
  path: String
  assume_role_policy: TrustPolicy
  max_session_duration: Int
}

// ── Trust policies ────────────────────────────────────────────────

type TrustPolicy {
  version: String
  statements: List<TrustStatement>
}

type TrustPrincipal
  = AwsAccount { account_id: String }
  | AwsService { service: String }
  | Federated { provider: String }

type TrustStatement {
  effect: String
  principal: TrustPrincipal
  action: String
  condition: Map<String, String>?
}

// ── Policies ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────

type AwsPolicyDocument {
  version: String
  statements: List<AwsPolicyStatement>
}

type AwsPolicyEffect = AwsAllow | AwsDeny

// Comprehensive IAM policy statement matching the AWS JSON policy schema.
// S3 bucket policies, SQS policies, etc. are all standard IAM policy documents
// with the addition of Principal. The Not* fields model negative bounds
// ("allow all except X"), critical for secure SDLC boundaries.
type AwsPolicyStatement {
  effect: AwsPolicyEffect
  principal: String?
  not_principal: String?
  action: List<String>
  not_action: List<String>?
  resource: List<String>
  not_resource: List<String>?
  condition: Map<String, String>?
}

type ManagedPolicy {
  arn: String
  name: String
  description: String?
}

// ── Operation behaviors ───────────────────────────────────────────

type AwsIamOperationBehavior {
  operation: String
  behavior: OperationBehavior
}

data operation_behaviors: List<AwsIamOperationBehavior> = [
  {
    operation: "GetRole",

// extdeps/cloud/aws/lambda.dag -- "What is AWS Lambda?"

}

// ── Runtimes ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────

// A strict enum forces a compiler update for each new runtime. Use String

]

type LambdaFunction {
  arn: String
  name: String
  runtime: LambdaRuntime
  handler: String
  memory_mb: Int
  timeout_seconds: Int
  role_arn: String
}

// ── Layers ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

type LambdaLayer {
  arn: String
  version: Int
  compatible_runtimes: List<LambdaRuntime>
}

// ── Invocation ────────────────────────────────────────────────────

type InvocationType = RequestResponse | LambdaEvent | LambdaDryRun

// ── Constants ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────

data max_memory_mb: Int = 10240

data max_timeout_seconds: Int = 900

data max_layers: Int = 5

// ── Operation behaviors ───────────────────────────────────────────

  operation: String
  behavior: OperationBehavior
}

// ── Container Apps ────────────────────────────────────────────────

}

  header: String
  format: String

  resource: String
  limit: Int

}

}

// extdeps/coordination/core.dag -- "What is a coordination store?"

module extdeps.coordination.core

import std.coordination {
  CasMechanism, DeadLetterPolicy, NotificationMechanism, DeliveryGuarantee
}

type CoordinationBackend = ObjectStore | RelationalDb | EmbeddedDb

type CasPattern {
  mechanism: CasMechanism
  conflict_resolution: String
}

type QueuePattern {
  claiming: String
  visibility: Int?
  dead_letter: DeadLetterPolicy?
}

type LeasePattern {
  acquisition: String
  heartbeat: String
  expiry: String
}

type NotificationPattern {
  mechanism: NotificationMechanism
  latency: String
  ordering: String
}

type PatternCompositionRule {
  name: String
  backend: CoordinationBackend
  requires: List<String>
  outcome: String
  guarantee: DeliveryGuarantee
}

data pattern_composition_rules: List<PatternCompositionRule> = [
  {
    name: "cas_plus_lease_distributed_lock",
    backend: RelationalDb,
    requires: ["cas", "lease"],
    outcome: "Distributed lock with fencing",
    guarantee: AtLeastOnce
  },
  {
    name: "queue_plus_cas_exactly_once_effective",
    backend: ObjectStore,
    requires: ["queue_claim", "cas_commit"],
    outcome: "Exactly-once effective processing at workflow level",
    guarantee: ExactlyOnce
  },
  {
    name: "queue_only_at_least_once",
    backend: EmbeddedDb,
    requires: ["queue_claim"],
    outcome: "At-least-once delivery without deduplication ledger",
    guarantee: AtLeastOnce
  }
]

// extdeps/coordination/gcs.dag -- "GCS as a coordination store."

module extdeps.coordination.gcs

import std.behavioral {
  OperationBehavior, SideEffects, Determinism, Confidence, PrerequisiteKind, Severity
}
import std.coordination { CasMechanism, NotificationMechanism }
import std.rate_limit { PropagationDelay }

type GcsGeneration = Int
type GcsMetageneration = Int

type GcsPrecondition
  = IfGenerationMatch { generation: GcsGeneration }
  | IfMetagenerationMatch { metageneration: GcsMetageneration }
  | IfGenerationNotMatch { generation: GcsGeneration }

type GcsCoordinationOperationBehavior {
  operation: String
  behavior: OperationBehavior
}

type GcsCasPattern {
  mechanism: CasMechanism
  create_only_generation: Int
  conflict_status: Int
}

type NotificationLatency {
  mechanism: NotificationMechanism
  delay: PropagationDelay
}

data operation_behaviors: List<GcsCoordinationOperationBehavior> = [
  {
    operation: "GetObject",
    behavior: {
      side_effects: ReadOnly,
      idempotent: true,
      idempotency_keys: null,
      determinism: Deterministic,
      failure_modes: [{ name: "NotFound", condition: "object_absent", http_status: 404, recoverable: false, retry_safe: false }],
      edge_cases: [{ description: "generation and metageneration are separate monotonic counters", trigger: null, severity: Medium }],
      confidence: Documented,
      prerequisites: [{ description: "storage.objects.get permission", kind: Capability }],
      assumptions: ["Read path can request media payload via alt=media"],
      unknowns: ["Regional latency variance for cold objects"]
    }
  },
  {
    operation: "InsertObject",
    behavior: {
      side_effects: WritesState,
      idempotent: true,
      idempotency_keys: ["bucket", "object", "ifGenerationMatch"],
      determinism: Deterministic,
      failure_modes: [{ name: "PreconditionFailed", condition: "generation_mismatch", http_status: 412, recoverable: true, retry_safe: false }],
      edge_cases: [{ description: "ifGenerationMatch=0 enforces create-only semantics", trigger: "create_only_write", severity: High }],
      confidence: Documented,
      prerequisites: [{ description: "storage.objects.create permission", kind: Capability }],
      assumptions: ["Returned generation is authoritative for future CAS writes"],
      unknowns: ["Exact contention profile under high-frequency concurrent writers"]
    }
  },
  {
    operation: "PatchMetadata",
    behavior: {
      side_effects: WritesState,
      idempotent: true,
      idempotency_keys: ["bucket", "object", "ifMetagenerationMatch"],
      determinism: Deterministic,
      failure_modes: [{ name: "PreconditionFailed", condition: "metageneration_mismatch", http_status: 412, recoverable: true, retry_safe: false }],
      edge_cases: [],
      confidence: HighConfidence,
      prerequisites: [{ description: "storage.objects.update permission", kind: Capability }],
      assumptions: ["Metadata writes are serialized by metageneration checks"],
      unknowns: []
    }
  },
  {
    operation: "DeleteObject",
    behavior: {
      side_effects: WritesState,
      idempotent: true,
      idempotency_keys: ["bucket", "object", "ifGenerationMatch"],
      determinism: Deterministic,
      failure_modes: [{ name: "PreconditionFailed", condition: "generation_mismatch", http_status: 412, recoverable: true, retry_safe: false }],
      edge_cases: [],
      confidence: Documented,
      prerequisites: [{ description: "storage.objects.delete permission", kind: Capability }],

// extdeps/git.dag -- "What is Git?"
//
// Core Git object model: commits, branches, refs, diffs, merge strategies.
// Facts about Git's data model, not how we invoke it (that's services/git.dag).
//
// Consumers:
//   services/git.dag               — shell transport wiring
//   extdeps/github/pull_requests.dag — PR branch refs
//   tools/build.dag                — branch detection

module extdeps.git

import std.behavioral {
  OperationBehavior, SideEffects, Determinism, Confidence, PrerequisiteKind, Severity
}
import std.types { CommitSha, Timestamp }

// ── Object model ──────────────────────────────────────────────────

type ObjectType = BlobObj | TreeObj | CommitObj | TagObj

type GitAuthor {
  name: String
  email: String
  timestamp: Timestamp
}

// Git separates author (who wrote the patch) from committer (who applied
// it to the tree — e.g., merge queue, bot, maintainer). Both are needed
// for SLSA provenance and accurate attribution in automated workflows.
type GitCommit {
  sha: CommitSha
  message: String
  author: GitAuthor
  committer: GitAuthor
  parent_shas: List<CommitSha>
}

// ── Refs ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

type GitRef
  = BranchRef { name: String }
  | TagRef { name: String }
  | CommitRef { sha: CommitSha }

type GitBranch {
  name: String
  upstream: String?
  is_head: Bool
}

type GitRemote {
  name: String
  url: String
  fetch_refspec: String
}

// ── Merge strategies ──────────────────────────────────────────────

type GitMergeStrategy = GitMerge | GitSquash | GitRebase | GitFastForward

// ── Diff model ────────────────────────────────────────────────────

type DiffStat {
  files_changed: Int
  insertions: Int
  deletions: Int
}

type DiffLine
  = DiffAdded { content: String }
  | DiffRemoved { content: String }
  | DiffContext { content: String }

type DiffHunk {
  file_path: String
  old_start: Int
  new_start: Int
  lines: List<DiffLine>
}

// ── Working tree status ───────────────────────────────────────────

type GitFileStatus = GitClean | GitModified | GitAdded | GitDeleted | GitRenamed | GitUntracked

// ── Constants ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────

data default_remote: String = "origin"

data default_branch_names: List<String> = ["main", "master"]

// ── Operation behaviors ───────────────────────────────────────────

type GitOperationBehavior {
  operation: String
  behavior: OperationBehavior
}

data operation_behaviors: List<GitOperationBehavior> = [
  {
    operation: "clone",

      edge_cases: [],
      confidence: Documented,
