// extdeps/github/issues.dag -- "What is a GitHub Issue?"
//
// The issue resource model: states, labels, events, comments, timeline.
// This is the raw GitHub model. The SDLC lifecycle stage model
// (IssueLifecycleStage) lives in std/types.dag and maps onto this.
//
// Consumers:
//   services/github/issues.dag             — transport wiring
//   funcs/sdlc_stages.dag                  — stage handler logic
//   extdeps/github/pull_requests.dag       — cross-reference

module extdeps.github.issues

import extdeps.github.core { GitHubUser }
import std.behavioral {
  OperationBehavior, SideEffects, Determinism, Confidence, PrerequisiteKind, Severity
}
import std.types { Timestamp }

// ── Issue model ───────────────────────────────────────────────────

type GitHubIssueState = Open | Closed

type Label {
  id: Int
  name: String
  color: String
  description: String?
}

type GitHubIssue {
  id: Int
  number: Int
  title: String
  body: String?
  state: GitHubIssueState
  state_reason: String?
  labels: List<Label>
  user: String
  created_at: Timestamp
  updated_at: Timestamp
  closed_at: Timestamp?
  url: String
}

// ── Comments ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────

type IssueComment {
  id: Int
  body: String
  user: String
  created_at: Timestamp
  updated_at: Timestamp
}

// ── Events & timeline ─────────────────────────────────────────────

type IssueEventType
  = Labeled
  | Unlabeled
  | IssueClosed
  | Reopened
  | Assigned
  | Unassigned
  | Milestoned
  | Commented

type IssueEvent {
  id: Int
  event: IssueEventType
  actor: String
  created_at: Timestamp
}

// ── Filters ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────

type IssueFilter
  = ByState { state: GitHubIssueState }
  | ByLabel { label: String }
  | ByAssignee { login: String }

// ── State machine ─────────────────────────────────────────────────

// state_reason values: "completed", "not_planned", "reopened".
// Distinguishes successful completion from intentional abandonment.
type IssueStateTransition {
  from: GitHubIssueState
  to: GitHubIssueState
  action: String
  state_reason: String?
}

data state_transitions: List<IssueStateTransition> = [
  { from: Open, to: Closed, action: "close", state_reason: "completed" },
  { from: Open, to: Closed, action: "close_not_planned", state_reason: "not_planned" },
  { from: Closed, to: Open, action: "reopen", state_reason: "reopened" }
]

// ── Operation behaviors ───────────────────────────────────────────

type IssueOperationBehavior {
  operation: String
  behavior: OperationBehavior
}

data operation_behaviors: List<IssueOperationBehavior> = [
  {
    operation: "create",
    behavior: {
      side_effects: WritesState,
      idempotent: false,
      idempotency_keys: null,
      determinism: Deterministic,
      failure_modes: [
        { name: "ValidationError", condition: "invalid_input", http_status: 422, recoverable: false, retry_safe: false },
        { name: "AuthError", condition: "insufficient_scopes", http_status: 401, recoverable: false, retry_safe: false }
      ],

// extdeps/github/pull_requests.dag -- "What is a GitHub Pull Request?"
//
// PR resource model: states, reviews, checks, merge strategies,
// branch protection, file changes. State machine: draft → open →
// review → merged/closed.
//
// Consumers:
//   services/github/pull_request.dag — transport wiring
//   funcs/sdlc_stages.dag           — code review stage

module extdeps.github.pull_requests

import extdeps.github.core { Repository }
import std.behavioral {
  OperationBehavior, SideEffects, Determinism, Confidence, PrerequisiteKind, Severity
}
import std.types { CommitSha, Timestamp }

// ── PR model ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────

// Wire format: state is strictly "open" or "closed".
// A merged PR is state=closed with merged=true (see PullRequest.merged).
type PrState = PrOpen | PrClosed

type PrBranchRef {
  ref: String
  sha: CommitSha
  repo: String
}

type PullRequest {
  id: Int
  number: Int
  title: String
  body: String?
  state: PrState
  head: PrBranchRef
  base: PrBranchRef
  user: String
  draft: Bool
  mergeable: Bool?
  merged: Bool
  created_at: Timestamp
}

// ── Reviews ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────

type ReviewState = Approved | ChangesRequested | ReviewCommented | Dismissed | Pending

type Review {
  id: Int
  user: String
  state: ReviewState
  body: String?
  submitted_at: Timestamp
}

// ── Checks ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

type CheckStatus = CheckQueued | CheckInProgress | CheckCompleted

type CheckConclusion
  = CheckSuccess
  | CheckFailure
  | Neutral
  | Cancelled
  | Skipped
  | TimedOut
  | ActionRequired

// ── Merge ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

type PrMergeStrategy = PrMerge | PrSquash | PrRebase

// ── Branch protection ─────────────────────────────────────────────

type BranchProtection {
  required_reviews: Int
  dismiss_stale: Bool
  require_status_checks: Bool
  enforce_admins: Bool
}

// ── File changes ──────────────────────────────────────────────────

type PrFileStatus = FileAdded | FileRemoved | FileModified | FileRenamed

type PrFile {
  filename: String
  status: PrFileStatus
  additions: Int
  deletions: Int
}

// ── State machine ─────────────────────────────────────────────────

type PrStateTransition {
  from: PrState
  to: PrState
  action: String
  terminal: Bool
}

data pr_state_machine: List<PrStateTransition> = [
  { from: PrOpen, to: PrClosed, action: "close", terminal: false },
  { from: PrOpen, to: PrClosed, action: "merge", terminal: true },
  { from: PrClosed, to: PrOpen, action: "reopen", terminal: false }
]

// ── Operation behaviors ───────────────────────────────────────────

type PrOperationBehavior {
  operation: String
  behavior: OperationBehavior
}

data operation_behaviors: List<PrOperationBehavior> = [
  {
    operation: "create",
    behavior: {
      side_effects: WritesState,
      idempotent: false,
      idempotency_keys: null,
      determinism: Deterministic,
      failure_modes: [
        { name: "ValidationError", condition: "invalid_head_or_base", http_status: 422, recoverable: false, retry_safe: false }
      ],
      edge_cases: [{ description: "creating a PR from a fork requires cross-repo permissions", trigger: "fork_pr", severity: Medium }],
      confidence: Documented,
      prerequisites: [{ description: "repo write access", kind: Capability }],

      unknowns: []
    }
  },
  {
    operation: "get",
    behavior: {
      side_effects: ReadOnly,

      idempotency_keys: null,
      determinism: Deterministic,
      failure_modes: [{ name: "NotFound", condition: "pr_absent", http_status: 404, recoverable: false, retry_safe: false }],
      edge_cases: [],
      confidence: Documented,
      prerequisites: [{ description: "repo read access", kind: Capability }],
      assumptions: [],
      unknowns: []
    }
  },
  {
    operation: "merge",

      side_effects: WritesExternal,

// extdeps/github_actions.dag -- "What is GitHub Actions?"
//
// Stable domain model of GitHub Actions as a CI/CD platform.
// Tautological definitions: a workflow has triggers, permissions,
// env, and jobs. A job has a runner, steps. A step uses an action
// or runs a command.
//
// Facts about the platform's schema — no opinions about our repo.
// Our CI configuration lives in config/ci.dag (Layer 2).
//
// Consumers:
//   config/ci.dag          — our CI configuration data
//   tools/cigen.dag        — rendering + tool entrypoint

module extdeps.github_actions

// ── Trigger ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
// "How does a workflow start?"

type Trigger {
  push_branches: List<String>
  pr_branches: List<String>
}

// ── Permission ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
// "What can the workflow do?"

type Permission {
  scope: String
  level: String
}

// ── Environment ────────────────────────────────────────────────────

type EnvVar {
  key: String
  value: String
}

// ── Secrets ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
// GitHub Actions references secrets via ${{ secrets.NAME }}.

type SecretRef {
  name: String
}

// ── Cache ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
// "How does caching work?"

type Cache {
  key: String
  paths: List<String>
  restore_keys: List<String>
}

// ── Checkout ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────

type Checkout {
  fetch_depth: Int?
  submodules: String?
}

// ── Runner ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
// "Where does the job run?"

type RunnerImage {
  id: String
}

data ubuntu_latest: RunnerImage = { id: "ubuntu-latest" }
data ubuntu_22_04: RunnerImage = { id: "ubuntu-22.04" }
data macos_latest: RunnerImage = { id: "macos-latest" }
data windows_latest: RunnerImage = { id: "windows-latest" }

// ── Actions ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
// Well-known reusable actions with pinned versions.

data checkout_action: String = "actions/checkout@v4"
data rust_toolchain_action: String = "dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable"
data cache_action: String = "actions/cache@v4"

// ── Step ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
// "What is a workflow step?"
// A step either uses a reusable action or runs a shell command.

type Step
  = Run { name: String, command: String, env: List<EnvVar> }
  | Uses { name: String, action: String, with_params: Map<String, String> }

// ── Job ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
// "What is a workflow job?"

type Job {
  id: String
  name: String
  runner: RunnerImage
  timeout_minutes: Int
  steps: List<Step>
  needs: List<String>
}

// ── Workflow ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
// "What is a GitHub Actions workflow?"

type Workflow {
  name: String
  trigger: Trigger
  permissions: List<Permission>
  env: List<EnvVar>
  cache: Cache?
  jobs: List<Job>
}

// ── Output ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
// "Where does the workflow file go?"

data output_dir: String = ".github/workflows"
```

# dsl/extdeps/gitignore.dag
```
// extdeps/gitignore.dag -- "What is .gitignore?"
//
// Stable domain model of .gitignore files. Tautological definitions:
// categories group exclusion patterns with provenance and rationale.
//
// Consumers: config/gitignore.dag (data), tools/bootstrap.dag (rendering).

module extdeps.gitignore

// A category of gitignore rules with provenance tracking.
type GitignoreCategory {
  id: String
  name: String
  source: String?
  items: List<String>
  rationale: String?
  when_build_system: String?
}

// A complete .gitignore file with provenance rule comment.
type GitignoreFile {
  rule_comment: String
  categories: List<GitignoreCategory>
}

// ── Domain rendering ─────────────────────────────────────────────────

fn render_category_header(cat: GitignoreCategory) -> String {
  match cat.source {
    None => "# --- {cat.name} ---"
    _ => "# --- {cat.name} (from {cat.source}) ---"
  }
}

fn render_category(cat: GitignoreCategory) -> String {
  let header = render_category_header(cat: cat)
  let rationale_line = match cat.rationale {
    None => ""
    _ => "# {cat.rationale}\n"
  }
  let items = cat.items |> join("\n")
  "{header}\n{rationale_line}{items}\n"
}

fn render_gitignore_content(file: GitignoreFile) -> String {
  let rule = "# {file.rule_comment}\n\n"
  let body = file.categories |> map(c => render_category(cat: c)) |> join("\n")
  "{rule}{body}"
}

// ── Category filtering ───────────────────────────────────────────────

fn filter_categories(categories: List<GitignoreCategory>, build_system: String) -> List<GitignoreCategory> {
  categories |> filter(c => match c.when_build_system {
    None => true
    _ => c.when_build_system == build_system
  }) |> filter(c => c.items |> count() > 0)
}
```

// extdeps/gunbc.dag -- "What is gunbc?"
//
// Meta model of this repo's workspace structure. Technically an
// internal system, but modeled as an extdep because:
//   1. The crate graph is a stable fact (changes rarely)
//   2. Multiple tools derive from it (clippy policy, makegen, testgen)
//   3. Treating it uniformly with external deps simplifies composition
//

//   config/clippy_policy.dag — crate policies reference roles
//   tools/makegen.dag        — registry references workspace binaries

  = TransportBoundary
  | Compiler
  | CodegenBootstrap
  | Runtime
  | Infra
  | Library
  | Tool

# dsl/extdeps/make.dag
```
// extdeps/make.dag -- "What is Make?"
//
// Stable domain model of GNU Make. Tautological definitions:
// targets have names, dependencies, and recipe commands.
//
// Consumers: tools/makegen.dag (rendering), config/build_policy.dag (rules).
// See also: std/languages.dag makefile_format (comment syntax, extensions).

module extdeps.make

// Canonical target name in the global Make namespace.
type TargetName = String

// Where a target originates in gunbc make projections.
type TargetOrigin =
  Help
  | Core
  | Meta
  | MetaFix
  | MetaCheck
  | Tool
  | ToolDry
  | ToolExtra

// A Make target: the fundamental unit.
type MakeTarget {
  name: TargetName
  description: String
  deps: List<TargetName>
  commands: List<String>
  comment: String?
  phony: Bool
}

// Canonical target used by makegen renderers after namespace validation.
type CanonicalTarget {
  name: TargetName
  deps: List<TargetName>
  commands: List<String>
  comment: String?
  phony: Bool
  origin: TargetOrigin
  owner: String
}

// Canonical global namespace for Make targets.
// Map keys are unique by construction, so duplicate target names are
// structurally unrepresentable in this model.
type TargetNamespace = Map<TargetName, CanonicalTarget>

// A Make variable assignment.
type MakeVariable {
  name: String
  value: String
}

// A section in a Makefile (group of related targets).
type MakeSection {
  title: String
  targets: List<MakeTarget>
}

// Entrypoint parameter — how a CLI tool exposes itself through Make.
// Maps a DAG port to a Make variable + CLI flag.
type EntrypointParam {
  port_name: String
  make_var: String
  cli_flag: String
  type_hint: String
  default: String?
  repeatable: Bool
}

// A tool that gets a Make target.
type ToolTarget {
  name: String
  description: String
  make_target: String?
  entrypoints: List<EntrypointParam>
}

// A core build workflow (e.g., "codegen", "build", "testgen").
// These are the orchestration targets, not tools or meta targets.
type CoreWorkflow {
  name: String
  description: String
  deps: List<String>
  body: List<String>        // recipe lines (e.g., ["@cargo test --workspace"])
  comment: String?          // override comment (e.g., "Full build transaction: ...")
}

// What resource a meta target needs and how.
type ResourceNeed {
  resource: String           // resource identifier (e.g., "compiled_code")
  mode: String               // "ensure" or "verify"
}

// A meta target definition (e.g., "test", "check", "fmt").
// Meta targets compose resource needs with a build operation.
type MetaTargetDef {
  name: String
  description: String
  has_check: Bool
  has_fix: Bool
  command: String                     // pre-rendered shell command
  check_command: String?              // for -check variant
  fix_command: String?                // for -fix variant
  command_prefix: String?             // e.g., "GUNBC_TEST_MAX_COST=XL"
  resource_needs: List<ResourceNeed>  // [{resource: "compiled_code", mode: "ensure"}, ...]
  fix_prerequisites: List<String>     // ["fmt-fix", "lint-fix"]
}

// Maps a resource identifier to its Make targets for ensure/verify modes.
type ResourceTargetEntry {
  resource: String           // e.g., "generated_cli"
  ensure_target: String      // e.g., "ensure-codegen"
  verify_target: String      // e.g., "ensure-codegen"
}

// A tool discovered at build time via inventory/DSL introspection.
type DiscoveredTool {
  short_name: String
  description: String
  binary_name: String
  command: String             // pre-rendered invocation command
  dry_run_command: String     // with --dry-run strict
  deps: List<String>          // make target dependencies
  entrypoints: List<EntrypointParam>
  extra_targets: List<ExtraTarget>
  live_secrets: List<String>
}

// An extra composite target for a tool (e.g., "viz-serve").
type ExtraTarget {
  suffix: String
  description: String
  post_commands: List<String>
}

// Complete Makefile structure.
type Makefile {
  variables: List<MakeVariable>
  sections: List<MakeSection>
}

// Canonical Makefile projection with uniqueness encoded in the type model.
type CanonicalMakefile {
  variables: List<MakeVariable>
  targets: TargetNamespace
}
```

// extdeps/secrets/core.dag -- Abstract "what is a secret provider?" model.

module extdeps.secrets.core

  created_at: Timestamp?
}

type RotationPolicy {
  period_seconds: Int
  next_rotation: String?
}

type SecretAccessPolicy {
  principal: String
  permission: String
  condition: String?
}

type SecretEncryption = ProviderManaged | CustomerManaged { key_id: String }

type SecretOperationBehavior {
  operation: String
  behavior: OperationBehavior
}

data shared_secret_operation_behaviors: List<SecretOperationBehavior> = [

      ],
      edge_cases: [

      ],

      assumptions: ["Create allocates secret metadata and policy context"],
      unknowns: ["Cross-region create latency under control-plane load"]
    }
  },
  {
    operation: "AddSecretVersion",
    behavior: {
      side_effects: WritesState,
      idempotent: false,
      idempotency_keys: null,
      determinism: Deterministic,
      failure_modes: [
        { name: "SecretMissing", condition: "parent_secret_missing", http_status: 404, recoverable: false, retry_safe: false }
      ],
      edge_cases: [
        { description: "Version state may default to enabled immediately", trigger: null, severity: Low }
      ],
      confidence: HighConfidence,
      prerequisites: [{ description: "Caller can add versions to existing secret", kind: Capability }],
      assumptions: ["Version append is monotonic and does not mutate existing versions"],
      unknowns: ["Per-provider limits for versions per secret over long retention windows"]
    }
  }
]

# dsl/extdeps/yaml.dag
```
// extdeps/yaml.dag -- "What is YAML?"
//
// Tautological model of YAML as a serialization format.
// Thin parameterization of std/render.dag primitives for YAML's
// specific syntax: 2-space indent, ": " kv separator, "- " list
// prefix, "#" comments.
//
// Follows the extdeps pattern: facts about an external system,
// no opinions about our repo.
//
// Consumers:
//   tools/cigen.dag — CI YAML rendering

module extdeps.yaml

import std.languages { yaml_format }
import std.render {
  config_format_header, format_comment,
  indent_text, kv_pair, indented_kv, list_item, indented_list_item,
  text_block, list_block, kv_block
}

// YAML indent unit: 2 spaces.
data yaml_unit: String = "  "

// YAML kv separator: colon-space.
data yaml_sep: String = ": "

// YAML list prefix: dash-space.
data yaml_prefix: String = "- "

// ── Scalars ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

fn yaml_mapping(key: String, value: String) -> String {
  kv_pair(key: key, sep: yaml_sep, value: value)
}

fn yaml_sequence_item(value: String) -> String {
  list_item(prefix: yaml_prefix, value: value)
}

// ── Indentation ────────────────────────────────────────────────────

fn yaml_indent(level: Int, text: String) -> String {
  indent_text(level: level, unit: yaml_unit, text: text)
}

fn yaml_indented_mapping(level: Int, key: String, value: String) -> String {
  indented_kv(level: level, unit: yaml_unit, key: key, sep: yaml_sep, value: value)
}

fn yaml_indented_item(level: Int, value: String) -> String {
  indented_list_item(level: level, unit: yaml_unit, prefix: yaml_prefix, value: value)
}

// ── Blocks ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

fn yaml_block(header: String, level: Int, items: List<String>) -> String {
  text_block(header: header, level: level, unit: yaml_unit, items: items)
}

fn yaml_sequence_block(header: String, level: Int, items: List<String>) -> String {
  list_block(header: header, level: level, unit: yaml_unit, prefix: yaml_prefix, items: items)
}

fn yaml_mapping_block(level: Int, entries: List<{ key: String, value: String }>) -> String {
  kv_block(level: level, unit: yaml_unit, sep: yaml_sep, entries: entries)
}

// ── Comments ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────

fn yaml_comment(text: String) -> String {
  format_comment(syntax: yaml_format.comment, text: text)
}

// ── Header ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

fn yaml_header(generator: String, regen_command: String) -> String {
  config_format_header(format: yaml_format, generator: generator, regen_command: regen_command)
}

# dsl/funcs/approval_gate.dag
```
// funcs/approval_gate.dag -- SR-1: Approval gate wiring.
//
// Implements the approval yield protocol (D18, INV-22):
//   1. Worker persists PendingApproval in outcome ledger
//   2. Worker releases claim
//   3. Worker terminates with exit code 42 (pending_approval)
//   4. External approval event (GitHub comment/label) triggers rediscovery
//   5. New worker claims and resumes from the approval point
//
// The approval gate is a stage exit condition, not a blocking wait.
// Workers never busy-wait; they yield and are re-discovered.
//
// Acceptance criteria:
//   - Stage pauses at approval gate
//   - Approval signal resumes within 60s
//   - No duplicate work

module funcs.approval_gate

import interfaces.claim_store { ClaimStore }
import interfaces.outcome_ledger { OutcomeLedger }
import interfaces.issue_provider { IssueProvider }
import interfaces.signal_store { SignalStore }
import std.types {
  NonEmptyStr, StageOutcome, OutcomeStatus, Signal, SignalType
}

// Exit code for pending approval. Workers return this to signal
// that the stage requires human sign-off before continuing.
data APPROVAL_EXIT_CODE: Int = 42

type ApprovalGateResult {
  yielded: Bool
  approval_marker: String
  resume_stage: String
}

// Yield execution at an approval gate.
// Persists PendingApproval status and releases the claim so other
// workers can process different issues while this one awaits approval.
func approval_yield(
  issue_id: NonEmptyStr,
  stage: NonEmptyStr,
  run_key: NonEmptyStr,
  owner: NonEmptyStr,
  generation: Int
) -> { yielded: Bool, approval_marker: String }
  uses outcomes: OutcomeLedger
  uses claims: ClaimStore
{
  // Step 1: Persist PendingApproval in outcome ledger
  outcome = outcomes.upsert(
    run_key: run_key,
    stage: stage,
    outcome: {
      status: "PendingApproval",
      attempt_count: 1,
      retry_budget_remaining: 2
    }
  )

  // Step 2: Release the claim so other workers can process other issues
  release = claims.release(
    issue_id: issue_id,
    stage: stage,
    owner: owner,
    generation: generation
  )

  return {
    yielded: outcome.updated && release.released,
    approval_marker: "sdlc:approval-pending:{stage}"
  }
}

// Resume from an approval gate after approval signal is received.
// Checks that the approval event (label change, comment) has occurred
// and that the outcome ledger shows PendingApproval for the stage.
func approval_resume(
  issue_id: NonEmptyStr,
  stage: NonEmptyStr,
  run_key: NonEmptyStr,
  approval_label: NonEmptyStr
) -> { approved: Bool, resume: Bool }
  uses outcomes: OutcomeLedger
  uses issues: IssueProvider
{
  // Check outcome ledger for PendingApproval status
  prior = outcomes.get(
    run_key: run_key,
    stage: stage
  )

  // Check if issue has the approval label (set by human reviewer)
  issue = issues.get(id: issue_id)
  has_approval = issue.issue.labels |> any(l => l == approval_label)

  let approved = prior.found
    && prior.outcome.status == "PendingApproval"
    && has_approval

  return {
    approved: approved,
    resume: approved
  }
}

// Emit an approval-ready signal for the signal store.
// Called by the webhook handler when a GitHub comment/label indicates approval.
func emit_approval_signal(
  issue_id: NonEmptyStr,
  stage: NonEmptyStr,
  approver: NonEmptyStr
) -> { emitted: Bool }
  uses signals: SignalStore
{
  result = signals.emit(signal: {
    signal_type: "ApprovalGranted",
    idempotency_key: "approval::{issue_id}::{stage}::{approver}",
    payload: {
      issue_id: issue_id,
      stage: stage,
      approver: approver
    },
    produced_at: "now"
  })

  return { emitted: result.emitted }
}

// ── Tests ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

test approval_yield_persists_and_releases {

    input yield/prepare.issue_id -> "42"
    input yield/prepare.stage -> "design-review"
    input yield/prepare.run_key -> "sdlc::42::design-review::v1"
    input yield/prepare.owner -> "worker-1"
    input yield/prepare.generation -> 1

    mock upsert/execute.response -> rest_response(200, {
      updated: true, previous: null
    })

    mock release/execute.response -> rest_response(200, {
      released: true
    })

    expect result.yielded == true
}

test approval_resume_with_label {

    input resume/prepare.issue_id -> "42"
    input resume/prepare.stage -> "design-review"
    input resume/prepare.run_key -> "sdlc::42::design-review::v1"
    input resume/prepare.approval_label -> "approved"

    mock get/execute.response -> rest_response(200, {
      found: true,
      outcome: {
        status: "PendingApproval",
        attempt_count: 1,
        retry_budget_remaining: 2
      }
    })

    mock issues_get/execute.response -> rest_response(200, {
      id: "42",
      title: "Test issue",
      labels: ["sdlc:design-review", "approved"],
      state: "open"
    })

    expect result.approved == true
    expect result.resume == true
}

test approval_resume_without_label {

    input resume/prepare.issue_id -> "42"
    input resume/prepare.stage -> "design-review"
    input resume/prepare.run_key -> "sdlc::42::design-review::v1"
    input resume/prepare.approval_label -> "approved"

    mock get/execute.response -> rest_response(200, {
      found: true,
      outcome: {
        status: "PendingApproval",
        attempt_count: 1,
        retry_budget_remaining: 2
      }
    })

    mock issues_get/execute.response -> rest_response(200, {
      id: "42",
      title: "Test issue",
      labels: ["sdlc:design-review"],
      state: "open"
    })

    expect result.approved == false
    expect result.resume == false
}

# dsl/funcs/retry_budget.dag
```
// funcs/retry_budget.dag -- SR-2: Retry budget persistence.
//
// Retry count survives process restart. Store in outcome ledger
// alongside stage result. Enforce max retries per stage (configurable,
// default 3).
//
// Protocol:
//   1. Before stage execution, read prior outcome from ledger
//   2. If prior.status == Failed and budget > 0: decrement budget, retry
//   3. If prior.status == Failed and budget == 0: terminal failure
//   4. After stage execution, persist new outcome with updated budget
//
// Acceptance criteria:
//   - Failed stage retries up to budget
//   - Budget persists across restarts
//   - Budget=0 → terminal failure

module funcs.retry_budget

import interfaces.outcome_ledger { OutcomeLedger }
import std.types {
  NonEmptyStr, StageOutcome, OutcomeStatus
}

type RetryDecision
  = Proceed { attempt_number: Int, budget_remaining: Int }
  | TerminalFailed { reason: String, total_attempts: Int }
  | FirstAttempt { budget: Int }
  | AlreadySucceeded
  | AwaitingApproval

// Check retry budget before stage execution.
// Returns a RetryDecision that tells the worker whether to proceed,
// terminate, or skip (already succeeded).
func check_retry_budget(
  run_key: NonEmptyStr,
  stage: NonEmptyStr,
  max_retries: Int = 3
) -> { decision: RetryDecision }
  uses outcomes: OutcomeLedger
{
  prior = outcomes.get(
    run_key: run_key,
    stage: stage
  )

  let decision = match prior.found {
    false => FirstAttempt { budget: max_retries }
    true  => match prior.outcome.status {
      Success         => AlreadySucceeded
      PendingApproval => AwaitingApproval
      TerminalFailed  => TerminalFailed {
        reason: "previously marked terminal",
        total_attempts: prior.outcome.attempt_count
      }
      _ => if prior.outcome.retry_budget_remaining > 0 {
        Proceed {
          attempt_number: prior.outcome.attempt_count + 1,
          budget_remaining: prior.outcome.retry_budget_remaining - 1
        }
      } else {
        TerminalFailed {
          reason: "retry budget exhausted",
          total_attempts: prior.outcome.attempt_count
        }
      }
    }
  }

  return { decision: decision }
}

// Record stage outcome with retry budget tracking.
// Called after each stage execution to persist the result
// along with updated attempt count and budget.
func record_with_budget(
  run_key: NonEmptyStr,
  stage: NonEmptyStr,
  success: Bool,
  attempt_number: Int,
  budget_remaining: Int
) -> { recorded: Bool }
  uses outcomes: OutcomeLedger
{
  result = outcomes.upsert(
    run_key: run_key,
    stage: stage,
    outcome: {
      status: match success {
        true  => Success
        false => if budget_remaining > 0 { Failed } else { TerminalFailed }
      },
      attempt_count: attempt_number,
      retry_budget_remaining: budget_remaining
    }
  )

  return { recorded: result.updated }
}

// Mark a stage as terminal failure (budget exhausted or non-retryable error).
func mark_terminal(
  run_key: NonEmptyStr,
  stage: NonEmptyStr,
  attempt_count: Int,
  reason: String
) -> { marked: Bool }
  uses outcomes: OutcomeLedger
{
  result = outcomes.upsert(
    run_key: run_key,
    stage: stage,
    outcome: {
      status: TerminalFailed,
      attempt_count: attempt_count,
      retry_budget_remaining: 0
    }
  )

  return { marked: result.updated }
}

// ── Tests ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

test first_attempt_gets_full_budget {

    input check/prepare.run_key -> "sdlc::42::design::v1"
    input check/prepare.stage -> "design"
    input check/prepare.max_retries -> 3

    mock get/execute.response -> rest_response(200, {
      found: false, outcome: null
    })

    expect result.decision is FirstAttempt
}

test failed_stage_decrements_budget {

    input check/prepare.run_key -> "sdlc::42::design::v1"
    input check/prepare.stage -> "design"
    input check/prepare.max_retries -> 3

    mock get/execute.response -> rest_response(200, {
      found: true,
      outcome: {
        status: "Failed",
        attempt_count: 1,
        retry_budget_remaining: 2
      }
    })

    expect result.decision is Proceed
}

test budget_exhausted_terminal {

    input check/prepare.run_key -> "sdlc::42::design::v1"
    input check/prepare.stage -> "design"
    input check/prepare.max_retries -> 3

    mock get/execute.response -> rest_response(200, {
      found: true,
      outcome: {
        status: "Failed",
        attempt_count: 3,
        retry_budget_remaining: 0
      }
    })

    expect result.decision is TerminalFailed
}

// Success status → AlreadySucceeded (stage completed, no retry needed)
test successful_stage_skips {

    input check/prepare.run_key -> "sdlc::42::design::v1"
    input check/prepare.stage -> "design"

    mock get/execute.response -> rest_response(200, {
      found: true,
      outcome: {
        status: "Success",
        attempt_count: 1,
        retry_budget_remaining: 2
      }
    })

    expect result.decision is AlreadySucceeded
}

// PendingApproval status → AwaitingApproval (not yet succeeded, waiting on human)
test pending_approval_awaits {

    input check/prepare.run_key -> "sdlc::42::design::v1"
    input check/prepare.stage -> "design"

    mock get/execute.response -> rest_response(200, {
      found: true,
      outcome: {
        status: "PendingApproval",
        attempt_count: 1,
        retry_budget_remaining: 2
      }
    })

    expect result.decision is AwaitingApproval
}

test record_preserves_budget {

    input record/prepare.run_key -> "sdlc::42::design::v1"
    input record/prepare.stage -> "design"
    input record/prepare.success -> true
    input record/prepare.attempt_number -> 2
    input record/prepare.budget_remaining -> 1

    mock upsert/execute.response -> rest_response(200, {
      updated: true, previous: null
    })

    expect result.recorded == true
}

# dsl/funcs/review_pipeline.dag
```
// funcs/review_pipeline.dag -- Four-dimension review pipeline (D-1).
//
// Compositional review model: ReviewConcern types parameterize the
// generic dimension_review func. Phasing is structural -- the
// aspirational dimension depends on prior findings via data flow,
// so the DAG scheduler runs coherence/quality/requirements in
// parallel and aspirational sequentially after.
//
// Replaces: lib/review/src/graph.rs (1,727 lines)

module funcs.review_pipeline

import std.types {
  NonEmptyStr, ReviewConcern, DimensionReviewOutput, MergedReviewOutput
}
import services.review.dimension
import services.llm.anthropic
import services.git

// ── Generic dimension review func ─────────────────────────────────────
// One func handles any single dimension. The caller instantiates it
// once per active dimension. The concern type provides the dimension
// name and system prompt preamble.

func dimension_review(
  concern: ReviewConcern,
  artifact: NonEmptyStr,
  criteria: Json,
  depth: String,
  provider: NonEmptyStr,
  model: NonEmptyStr,
  prior_findings: String?
) -> { output: Json, errors: Json }
{
  prompt = review.Dimension.PrepareDimensionPrompt(
    artifact: artifact,
    criteria: criteria,
    dimension: concern.dimension,
    depth: depth,
    prior_findings: prior_findings
  )

  llm_response = llm.Anthropic.Messages(
    model: model,
    messages: [{ role: "user", content: prompt.question }],
    system: prompt.system_prompt,
    max_tokens: 4096
  )

  parsed = review.Dimension.ParseDimensionResponse(
    answer: llm_response.content,
    criteria: criteria,
    dimension: concern.dimension
  )

  return { output: parsed.output, errors: parsed.errors }
}

// ── Full dimension-based review pipeline ──────────────────────────────
// Replaces build_dimension_diff_review_graph_with_cloud_config().
//
// Coherence, quality, requirements have no data dependencies →
// implicit parallelism. Aspirational depends on prior findings →
// sequential after parallel.

func diff_dimension_review(
  base_ref: String,
  provider: NonEmptyStr,
  model: NonEmptyStr,
  coherence_criteria: Json?,
  quality_criteria: Json?,
  requirements_criteria: Json?,
  aspirational_criteria: Json?,
  depth: String
) -> { output: Json, summary: String }
{
  diff = git.Core.Diff(base: base_ref)
  artifact = review.Dimension.FormatDiffArtifact(diff_files: diff.diff)

  // ── Parallel dimensions ─────────────────────────────────────────
  coherence_result = if coherence_criteria != None {
    dimension_review(
      concern: ReviewConcern {
        dimension: "coherence",
        system_prompt_preamble: "You are reviewing for internal consistency -- bugs, contradictions, state mismatches."
      },
      artifact: artifact.artifact,
      criteria: coherence_criteria,
      depth: depth,
      provider: provider,
      model: model
    )
  }

  quality_result = if quality_criteria != None {
    dimension_review(
      concern: ReviewConcern {
        dimension: "quality",
        system_prompt_preamble: "You are reviewing against coding standards and quality best practices."
      },
      artifact: artifact.artifact,
      criteria: quality_criteria,
      depth: depth,
      provider: provider,
      model: model
    )
  }

  requirements_result = if requirements_criteria != None {
    dimension_review(
      concern: ReviewConcern {
        dimension: "requirements",
        system_prompt_preamble: "You are reviewing whether the code accomplishes its stated requirements."
      },
      artifact: artifact.artifact,
      criteria: requirements_criteria,
      depth: depth,
      provider: provider,
      model: model
    )
  }

  // ── Aspirational dimension ──────────────────────────────────────
  aspirational_result = if aspirational_criteria != None {
    prior = review.Dimension.FormatPriorFindings(
      coherence_output: coherence_result?.output,
      quality_output: quality_result?.output,
      requirements_output: requirements_result?.output
    )

    dimension_review(
      concern: ReviewConcern {
        dimension: "aspirational",
        system_prompt_preamble: "You are performing a final synthesis -- classifying each finding as must-fix, defer, or accept."
      },
      artifact: artifact.artifact,
      criteria: aspirational_criteria,
      depth: depth,
      provider: provider,
      model: model,
      prior_findings: prior.prior_findings
    )
  }

  // ── Merge all outputs ───────────────────────────────────────────
  merged = review.Dimension.MergeDimensionOutputs(
    coherence_output: coherence_result?.output,
    quality_output: quality_result?.output,
    requirements_output: requirements_result?.output,
    aspirational_output: aspirational_result?.output
  )

  return { output: merged.output, summary: merged.summary }
}
```

// funcs/sdlc_dispatch_runtime.dag -- compiled SDLC stage dispatch policy.
//
// Each function returns deterministic transition directives for a single
// lifecycle stage. Rust selects which compiled callable to execute based on
// the current stage, while side-effects (claim/retry/report updates) remain
// in the worker runtime.

module funcs.sdlc_dispatch_runtime

func dispatch_idea(
  run_key: String,
  worker_id: String,
  issue_id: Int,
  owner: String,
  repo: String
) -> { next_stage: String, awaiting_approval: Bool, marker: String, message: String, value: Json } {
  return {
    next_stage: "design",
    awaiting_approval: false,
    marker: "design-marker",
    message: "Generated design prompt",
    value: { "next_stage": "design", "awaiting_approval": false }
  }
}

func dispatch_design(
  run_key: String,
  worker_id: String,
  issue_id: Int,
  owner: String,
  repo: String
) -> { next_stage: String, awaiting_approval: Bool, marker: String, message: String, value: Json } {
  return {
    next_stage: "design-review",
    awaiting_approval: false,
    marker: "sdlc:design-review",
    message: "Design review initiated for run_key `{run_key}`",
    value: { "next_stage": "design-review", "awaiting_approval": false }
  }
}

func dispatch_design_review(
  run_key: String,
  worker_id: String,
  issue_id: Int,
  owner: String,
  repo: String
) -> { next_stage: String, awaiting_approval: Bool, marker: String, message: String, value: Json } {
  return {
    next_stage: "design-review",
    awaiting_approval: true,
    marker: "sdlc:approval-gate",
    message: "Awaiting explicit approval for run_key `{run_key}`; transition to `accepted` after review sign-off.",
    value: { "next_stage": "design-review", "awaiting_approval": true }
  }
}

func dispatch_accepted(
  run_key: String,
  worker_id: String,
  issue_id: Int,
  owner: String,
  repo: String
) -> { next_stage: String, awaiting_approval: Bool, marker: String, message: String, value: Json } {
  return {
    next_stage: "implementation",
    awaiting_approval: false,
    marker: "sdlc:implementation",
    message: "Implementation started on branch `sdlc/issue-{issue_id}` for `{owner}/{repo}` (worker: `{worker_id}`)",
    value: { "next_stage": "implementation", "awaiting_approval": false }
  }
}

func dispatch_implementation(
  run_key: String,
  worker_id: String,
  issue_id: Int,
  owner: String,
  repo: String
) -> { next_stage: String, awaiting_approval: Bool, marker: String, message: String, value: Json } {
  return {
    next_stage: "closed",
    awaiting_approval: false,
    marker: "sdlc:acceptance",
    message: "Acceptance testing and close for run_key `{run_key}` in `{owner}/{repo}` (worker: `{worker_id}`)",
    value: { "next_stage": "closed", "awaiting_approval": false }
  }
}

func dispatch_closed(
  run_key: String,
  worker_id: String,
  issue_id: Int,
  owner: String,
  repo: String
) -> { next_stage: String, awaiting_approval: Bool, marker: String, message: String, value: Json } {
  return {

    awaiting_approval: false,
    marker: "",
    message: "",
    value: { "next_stage": "closed", "awaiting_approval": false }
  }
}

# dsl/funcs/sdlc_stages.dag
```
// funcs/sdlc_stages.dag -- Per-stage handler functions for the SDLC pipeline.
//
// Each function handles exactly one lifecycle stage transition.
// The worker dispatch function (sdlc_worker.dag) routes to the
// appropriate handler based on the issue's current stage label.
//
// Stage chain:
//   idea -> design -> design-review -> accepted -> implementing ->
//   code-review -> testing -> done
//
// Each handler:
//   1. Executes stage-specific logic (LLM call, agent spawn, CI, etc.)
//   2. Posts artifact as issue comment (via IssueProvider)
//   3. Transitions labels to next stage (via IssueProvider.set_labels)
//   4. Returns success/failure with next_stage
//
// All handlers use domain interfaces (Layer 2), not concrete services.
// Gap H resolved: real code review (PR diff + LLM) and acceptance testing (cargo).

module funcs.sdlc_stages

import interfaces.issue_provider { IssueProvider }
import interfaces.outcome_ledger { OutcomeLedger }
import interfaces.agent_provider { AgentProvider }
import interfaces.artifact_store { ArtifactStore }
import tools.design { generate_design, review_design }
import services.github.pull_request { PullRequest }
import services.cargo { Build }
import services.llm.anthropic
import std.types {
    IssueLifecycleStage, StageOutcome, OutcomeStatus, ApprovalMode,
    NonEmptyStr, ArtifactPayload, ArtifactType, ArtifactMarker, MarkerKind
}
import std.state_machines {
    determine_stage, stage_to_label
}

// ── Next stage mapping ─────────────────────────────────────────────

fn next_stage_label(current: IssueLifecycleStage) -> String {
  match current {
    Idea            => stage_to_label(stage: Design)
    Design          => stage_to_label(stage: DesignReview)
    DesignReview    => stage_to_label(stage: Accepted)
    Accepted        => stage_to_label(stage: Implementing)
    Implementing    => stage_to_label(stage: CodeReview)
    CodeReview      => stage_to_label(stage: Testing)
    Testing         => stage_to_label(stage: Done)
    Done            => stage_to_label(stage: Done)
  }
}

// ── Code review prompt ─────────────────────────────────────────────

fn code_review_system_prompt() -> String {
  "You are a senior code reviewer. Review the pull request diff for correctness, security, performance, and style. Return a JSON object with fields: approved (bool), findings (array of {check_id, observation, severity, candidate_fix}), summary (string)."
}

fn code_review_user_prompt(title: String, files_summary: String, diff: String) -> String {
  "Review this pull request.\n\nTitle: {title}\n\nChanged files:\n{files_summary}\n\nDiff:\n```\n{diff}\n```\n\nReturn your review as JSON."
}

// ── Stage dispatch ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
// Routes by current stage to the appropriate handler.

func execute_stage(
  issue_id: NonEmptyStr,
  stage: IssueLifecycleStage,
  title: String,
  body: String,
  run_key: NonEmptyStr,
  owner: String,
  repo: String,
  number: Int,
  llm_provider: String,
  llm_model: String
) -> { success: Bool, next_stage: IssueLifecycleStage, artifact_posted: Bool, payload: ArtifactPayload?, value: Json }
  uses issues: IssueProvider
  uses outcomes: OutcomeLedger
  uses agents: AgentProvider
{
  result = match stage {
    Idea            => handle_idea_to_design(
                           issue_id: issue_id, title: title, body: body,
                           run_key: run_key, owner: owner, repo: repo,
                           number: number, llm_provider: llm_provider,
                           llm_model: llm_model)
    Design          => handle_design_to_review(
                           issue_id: issue_id, body: body, run_key: run_key,
                           owner: owner, repo: repo, number: number,
                           llm_provider: llm_provider, llm_model: llm_model)
    DesignReview    => handle_review_to_accepted(
                           issue_id: issue_id, run_key: run_key,
                           owner: owner, repo: repo, number: number)
    Accepted        => handle_accepted_to_implementing(
                           issue_id: issue_id, body: body, run_key: run_key,
                           owner: owner, repo: repo, number: number)
    Implementing    => handle_implementing_to_code_review(
                           issue_id: issue_id, run_key: run_key,
                           owner: owner, repo: repo, number: number)
    CodeReview      => handle_code_review_to_testing(
                           issue_id: issue_id, run_key: run_key,
                           owner: owner, repo: repo, number: number,
                           llm_provider: llm_provider, llm_model: llm_model)
    Testing         => handle_testing_to_done(
                           issue_id: issue_id, run_key: run_key,
                           owner: owner, repo: repo, number: number)
    Done            => handle_done(
                           issue_id: issue_id, run_key: run_key,
                           owner: owner, repo: repo, number: number)
  }

  return {
    success: result.success,
    next_stage: result.next_stage,
    artifact_posted: result.artifact_posted,
    payload: result.payload,
    value: {
      "success": result.success,
      "next_stage": "{result.next_stage}",
      "artifact_posted": result.artifact_posted
    }
  }
}

// ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
// Per-Stage Handlers
// ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

// ── Stage 1: Idea -> Design ────────────────────────────────────────
// Generate a design document from the issue body via LLM.
// Posts design as issue comment. Transitions: sdlc:idea -> sdlc:design.

func handle_idea_to_design(
  issue_id: NonEmptyStr,
  title: String,
  body: String,
  run_key: NonEmptyStr,
  owner: String,
  repo: String,
  number: Int,
  llm_provider: String,
  llm_model: String
) -> { success: Bool, next_stage: IssueLifecycleStage, artifact_posted: Bool, payload: ArtifactPayload? }
  uses issues: IssueProvider
  uses outcomes: OutcomeLedger
{
  // Generate design via LLM
  design = generate_design(
    idea: body,
    context: title,
    provider: llm_provider,
    model: llm_model
  )

  // Post design as comment
  comment = issues.comment(
    id: issue_id,
    body: "## Generated Design\n\n> Design generated\n\n---\n\n{body}\n\n---\n_Generated by gunbc SDLC pipeline_",
    marker: "sdlc:design:{run_key}"
  )

  // Transition labels: idea -> design
  labels = issues.set_labels(
    id: issue_id,
    labels: [stage_to_label(stage: Design)]
  )

  return { success: true, next_stage: Design, artifact_posted: comment.ok, payload: None }
}

// ── Stage 2: Design -> DesignReview ────────────────────────────────
// Review the design document via LLM. Posts findings as comment.
// Transitions: sdlc:design -> sdlc:design-review.

func handle_design_to_review(
  issue_id: NonEmptyStr,
  body: String,
  run_key: NonEmptyStr,
  owner: String,
  repo: String,
  number: Int,
  llm_provider: String,
  llm_model: String
) -> { success: Bool, next_stage: IssueLifecycleStage, artifact_posted: Bool, payload: ArtifactPayload? }
  uses issues: IssueProvider
  uses outcomes: OutcomeLedger
{
  // Review design via LLM
  review = review_design(
    design: body,
    provider: llm_provider,
    model: llm_model
  )

  // Format review findings
  review_body = match review.approved {
    true  => "## Design Review: APPROVED\n\n{review.summary}\n\n---\n_Reviewed by gunbc SDLC pipeline_"
    false => "## Design Review: CHANGES REQUESTED\n\n{review.summary}\n\n---\n_Reviewed by gunbc SDLC pipeline_"
  }

  // Post review as comment
  comment = issues.comment(
    id: issue_id,
    body: review_body,
    marker: "sdlc:design-review:{run_key}"
  )

  // Transition labels: design -> design-review
  labels = issues.set_labels(
    id: issue_id,
    labels: [stage_to_label(stage: DesignReview)]
  )

  return { success: true, next_stage: DesignReview, artifact_posted: comment.ok, payload: None }
}

// ── Stage 3: DesignReview -> Accepted ──────────────────────────────
// Approve the design. Transitions: sdlc:design-review -> sdlc:accepted.

func handle_review_to_accepted(
  issue_id: NonEmptyStr,
  run_key: NonEmptyStr,
  owner: String,
  repo: String,
  number: Int
) -> { success: Bool, next_stage: IssueLifecycleStage, artifact_posted: Bool, payload: ArtifactPayload? }
  uses issues: IssueProvider
{
  // Post acceptance comment
  comment = issues.comment(
    id: issue_id,
    body: "## Design Accepted\n\nDesign review passed. Ready for implementation.\n\n---\n_Approved by gunbc SDLC pipeline_",
    marker: "sdlc:accepted:{run_key}"
  )

  // Transition labels: design-review -> accepted
  labels = issues.set_labels(
    id: issue_id,
    labels: [stage_to_label(stage: Accepted)]
  )

  return { success: true, next_stage: Accepted, artifact_posted: comment.ok, payload: None }
}

// ── Stage 4: Accepted -> Implementing ──────────────────────────────
// Spawn an agent to implement the design. Creates a deterministic
// branch (sdlc/issue-{number}) and dispatches the agent.
// Transitions: sdlc:accepted -> sdlc:implementing.

func handle_accepted_to_implementing(
  issue_id: NonEmptyStr,
  body: String,
  run_key: NonEmptyStr,
  owner: String,
  repo: String,
  number: Int
) -> { success: Bool, next_stage: IssueLifecycleStage, artifact_posted: Bool, payload: ArtifactPayload? }
  uses issues: IssueProvider
  uses agents: AgentProvider
{
  // Deterministic branch name per issue
  branch = "sdlc/issue-{number}"

  // Spawn agent
  agent = agents.spawn(
    prompt: "Implement the design for issue #{number}:\n\n{body}",
    repo_path: ".",
    branch: branch,
    model: None,
    timeout_seconds: 600,
    approval_mode: FullAuto
  )

  // Post dispatch notification
  comment = issues.comment(
    id: issue_id,
    body: "## Agent Dispatched\n\nAgent run `{agent.run_id}` started on branch `{branch}`.\nImplementation in progress.\n\n---\n_Dispatched by gunbc SDLC pipeline_",
    marker: "sdlc:implementing:{run_key}"
  )

  // Transition labels: accepted -> implementing
  labels = issues.set_labels(
    id: issue_id,
    labels: [stage_to_label(stage: Implementing)]
  )

  return {
    success: agent.started,
    next_stage: Implementing,
    artifact_posted: comment.ok,
    payload: None
  }
}

// ── Stage 5: Implementing -> CodeReview ────────────────────────────
// Agent has completed. Poll result, create a PR from the agent's
// branch, and transition to code review.
// Transitions: sdlc:implementing -> sdlc:code-review.

func handle_implementing_to_code_review(
  issue_id: NonEmptyStr,
  run_key: NonEmptyStr,
  owner: String,
  repo: String,
  number: Int
) -> { success: Bool, next_stage: IssueLifecycleStage, artifact_posted: Bool, payload: ArtifactPayload? }
  uses issues: IssueProvider
  uses agents: AgentProvider
  uses outcomes: OutcomeLedger
{
  branch = "sdlc/issue-{number}"

  // Retrieve the agent run_id from the prior "accepted" stage outcome.
  // The worker stores agent_run_id in the outcome payload after spawn.
  accepted_run_key = "sdlc::{owner}/{repo}#{number}::Accepted::v1"
  prior_outcome = outcomes.get(
    run_key: accepted_run_key,
    stage: Accepted
  )
  agent_run_id = prior_outcome.outcome.payload.agent_run_id

  // Poll agent for completion
  agent_status = agents.poll(run_id: agent_run_id)

  // Create PR from agent branch
  pr = PullRequest.Create(
    owner: owner,
    repo: repo,
    title: "feat: implement issue #{number}",
    body: "Closes #{number}\n\nGenerated by SDLC pipeline run `{run_key}`.\n\n---\n_Created by gunbc SDLC pipeline_",
    head: branch,
    base: "main"
  )

  // Post transition comment
  comment = issues.comment(
    id: issue_id,
    body: "## Code Review Requested\n\nImplementation complete. PR #{pr.number} created.\nBranch: `{branch}`\n\nCode review in progress.\n\n---\n_Transitioned by gunbc SDLC pipeline_",
    marker: "sdlc:code-review:{run_key}"
  )

  // Transition labels: implementing -> code-review
  labels = issues.set_labels(
    id: issue_id,
    labels: [stage_to_label(stage: CodeReview)]
  )

  return { success: true, next_stage: CodeReview, artifact_posted: comment.ok, payload: None }
}

// ── Stage 6: CodeReview -> Testing ─────────────────────────────────
// Real code review: retrieve PR diff, run LLM review, post findings.
// Transitions: sdlc:code-review -> sdlc:testing.

func handle_code_review_to_testing(
  issue_id: NonEmptyStr,
  run_key: NonEmptyStr,
  owner: String,
  repo: String,
  number: Int,
  llm_provider: String,
  llm_model: String
) -> { success: Bool, next_stage: IssueLifecycleStage, artifact_posted: Bool, payload: ArtifactPayload? }
  uses issues: IssueProvider
{
  // Find the PR for this issue (convention: PR head = sdlc/issue-{number})
  pr = PullRequest.Get(
    owner: owner,
    repo: repo,
    number: number
  )

  // List changed files in the PR
  files = PullRequest.ListFiles(
    owner: owner,
    repo: repo,
    number: number
  )

  // Build a summary of changed files
  files_summary = files.files
    |> map(f => "- {f.filename} ({f.status}, +{f.additions}/-{f.deletions})")
    |> join("\n")

  // Get the diff text (from PR body or synthesize from file list)
  diff_text = files.files
    |> map(f => "--- a/{f.filename}\n+++ b/{f.filename}\n{f.patch}")
    |> join("\n\n")

  // Run LLM code review
  review_response = llm.Anthropic.Messages(
    model: llm_model,
    messages: [{
      role: "user",
      content: code_review_user_prompt(
        title: pr.title,
        files_summary: files_summary,
        diff: diff_text
      )
    }],
    system: code_review_system_prompt(),
    max_tokens: 4096
  )

  // Format review findings for comment
  review_text = review_response.content

  // Post code review as PR comment
  pr_comment = PullRequest.AddComment(
    owner: owner,
    repo: repo,
    number: number,
    body: "## Code Review\n\n{review_text}\n\n---\n_Reviewed by gunbc SDLC pipeline_"
  )

  // Post status to issue
  comment = issues.comment(
    id: issue_id,
    body: "## Code Review: COMPLETED\n\nPR #{number} reviewed. Proceeding to acceptance testing.\n\n### Changed Files\n{files_summary}\n\n---\n_Reviewed by gunbc SDLC pipeline_",
    marker: "sdlc:testing:{run_key}"
  )

  // Transition labels: code-review -> testing
  labels = issues.set_labels(
    id: issue_id,
    labels: [stage_to_label(stage: Testing)]
  )

  return { success: true, next_stage: Testing, artifact_posted: comment.ok, payload: None }
}

// ── Stage 7: Testing -> Done ───────────────────────────────────────
// Real acceptance testing: run cargo test + cargo clippy on PR branch.
// Transitions: sdlc:testing -> sdlc:done.

func handle_testing_to_done(
  issue_id: NonEmptyStr,
  run_key: NonEmptyStr,
  owner: String,
  repo: String,
  number: Int
) -> { success: Bool, next_stage: IssueLifecycleStage, artifact_posted: Bool, payload: ArtifactPayload? }
  uses issues: IssueProvider
{
  // Run cargo test
  test_result = Build.Test()

  // Run cargo clippy
  clippy_result = Build.Clippy()

  // Determine overall success
  all_passed = test_result.success && clippy_result.success

  // Format test report
  test_status = match test_result.success {
    true  => "PASSED"
    false => "FAILED"
  }
  clippy_status = match clippy_result.success {
    true  => "PASSED"
    false => "FAILED"
  }

  report_body = match all_passed {
    true  => "## Acceptance Tests: PASSED\n\n| Check | Status |\n|-------|--------|\n| cargo test | {test_status} |\n| cargo clippy | {clippy_status} |\n\nAll checks passed. Issue complete.\n\n---\n_Tested by gunbc SDLC pipeline_"
    false => "## Acceptance Tests: FAILED\n\n| Check | Status |\n|-------|--------|\n| cargo test | {test_status} |\n| cargo clippy | {clippy_status} |\n\n### Test Output\n```\n{test_result.stderr}\n```\n\n### Clippy Output\n```\n{clippy_result.stderr}\n```\n\n---\n_Tested by gunbc SDLC pipeline_"
  }

  // Post result
  comment = issues.comment(
    id: issue_id,
    body: report_body,
    marker: "sdlc:done:{run_key}"
  )

  // Only transition if all passed
  if all_passed {
    labels = issues.set_labels(
      id: issue_id,
      labels: [stage_to_label(stage: Done)]
    )
  }

  return { success: all_passed, next_stage: match all_passed { true => Done, false => Testing }, artifact_posted: comment.ok, payload: None }
}

// ── Stage 8: Done (terminalize, close issue) ───────────────────────
// Final stage. Close the issue and post a summary.

func handle_done(
  issue_id: NonEmptyStr,
  run_key: NonEmptyStr,
  owner: String,
  repo: String,
  number: Int
) -> { success: Bool, next_stage: IssueLifecycleStage, artifact_posted: Bool, payload: ArtifactPayload? }
  uses issues: IssueProvider
{
  // Post final summary
  comment = issues.comment(
    id: issue_id,
    body: "## SDLC Pipeline Complete\n\nAll stages completed successfully. Closing issue.\n\n---\n_Closed by gunbc SDLC pipeline_",
    marker: "sdlc:final:{run_key}"
  )

  // Close the issue
  closed = issues.close(id: issue_id)

  return { success: closed.ok, next_stage: Done, artifact_posted: comment.ok, payload: None }
}

// ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

// funcs/sdlc_validation_runtime.dag -- compiled SDLC validation policy.
//
// This module centralizes implementation-close and validate-pr gate policy
// decisions in DSL so worker command flow remains policy-thin in Rust.

module funcs.sdlc_validation_runtime

func evaluate_review_gate(
  blocking_count: Int,
  blocking_summaries: String
) -> { review_passed: Bool, should_run_ci: Bool, ci_summary: String, review_failure: String } {
  review_passed = blocking_count == 0
  should_run_ci = review_passed
  ci_summary = if should_run_ci { "" } else { "skipped: blocking code review findings" }
  review_failure = if review_passed { "" } else { blocking_summaries }
  return {
    review_passed: review_passed,
    should_run_ci: should_run_ci,
    ci_summary: ci_summary,
    review_failure: review_failure
  }
}

func summarize_validation_status(
  review_passed: Bool,
  ci_passed: Bool
) -> { all_passed: Bool, stage_after: String } {
  all_passed = review_passed && ci_passed
  stage_after = if all_passed { "closed" } else { "implementation" }
  return {
    all_passed: all_passed,
    stage_after: stage_after
  }
}

func implementation_validation_failure(
  intake_key: String,
  review_passed: Bool,
  ci_passed: Bool,
  ci_summary: String,
  review_failure: String
) -> { passed: Bool, failure_message: String } {
  passed = review_passed && ci_passed
  review_failure_message = "implementation validation failed for intake `{intake_key}` due to blocking code review findings: {review_failure}"
  ci_failure_message = "implementation validation failed for intake `{intake_key}`: review_passed={review_passed}, ci_passed={ci_passed}, ci_summary={ci_summary}"
  failure_message = if passed {
    ""
  } else {
    if !review_passed {
      review_failure_message
    } else {
      ci_failure_message
    }
  }
  return {
    passed: passed,
    failure_message: failure_message
  }
}

# dsl/funcs/sdlc_worker.dag
```
// funcs/sdlc_worker.dag -- SDLC worker dispatch function.
//
// The outer loop that drives the SDLC pipeline. Called by a scheduler
// (Cloud Scheduler cron, webhook handler, or CLI). For each open issue
// with an SDLC label, it:
//
//   1. Discovers issues with SDLC labels (via IssueProvider)
//   2. Determines the current lifecycle stage from labels
//   3. Acquires a stage claim (via ClaimStore)
//   4. Checks for prior outcomes / replay-skip (via OutcomeLedger)
//   5. Dispatches the appropriate stage handler (via execute_stage)
//   6. Records outcome and releases claim
//
// This is the "thin worker" -- all business logic lives in the
// per-stage funcs (sdlc_stages.dag). The worker's only job is
// discovery + claim + dispatch + record.
//
// DSL-native implementation of gap analysis Steps 1-5:
//   Step 1: Multi-stage dispatch via execute_stage() router
//   Step 2: Stage handlers advance ledger stage (in sdlc_stages.dag)
//   Step 3: All stage handlers (idea through done) in sdlc_stages.dag
//   Step 4: Worker loop iteration (for issue in issues)
//   Step 5: Integration test for multi-stage progression
//
// Uses domain interfaces (Layer 2), not concrete services.
// Profile binding (profiles/sdlc.dag) selects concrete implementations.

module funcs.sdlc_worker

import interfaces.issue_provider { IssueProvider }
import interfaces.claim_store { ClaimStore }
import interfaces.outcome_ledger { OutcomeLedger }
import interfaces.agent_provider { AgentProvider }
import funcs.sdlc_stages { determine_stage, execute_stage }
import shared.dag_util { stage_result, aggregate_results, format_report }
import std.types {
    TrackedIssue, IssueLifecycleStage, IssueState, StageOutcome, OutcomeStatus,
    StageResult, Summary, NonEmptyStr
}

// ── Configuration ─────────────────────────────────────────────────

// All SDLC stage labels for discovery filter
fn sdlc_discovery_labels() -> String {
  "sdlc:idea,sdlc:design,sdlc:design-review,sdlc:accepted,sdlc:implementing,sdlc:code-review,sdlc:testing,sdlc:done"
}

// Returns the issue number as a string for use as the IssueProvider id.
// The GitHub provider interpolates this into /issues/{id} endpoints,
// so it must be just the number (not a composite key like "owner/repo#N").
fn make_issue_id(number: Int) -> String {
  "{number}"
}

fn make_run_key(owner: String, repo: String, number: Int, stage: IssueLifecycleStage) -> String {
  "sdlc::{owner}/{repo}#{number}::{stage}::v1"
}

// ── Main worker function ──────────────────────────────────────────
// Parameters (owner, repo, worker_id, llm_provider, llm_model) are
// bound at invocation time (CLI args, webhook, cron).
// Discovers all open issues with SDLC labels, claims each,
// dispatches the appropriate stage handler, records outcomes.
//
// Step 4 (gap analysis): worker loop iteration.
// Each invocation processes one stage transition per issue.
// To progress idea -> done, invoke the worker multiple times
// (or use --until-stable flag once implemented).

func dispatch_sdlc(
  owner: String,
  repo: String,
  worker_id: String,
  llm_provider: String,
  llm_model: String
) -> { processed: Int, skipped: Int, conflicts: Int, stages: List<StageResult> }
  uses issues: IssueProvider
  uses claims: ClaimStore
  uses outcomes: OutcomeLedger
  uses agents: AgentProvider
{
  // Step 4a: Discover all open issues with SDLC labels
  discovered = issues.discover(
    labels: ["sdlc:idea", "sdlc:design", "sdlc:design-review", "sdlc:accepted",
             "sdlc:implementing", "sdlc:code-review", "sdlc:testing", "sdlc:done"],
    state: Open
  )

  // Step 4b: Process each discovered issue
  results = for issue in discovered.issues {
    // Determine current stage from labels
    stage = determine_stage(labels: issue.labels)
    issue_id = make_issue_id(number: issue.id)
    run_key = make_run_key(owner: owner, repo: repo, number: issue.id, stage: stage)

    // Step 1: Acquire claim for this (issue_id, stage) pair
    claim = claims.acquire(
      issue_id: issue_id,
      stage: stage,
      owner: worker_id,
      lease_ttl_ms: 30000
    )

    if claim.acquired {
      // Check for prior outcome (replay-skip)
      prior = outcomes.get(
        run_key: run_key,
        stage: stage
      )

      if prior.found && prior.outcome.status == Success {
        // Replay-skip: prior SUCCESS exists, release claim and skip.
        // Failed outcomes are NOT skipped so the worker can retry.
        skip_release = claims.release(
          issue_id: issue_id,
          stage: stage,
          owner: worker_id,
          generation: claim.lease_generation
        )

        stage_result(name: stage, success: true, stderr: "replay-skip")
      } else {
        // Step 1 (gap analysis): dispatch to multi-stage handler
        stage_outcome = execute_stage(
          issue_id: issue_id,
          stage: stage,
          title: issue.title,
          body: issue.body,
          run_key: run_key,
          owner: owner,
          repo: repo,
          number: issue.id,
          llm_provider: llm_provider,
          llm_model: llm_model
        )

        // Record outcome in ledger (Step 2: stage handlers advance stage)
        outcome_record = outcomes.upsert(
          run_key: run_key,
          stage: stage,
          outcome: {
            run_key: run_key,
            stage: stage,
            status: match stage_outcome.success {
              true  => Success
              false => Failed
            },
            payload: stage_outcome.payload,
            error: None,
            attempt_count: 1,
            retry_budget_remaining: 2,
            next_attempt_at: None,
            created_at: "",
            updated_at: ""
          }
        )

        // Release claim after stage execution
        release = claims.release(
          issue_id: issue_id,
          stage: stage,
          owner: worker_id,
          generation: claim.lease_generation
        )

        stage_result(
          name: "{stage}->{stage_outcome.next_stage}",
          success: stage_outcome.success,
          stderr: ""
        )
      }
    } else {
      // Claim conflict: another worker holds this (issue_id, stage)
      stage_result(name: stage, success: false, stderr: "claim-conflict")
    }
  }

  // Aggregate results
  processed_count = results |> filter(r => r.success) |> count()
  skipped_count = results |> filter(r => r.stderr == "replay-skip") |> count()
  conflict_count = results |> filter(r => r.stderr == "claim-conflict") |> count()

  return {
    processed: processed_count,
    skipped: skipped_count,
    conflicts: conflict_count,
    stages: results
  }
}

// ── Tests ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

// Step 5 (gap analysis): integration test for multi-stage progression.

test worker_dispatches_and_advances_stage {

    input dispatch/prepare.owner -> "gunb-ai"
    input dispatch/prepare.repo -> "gunbc"
    input dispatch/prepare.worker_id -> "test-worker-1"
    input dispatch/prepare.llm_provider -> "anthropic"
    input dispatch/prepare.llm_model -> "claude-sonnet-4-20250514"

    // Mock: discover returns one issue at "idea" stage
    mock discover/execute.response -> rest_response(200, {
        issues: [
            {
                id: "42",
                title: "Add feature X",
                body: "We need feature X for the SDLC pipeline.",
                stage: "Idea",
                labels: ["sdlc:idea"],
                url: "https://github.com/gunb-ai/gunbc/issues/42",
                author: "test-user",
                created_at: "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z",
                updated_at: "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"
            }
        ]
    })

    // Mock: claim succeeds
    mock acquire/execute.response -> rest_response(200, {
        acquired: true,
        conflict: false,
        lease_generation: 1
    })

    // Mock: no prior outcome (not a replay)
    mock get/execute.response -> rest_response(200, {
        found: false,
        outcome: null
    })

    // Mock: LLM design generation
    mock design/llm/execute.response -> rest_response(200, {
        content: [{ type: "text", text: "## Design\n\nFeature X implementation." }],
        model: "claude-sonnet-4-20250514",
        stop_reason: "end_turn",
        usage: { input_tokens: 100, output_tokens: 200 }
    })

    // Mock: comment and label mutations
    mock comment/execute.response -> rest_response(201, { comment_id: "999", ok: true })
    mock set_labels/execute.response -> rest_response(200, { ok: true })

    // Mock: outcome upsert
    mock upsert/execute.response -> rest_response(200, { updated: true, previous: null })

    // Mock: claim release
    mock release/execute.response -> rest_response(200, { released: true })

    expect result.processed >= 1
}

test worker_skips_on_claim_conflict {

    input dispatch/prepare.owner -> "gunb-ai"
    input dispatch/prepare.repo -> "gunbc"
    input dispatch/prepare.worker_id -> "test-worker-2"
    input dispatch/prepare.llm_provider -> "anthropic"
    input dispatch/prepare.llm_model -> "claude-sonnet-4-20250514"

    mock discover/execute.response -> rest_response(200, {
        issues: [
            {
                id: "43",
                title: "Already claimed",
                body: "This issue is being processed.",
                stage: "Design",
                labels: ["sdlc:design"],
                url: "https://github.com/gunb-ai/gunbc/issues/43",
                author: "test-user",
                created_at: "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z",
                updated_at: "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"
            }
        ]
    })

    // Mock: claim fails (conflict)
    mock acquire/execute.response -> rest_response(200, {
        acquired: false,
        conflict: true,
        lease_generation: 2
    })

    expect result.conflicts >= 1
}

test worker_replay_skips_completed_stage {

    input dispatch/prepare.owner -> "gunb-ai"
    input dispatch/prepare.repo -> "gunbc"
    input dispatch/prepare.worker_id -> "test-worker-3"

    mock acquire/execute.response -> rest_response(200, {

    })

    // Mock: prior outcome exists with Success status (replay-skip)

        found: true,

    })

    mock release/execute.response -> rest_response(200, { released: true })

test worker_retries_failed_stage {

    input dispatch/prepare.owner -> "gunb-ai"

    mock discover/execute.response -> rest_response(200, {

# dsl/infra/aws/resources.dag
```
// infra/aws/resources.dag -- AWS infrastructure as first-class resources.
//
// Each resource implements an abstract interface from infra/core.dag.
// The acquire block contains the AWS-specific ensure/upsert DAG.
// Same resource model as GCP -- different API calls, same pattern.

module infra.aws.resources

import infra.core { ObjectStorage, Compute, SecretStore, Identity, Queue, QueueMessage }
import infra.spec { ResourceFingerprint, ReconcileAction }
import infra.aws.services
import std.types { Timestamp }


// =========================================================================
// S3 Bucket  --  implements ObjectStorage
// =========================================================================

resource S3Bucket implements ObjectStorage {
  kind: Capability
  mode: ReadWrite
  key: name

  config {
    name: NonEmptyStr
    region: String = "us-east-1"
  }

  acquire {
    check = aws.S3.HeadBucket(bucket: config.name)

    create [when !check.exists] = aws.S3.CreateBucket(
      bucket: config.name,
      region: config.region,
      tags: ResourceFingerprint { spec_hash: hash(config) }.to_tags()
    )

  }

  release {}

  capability read {
    readonly
    idempotent
    input { key: NonEmptyStr }
    output { content: Bytes, found: Bool }
  }

  capability write {
    input { key: NonEmptyStr, content: Bytes }
    output { ok: Bool }
  }

  capability delete {
    input { key: NonEmptyStr }
    output { ok: Bool }
  }

  capability list {
    readonly
    idempotent
    input { prefix: String }
    output { keys: List<NonEmptyStr> }
  }
}


// =========================================================================
// Lambda Function  --  implements Compute
// =========================================================================

resource LambdaFunction implements Compute {
  kind: Capability
  mode: ReadWrite
  key: name

  config {
    name: NonEmptyStr
    region: String = "us-east-1"
    role_arn: NonEmptyStr
    runtime: String = "provided.al2023"
    handler: String = "bootstrap"
    code_s3_bucket: NonEmptyStr
    code_s3_key: NonEmptyStr
    memory_size: Int = 512
    timeout: Int = 300
    env: Map<String, String>?
  }

  acquire {
    check = aws.Lambda.GetFunction(function_name: config.name)

    create [when !check.exists] = aws.Lambda.CreateFunction(
      function_name: config.name,
      runtime: config.runtime,
      handler: config.handler,
      role: config.role_arn,
      code_s3_bucket: config.code_s3_bucket,
      code_s3_key: config.code_s3_key,
      memory_size: config.memory_size,
      timeout: config.timeout,
      environment: config.env,
      tags: ResourceFingerprint { spec_hash: hash(config) }.to_tags()
    )

    // Update if spec changed
    update_code [when check.exists && check.state == "Active"] = aws.Lambda.UpdateFunctionCode(
      function_name: config.name,
      s3_bucket: config.code_s3_bucket,
      s3_key: config.code_s3_key
    )

    update_config [when check.exists] = aws.Lambda.UpdateFunctionConfiguration(
      function_name: config.name,
      memory_size: config.memory_size,
      timeout: config.timeout,
      environment: config.env
    ) [after update_code]

  }

  release {}

  capability deploy {
    input { image: NonEmptyStr, env: Map<String, String>? }
    output { ok: Bool }
  }

  capability invoke {
    input { path: String, body: Json }
    output { response: Json, status: Int }
    // Lambda invocation via function URL or API Gateway
  }

  capability get_url {
    readonly
    idempotent
    input {}
    output { url: Url }
    // Returns the function URL if configured
  }

  capability scale {
    input { min_instances: Int, max_instances: Int }
    output { ok: Bool }
    // Lambda: provisioned concurrency
  }
}


// =========================================================================
// AWS Secret  --  implements SecretStore
// =========================================================================

resource AwsSecret implements SecretStore {
  kind: Capability
  mode: Read
  key: name
  expires: true

  config {
    name: NonEmptyStr
    region: String = "us-east-1"
  }

  acquire {
    check = aws.SecretsManager.DescribeSecret(secret_id: config.name)

    create [when !check.exists] = aws.SecretsManager.CreateSecret(
      name: config.name,
      secret_string: "",   // empty placeholder; value set via write_value
      tags: ResourceFingerprint { spec_hash: hash(config) }.to_tags()
    )

  }

  release {}

  capability read_value {
    readonly
    idempotent
    input {}
    output { value: Secret }
  }

  capability write_value {
    input { value: Secret }
    output { ok: Bool, version: NonEmptyStr }
  }

  capability rotate {
    input { new_value: Secret }
    output { ok: Bool, new_version: NonEmptyStr }
  }

  capability list_versions {
    readonly
    idempotent
    input {}
    output { versions: List<NonEmptyStr> }
  }
}


// =========================================================================
// IAM Role  --  implements Identity
// =========================================================================

resource AwsIamRole implements Identity {
  kind: Capability
  mode: Read
  key: name

  config {
    name: NonEmptyStr
    assume_role_policy: Json
    description: String?
    managed_policy_arns: List<String>
  }

  acquire {
    check = aws.IAM.GetRole(role_name: config.name)

    create [when !check.exists] = aws.IAM.CreateRole(
      role_name: config.name,
      assume_role_policy: config.assume_role_policy,
      description: config.description,
      tags: ResourceFingerprint { spec_hash: hash(config) }.to_tags()
    )

    policies = for policy_arn in config.managed_policy_arns {
      aws.IAM.AttachRolePolicy(
        role_name: config.name,
        policy_arn: policy_arn
      )
    } [after create]

  }

  release {}

  capability assume {
    readonly
    input { scopes: List<String>, lifetime_seconds: Int = 3600 }
    output { token: Secret, expires_at: Timestamp }
    // AWS: maps to STS AssumeRole
  }

  capability grant {
    input { role: NonEmptyStr, target: NonEmptyStr }
    output { ok: Bool }
    // AWS: AttachRolePolicy
  }

  capability revoke {
    input { role: NonEmptyStr, target: NonEmptyStr }
    output { ok: Bool }
    // AWS: DetachRolePolicy
  }
}


// =========================================================================
// SQS Queue  --  implements Queue<String>
// =========================================================================

resource SqsQueue implements Queue<String> {
  kind: Capability
  mode: ReadWrite
  key: name

  config {
    name: NonEmptyStr
    region: String = "us-east-1"
    visibility_timeout: Int = 30
    message_retention_period: Int = 345600
  }

  acquire {
    check = aws.SQS.GetQueueUrl(queue_name: config.name)

    create [when !check.exists] = aws.SQS.CreateQueue(
      queue_name: config.name,
      visibility_timeout: config.visibility_timeout,
      message_retention_period: config.message_retention_period,
      tags: ResourceFingerprint { spec_hash: hash(config) }.to_tags()
    )

  }

  release {}

  capability publish {
    input { message: String }
    output { message_id: NonEmptyStr, ok: Bool }
  }

  capability subscribe {
    readonly
    input {}
    output { messages: List<QueueMessage<String>> }
  }

  capability ack {
    input { message_id: NonEmptyStr }
    output { ok: Bool }
  }

  capability purge {
    input {}
    output { purged_count: Int }
  }
}
