# dsl/services/sdlc/providers/rolling_deploy.dag
```
// services/sdlc/providers/rolling_deploy.dag -- SR-6: Rolling deploy with zero downtime.
//
// Cloud Run traffic migration: deploy new revision → route 10% →
// validate → route 100%. Rollback on health check failure.
//
// Acceptance criteria:
//   - Deploy completes with zero dropped webhook events
//   - Rollback tested

module services.sdlc.providers.rolling_deploy

import std.types { NonEmptyStr }
import std.errors { GcpErrorShape }

// Deployment state machine.
type DeployState
  = Pending
  | DeployingRevision { revision_name: String }
  | CanaryRouting { revision_name: String, traffic_percent: Int }
  | FullRouting { revision_name: String }
  | RolledBack { reason: String, previous_revision: String }

type DeployResult {
  success: Bool
  state: DeployState
  revision_name: String?
  rollback_reason: String?
}

type TrafficSplit {
  revision: String
  percent: Int
}

// Cloud Run service management for zero-downtime deploys.
service cloudrun.Deploy {

  config {
    project_id: NonEmptyStr
    region: NonEmptyStr = "us-central1"
    endpoint: "https://run.googleapis.com"
    auth: BearerToken
    auth_input: access_token
    retry: { max_attempts: 3, backoff: exponential, retry_on: [429, 500, 503] }
  }

  // Deploy a new revision (does not shift traffic).
  operation deploy_revision {
    input {
      access_token: Secret
      service_name: NonEmptyStr
      image: NonEmptyStr
      env_vars: Map<String, String>
    }
    output {
      revision_name: String
      deployed: Bool
    }
    transport rest {
      method: POST,
      path: "/v2/projects/\{project_id\}/locations/\{region\}/services/\{service_name\}:deploy"
    }
    response {
      200 => Json
      400 => GcpErrorShape
      401 => GcpErrorShape
      403 => GcpErrorShape
      404 => GcpErrorShape
      429 => GcpErrorShape
      5xx => GcpErrorShape
    }
  }

  // Set traffic split between revisions.
  operation set_traffic {
    input {
      access_token: Secret
      service_name: NonEmptyStr
      splits: List<TrafficSplit>
    }
    output { applied: Bool }
    transport rest {
      method: PATCH,
      path: "/v2/projects/\{project_id\}/locations/\{region\}/services/\{service_name\}"
    }
    response {
      200 => Json
      400 => GcpErrorShape
      401 => GcpErrorShape
      403 => GcpErrorShape
      429 => GcpErrorShape
      5xx => GcpErrorShape
    }
  }

  // Get current traffic split for a service.
  operation get_traffic {
    input {
      access_token: Secret
      service_name: NonEmptyStr
    }
    output {
      splits: List<TrafficSplit>
      latest_revision: String
    }
    readonly
    transport rest {
      method: GET,
      path: "/v2/projects/\{project_id\}/locations/\{region\}/services/\{service_name\}"
    }
    response {
      200 => Json
      401 => GcpErrorShape
      403 => GcpErrorShape
      404 => GcpErrorShape
      429 => GcpErrorShape
      5xx => GcpErrorShape
    }
  }

  // Check health of a specific revision.
  operation check_revision_health {
    input {
      access_token: Secret
      service_name: NonEmptyStr
      revision_name: NonEmptyStr
    }
    output {
      healthy: Bool
      ready_replicas: Int
      total_replicas: Int
    }
    readonly
    transport rest {
      method: GET,
      path: "/v2/projects/\{project_id\}/locations/\{region\}/services/\{service_name\}/revisions/\{revision_name\}"
    }
    response {
      200 => Json
      404 => GcpErrorShape
      429 => GcpErrorShape
      5xx => GcpErrorShape
    }
  }
}

// Validate that a percent value is in [0, 100].
fn validate_percent(value: Int) -> Bool {
  value >= 0 && value <= 100
}

// Orchestrate a rolling deploy with canary validation.
// Protocol:
//   1. Deploy new revision (no traffic)
//   2. Route 10% traffic to new revision (canary)
//   3. Validate health of new revision
//   4. If healthy: route 100% traffic to new revision
//   5. If unhealthy: rollback to previous revision
type CanarySplitResult
  = Valid { splits: List<TrafficSplit> }
  | InvalidPercent { value: Int, reason: String }

fn build_canary_splits(
  new_revision: String,
  old_revision: String,
  canary_percent: Int
) -> CanarySplitResult {
  match validate_percent(value: canary_percent) {
    false => InvalidPercent {
      value: canary_percent,
      reason: "canary_percent must be between 0 and 100"
    }
    true => Valid {
      splits: [
        { revision: new_revision, percent: canary_percent },
        { revision: old_revision, percent: 100 - canary_percent }
      ]
    }
  }
}

fn build_full_splits(revision: String) -> List<TrafficSplit> {
  [{ revision: revision, percent: 100 }]
}

// ── Tests ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

test deploy_new_revision {

    mock deploy_revision/execute.response -> rest_response(200, {
      name: "projects/gunbai-auto/locations/us-central1/services/sdlc-worker/revisions/sdlc-worker-00002-abc",
      conditions: [{ type: "Ready", status: "True" }]
    })

    expect result.deployed == true
}

test canary_traffic_split {

    let result = build_canary_splits(
      new_revision: "sdlc-worker-00002-abc",
      old_revision: "sdlc-worker-00001-xyz",
      canary_percent: 10
    )

    expect result is Valid
}

test canary_percent_out_of_range {

    let result = build_canary_splits(
      new_revision: "sdlc-worker-00002-abc",
      old_revision: "sdlc-worker-00001-xyz",
      canary_percent: 110
    )

    expect result is InvalidPercent
}

test canary_percent_negative {

    let result = build_canary_splits(
      new_revision: "sdlc-worker-00002-abc",
      old_revision: "sdlc-worker-00001-xyz",
      canary_percent: -5
    )

    expect result is InvalidPercent
}

test rollback_on_unhealthy {

    mock check_revision_health/execute.response -> rest_response(200, {
      ready_replicas: 0,
      total_replicas: 1
    })

    expect result.healthy == false
}
```

# dsl/services/sdlc/providers/structured_logging.dag
```
// services/sdlc/providers/structured_logging.dag -- SR-3: Structured execution logging.
//
// JSON-structured log lines with trace_id, issue_id, stage, node_id,
// duration_ms. Cloud Logging compatible.
//
// Every transport node emits structured log. Logs are queryable by trace_id.
//
// Acceptance criteria:
//   - Every transport node emits structured log
//   - Logs are queryable by trace_id
//   - Cloud Logging compatible JSON format

module services.sdlc.providers.structured_logging

import std.types { NonEmptyStr, EpochMs, Timestamp }

// Structured log entry. Each transport node execution produces one.
// Fields match Cloud Logging structured payload format.
type StructuredLogEntry {
  // Unique trace ID for this pipeline invocation (propagated across all stages)
  trace_id: NonEmptyStr

  // Issue being processed (e.g., "gunb-ai/gunbc#42")
  issue_id: NonEmptyStr

  // Pipeline stage (e.g., "design", "design-review")
  stage: NonEmptyStr

  // DAG node ID (e.g., "execute_transport_github_Issues_get")
  node_id: NonEmptyStr

  // Execution duration in milliseconds
  duration_ms: Int

  // Cloud Logging severity level
  severity: LogSeverity

  // Human-readable message
  message: String

  // Timestamp (ISO 8601)
  timestamp: Timestamp

  // Transport details (provider, operation, HTTP status)
  transport: TransportLogContext?

  // Error details (if severity >= ERROR)
  error: LogErrorContext?

  // Worker identity
  worker_id: NonEmptyStr
}

type LogSeverity = DEBUG | INFO | WARNING | ERROR | CRITICAL

type TransportLogContext {
  provider: String
  operation: String
  http_status: Int?
  http_method: String?
  endpoint: String?
  request_id: String?
}

type LogErrorContext {
  error_type: String
  message: String
  retryable: Bool
  stack_trace: String?
}

// Execution span for timing pipeline stages.
type ExecutionSpan {
  trace_id: NonEmptyStr
  span_id: NonEmptyStr
  parent_span_id: NonEmptyStr?
  operation_name: String
  start_time: EpochMs
  end_time: EpochMs?
  status: SpanStatus
  attributes: Map<String, String>
}

type SpanStatus = OK | SPAN_ERROR | UNSET

// Log filter for querying structured logs.
type LogFilter {
  trace_id: NonEmptyStr?
  issue_id: NonEmptyStr?
  stage: NonEmptyStr?
  severity_min: LogSeverity?
  time_range_start: EpochMs?
  time_range_end: EpochMs?
}

// Escape a string for safe JSON embedding.
// Handles double quotes, backslashes, and newlines.
fn json_escape(s: String) -> String {
  s
    |> split(delimiter: "\\")
    |> join(separator: "\\\\")
    |> split(delimiter: "\"")
    |> join(separator: "\\\"")
    |> split(delimiter: "\n")
    |> join(separator: "\\n")
    |> split(delimiter: "\t")
    |> join(separator: "\\t")
}

// Format a structured log entry as a JSON-compatible string.
// Cloud Logging auto-parses JSON payloads from stdout.
fn format_log_entry(entry: StructuredLogEntry) -> String {
  let msg = json_escape(s: entry.message)
  let transport_json = match entry.transport {
    Some(t) => ",\"transport\":{\"provider\":\"{json_escape(s: t.provider)}\",\"operation\":\"{json_escape(s: t.operation)}\"}"
    None => ""
  }
  let error_json = match entry.error {
    Some(e) => ",\"error\":{\"type\":\"{json_escape(s: e.error_type)}\",\"message\":\"{json_escape(s: e.message)}\",\"retryable\":{e.retryable}}"
    None => ""
  }
  "{\"severity\":\"{entry.severity}\",\"timestamp\":\"{entry.timestamp}\",\"trace_id\":\"{entry.trace_id}\",\"issue_id\":\"{entry.issue_id}\",\"stage\":\"{entry.stage}\",\"node_id\":\"{entry.node_id}\",\"duration_ms\":{entry.duration_ms},\"message\":\"{msg}\",\"worker_id\":\"{entry.worker_id}\"{transport_json}{error_json}}"
}

// Create a log entry for a successful transport execution.
// timestamp must be provided by the caller (ISO 8601 string from the runtime).
fn log_transport_success(
  trace_id: NonEmptyStr,
  issue_id: NonEmptyStr,
  stage: NonEmptyStr,
  node_id: NonEmptyStr,
  duration_ms: Int,
  worker_id: NonEmptyStr,
  provider: String,
  operation: String,
  http_status: Int,
  timestamp: Timestamp
) -> StructuredLogEntry {
  {
    trace_id: trace_id,
    issue_id: issue_id,
    stage: stage,
    node_id: node_id,
    duration_ms: duration_ms,
    severity: INFO,
    message: "Transport {provider}.{operation} completed ({http_status})",
    timestamp: timestamp,
    transport: ({
      provider: provider,
      operation: operation,
      http_status: http_status as Int?,
      http_method: None,
      endpoint: None,
      request_id: None
    } as TransportLogContext?),
    error: None,
    worker_id: worker_id
  }
}

// Create a log entry for a failed transport execution.
// timestamp must be provided by the caller (ISO 8601 string from the runtime).
fn log_transport_error(
  trace_id: NonEmptyStr,
  issue_id: NonEmptyStr,
  stage: NonEmptyStr,
  node_id: NonEmptyStr,
  duration_ms: Int,
  worker_id: NonEmptyStr,
  provider: String,
  operation: String,
  error_type: String,
  error_message: String,
  retryable: Bool,
  timestamp: Timestamp
) -> StructuredLogEntry {
  {
    trace_id: trace_id,
    issue_id: issue_id,
    stage: stage,
    node_id: node_id,
    duration_ms: duration_ms,
    severity: ERROR as LogSeverity,
    message: "Transport {provider}.{operation} failed: {error_message}",
    timestamp: timestamp,
    transport: ({
      provider: provider,
      operation: operation,
      http_status: None,
      http_method: None,
      endpoint: None,
      request_id: None
    } as TransportLogContext?),
    error: ({
      error_type: error_type,
      message: error_message,
      retryable: retryable,
      stack_trace: None
    } as LogErrorContext?),
    worker_id: worker_id
  }
}

// ── Tests ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

test structured_log_format {

    let entry = log_transport_success(
      trace_id: "trace-001",
      issue_id: "gunb-ai/gunbc#42",
      stage: "design",
      node_id: "execute_transport_github_Issues_get",
      duration_ms: 142,
      worker_id: "worker-1",
      provider: "github.Issues",
      operation: "get",
      http_status: 200,
      timestamp: "2026-03-02T00:00:00Z"
    )

    let formatted = format_log_entry(entry: entry)

    expect formatted contains "trace-001"
    expect formatted contains "design"
    expect formatted contains "142"
}

test structured_log_error_format {

    let entry = log_transport_error(
      trace_id: "trace-002",
      issue_id: "gunb-ai/gunbc#43",
      stage: "claim",
      node_id: "execute_transport_gcs_ClaimStore_acquire",
      duration_ms: 50,
      worker_id: "worker-2",
      provider: "gcs.ClaimStore",
      operation: "acquire",
      error_type: "PreconditionFailed",
      error_message: "412 Precondition Failed",
      retryable: true,
      timestamp: "2026-03-02T00:00:01Z"
    )

    let formatted = format_log_entry(entry: entry)

    expect formatted contains "ERROR"
    expect formatted contains "PreconditionFailed"
    expect formatted contains "retryable"
}

// services/shell.dag -- Shell utility operations.
//
// Operations that wrap specific CLI tools (gcloud, rustup, find, etc.)
// Each gets its own service so the compiler can reason about their
// transport properties independently.
//
// Replaces: various ops scattered across gunbc-app/src/*/ops.rs

module services.shell

import std.types { FilePath, NonEmptyStr, Secret }
import std.errors { GcpErrorShape }
import extdeps.cloud.gcp.core { GcpProject, GcpServiceAccount }
import extdeps.tools.package_managers { PackageManager, InstallSource }

service gcloud.Auth {
  operation Login {
    input { update_adc: Bool = true }
    output { ok: Bool }
    transport shell { argv: ["gcloud", "auth", "login", "--update-adc"] }
    exit {
      0 => Unit
      nonzero => String "Authentication failed"
    }
  }

  operation ReadADC {
    input { path: FilePath = "~/.config/gcloud/application_default_credentials.json" }
    output {
      client_id: String
      client_secret: Secret
      refresh_token: Secret
    }
    readonly
    // Parses JSON: extracts client_id, client_secret, refresh_token
    transport file { op: READ, path: "\{path\}" }
  }
}

service oauth2.Google {
  config { endpoint: "https://oauth2.googleapis.com" }

  operation Refresh {
    input {
      client_id: String
      client_secret: Secret
      refresh_token: Secret
    }
    output {
      access_token: Secret from "access_token"
      expires_in: Int from "expires_in"
    }
    idempotent
    transport rest { method: POST, path: "/token" }
    response {
      200 => Json
      400 => GcpErrorShape
      401 => GcpErrorShape
      5xx => GcpErrorShape
    }
  }
}

service shell.Find {
  operation ListDirs {
    input { path: FilePath, max_depth: Int = 1, min_depth: Int = 1 }
    output { dirs: List<FilePath> }
    readonly
    transport shell { argv: ["find", "{path}", "-maxdepth", "{max_depth}", "-mindepth", "{min_depth}", "-type", "d"] }
    exit {
      0 => Unit
      nonzero => String "Find command failed"
    }
  }
}

service shell.Codegen {
  operation Check {
    input {}
    output { needed: Bool }
    readonly
    // Checks if codegen output files exist / are stale
    transport shell { argv: ["test", "-f", "target/codegen/.stamp"] }
    exit {
      0 => Unit "File exists"
      1 => Unit "File does not exist"
    }
  }

  operation Run {
    input {}
    output {
      success: Bool
      stdout: String
      stderr: String
    }
    transport shell { argv: ["cargo", "run", "--bin", "gunbc-codegen", "--", "codegen"] }
    exit {
      0 => Unit
      nonzero => String "Codegen failed"
    }
  }
}

service rustup.Component {
  operation Add {
    input { component: NonEmptyStr }
    output { success: Bool }
    transport shell { argv: ["rustup", "component", "add", "{component}"] }
    exit {
      0 => Unit
      nonzero => String "Failed to add component"
    }
  }
}

service shell.Env {
  operation Get {
    input { name: NonEmptyStr }
    output { value: String? }
    readonly
    transport shell { argv: ["printenv", "{name}"] }
    exit {
      0 => Unit
      1 => Unit "Variable not set"
    }
  }
}

service shell.OAuth2 {
  operation RefreshToken {
    input { refresh_token: Secret }
    output { access_token: Secret, valid: Bool }
    transport shell { argv: ["curl", "-s", "-X", "POST", "https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token", "-d", "grant_type=refresh_token&refresh_token={refresh_token}"] }
    exit {
      0 => Unit
      nonzero => String "Token refresh failed"
    }
  }
}

service shell.GCloud {
  operation AuthPrintAccessToken {
    input {}
    output { access_token: Secret }
    readonly
    transport shell { argv: ["gcloud", "auth", "print-access-token"] }
    exit {
      0 => Unit
      nonzero => String "Failed to get access token"
    }
  }

  operation SecretManagerAccessVersion {
    input {
      project_id: NonEmptyStr
      secret_name: NonEmptyStr
      version: NonEmptyStr = "latest"
    }
    output { secret_value: Secret }
    readonly
    transport shell { argv: ["gcloud", "secrets", "versions", "access", "{version}", "--secret={secret_name}", "--project={project_id}"] }
    exit {
      0 => Unit
      nonzero => String "Failed to access secret"
    }
  }
}

service shell.Which {
  operation Check {
    input { command: NonEmptyStr }
    output { exists: Bool, path: FilePath? }
    readonly
    transport shell { argv: ["which", "{command}"] }
    exit {
      0 => Unit "Command found"
      1 => Unit "Command not found"
    }
  }
}

# dsl/shared/dag_util.dag
```
// shared/dag_util.dag -- Common utility functions used across tools.
//
// Extracted from repeated patterns in tool .dag files:
//   - Result aggregation (build.dag, ci.dag)
//   - Report formatting (ci.dag)
//   - StageResult construction (build.dag, ci.dag)
//   - Generated file headers (makegen, bootstrap, pragma, deps, docgen)
//   - Render-then-upsert helper (8+ tools)

module shared.dag_util

import std.types {
  Document,
  DocumentLine,
  DocumentSection,
  RenderedTextFile,
  StageResult,
  Summary,
  TextFile,
  TextFilePath
}
// --- Result aggregation -----------------------------------------------

fn aggregate_results(stages: List<StageResult>) -> Summary {
  let passed = stages |> filter(s => s.success) |> count()
  let failed = stages |> filter(s => !s.success && !s.skipped) |> count()
  { total: stages |> count(), passed: passed, failed: failed }
}

fn all_succeeded(stages: List<StageResult>) -> Bool {
  stages |> all(s => s.success || s.skipped)
}

// --- Report formatting ------------------------------------------------

fn format_report(summary: Summary, stages: List<StageResult>) -> String {
  let summary_line = "Total: {summary.total}, Passed: {summary.passed}, Failed: {summary.failed}"
  let detail_lines = stages
    |> map(s => if s.success {
      "[PASS] {s.name}"
    } else {
      if s.skipped {
        "[SKIP] {s.name}"
      } else {
        "[FAIL] {s.name} :: {s.stderr}"
      }
    })
    |> join("\n")
  let report_doc = doc(
    sections: [
      titled_section(
        title: "Report",
        lines: [text_line(text: summary_line), blank_line(), text_line(text: detail_lines)]
      )
    ]
  )
  render_document(document: report_doc)
}

// --- StageResult construction -----------------------------------------
// Avoids verbose inline record construction repeated 9+ times in ci.dag.

fn stage_result(name: String, success: Bool, stderr: String) -> StageResult {
  { name: name, success: success, stdout: "", stderr: stderr, skipped: false }
}

fn skipped_stage(name: String) -> StageResult {
  { name: name, success: false, stdout: "", stderr: "", skipped: true }
}

fn stage_from_output(name: String, success: Bool, stdout: String, stderr: String, skipped: Bool) -> StageResult {
  { name: name, success: success, stdout: stdout, stderr: stderr, skipped: skipped }
}

// --- Generated file header --------------------------------------------
// 7+ render fns start with "# Generated by gunbc {tool}\n".

fn generated_header(tool: String) -> String {
  "# Generated by gunbc {tool}\n"
}

// --- Structured document rendering -------------------------------------
// Shared "rendering engine" for Document/TextFile trees.

fn text_line(text: String) -> DocumentLine {
  { text: text, is_comment: false, is_blank: false }
}

fn comment_line(text: String) -> DocumentLine {
  { text: text, is_comment: true, is_blank: false }
}

fn blank_line() -> DocumentLine {
  { text: "", is_comment: false, is_blank: true }
}

fn section(lines: List<DocumentLine>) -> DocumentSection {
  { title: "", has_title: false, lines: lines }
}

fn titled_section(title: String, lines: List<DocumentLine>) -> DocumentSection {
  { title: title, has_title: true, lines: lines }
}

fn doc(sections: List<DocumentSection>) -> Document {
  {
    header: "",
    has_header: false,
    comment_prefix: "#",
    sections: sections,
    trailing_newline: true
  }
}

fn doc_with_header(header: String, comment_prefix: String, sections: List<DocumentSection>) -> Document {
  {
    header: header,
    has_header: true,
    comment_prefix: comment_prefix,
    sections: sections,
    trailing_newline: true
  }
}

fn render_document_line(line: DocumentLine, comment_prefix: String) -> String {
  if line.is_blank {
    ""
  } else {
    if line.is_comment {
      "{comment_prefix} {line.text}"
    } else {
      line.text
    }
  }
}

fn render_document_section(section: DocumentSection, comment_prefix: String) -> String {
  let title_line = if section.has_title {
    "{comment_prefix} {section.title}"
  } else {
    ""
  }
  let lines = section.lines
    |> map(line => render_document_line(line: line, comment_prefix: comment_prefix))
    |> join("\n")
  if section.has_title {
    "{title_line}\n{lines}"
  } else {
    lines
  }
}

fn render_document(document: Document) -> String {
  let sections = document.sections
    |> map(section => render_document_section(section: section, comment_prefix: document.comment_prefix))
    |> join("\n\n")
  let with_header = if document.has_header {
    "{document.header}\n\n{sections}"
  } else {
    sections
  }
  if document.trailing_newline {
    "{with_header}\n"
  } else {
    with_header
  }
}

# dsl/shared/gist_modes.dag
```
// shared/gist_modes.dag -- Shared helpers for the snapshot/diff/recent pattern.
//
// Both gist and dag-viz (and any future tool that wants to share content
// as a gist) follow the same 3-mode structure:
//
//   snapshot:  produce_content()               -> share
//   diff:      produce_content(base_ref)       -> share
//   recent:    resolve_base(since) -> diff mode -> share
//
// This module factors out the shared pieces:
//   resolve_recent_base  -- "recent" mode base ref resolution
//   share_content        -- branch detection + gist upload
//   branch_context       -- branch detection (used by snapshot/diff modes)

module shared.gist_modes

import services.git
import services.github.gist
import services.shell
import std.resources { Network }
import std.types { CommitSha, Url }

// Get branch context for any mode.
func branch_context() -> { branch: String } {
  current = git.Core.CurrentBranch()

  return {
    branch: current.branch
  }
}

// Resolve the base ref for "recent" mode.
func resolve_recent_base(since: String = "3.days.ago") -> { base_ref: CommitSha, branch: String } {
  ctx = branch_context()
  base = git.Core.RevListBase(since: since)

  return {
    base_ref: base.base_ref,
    branch: ctx.branch
  }
}

// Upload markdown content as a GitHub gist.
func gist_upload(markdown: String, branch: String, base_ref: CommitSha?, public: Bool = false) -> { url: Url }
  uses net: Network
{
  secret = shell.GCloud.SecretManagerAccessVersion(
    project_id: "gunbai-secrets",
    secret_name: "github-token"
  )

  result = github.Gist.Create(
    description: branch,
    content: markdown,
    public: public,
    auth_token: secret.secret_value
  )

  return { url: result.html_url as Url }
}

// Share any markdown content as a gist.
func share_content(markdown: String, branch: String, base_ref: CommitSha?, public: Bool = false) -> { url: Url } {
  result = gist_upload(
    markdown: markdown,
    branch: branch,
    base_ref: base_ref,
    public: public
  )

  return { url: result.url }
}

module std.access

// Lock/Key diagnostic vocabulary for resource acquisition.
//
// Every resource acquisition is a lock interaction. The lock (resource)
// and key (credential/capability) know how to describe themselves.
// The error system delegates to them.
//
// Types only — no fn items in std modules (avoids lowerer injection
// of unconnected nodes when imported transitively). Projection and
// rendering fns live in tool modules or Rust diagnostic.rs.

// What resource is being accessed.
type LockIdentity {
  resource: String,
  mode: String,
  target: String
}

// What credential/capability is being used to access it.
type KeyIdentity {
  scheme: String,
  hint: String,
  source: String
}

# dsl/std/behavioral.dag
```
// std/behavioral.dag -- Behavioral vocabulary for external-system modeling.
//
// Canonical operation behavior schema ported from the-gunbai Understanding
// model and used by Lane 4 extdeps + interface contracts.

module std.behavioral

// How an operation affects the world.
type SideEffects = ReadOnly | WritesState | WritesExternal

// Whether repeated invocations with equal inputs converge to one outcome.
type Determinism = Deterministic | NonDeterministic | EventuallyConsistent

// Severity used by modeled edge cases.
type Severity = Low | Medium | High | Critical

// Confidence assigned to a behavior declaration.
type Confidence = Documented | HighConfidence | MediumConfidence | LowConfidence | Assumed

// Coarse-grained prerequisite kind.
type PrerequisiteKind = Capability | Credential | Infrastructure | Policy | Tooling | Runtime | Other

type FailureMode {
  name: String
  condition: String?
  http_status: Int?
  recoverable: Bool
  retry_safe: Bool
}

type EdgeCase {
  description: String
  trigger: String?
  severity: Severity
}

type Prerequisite {
  description: String
  kind: PrerequisiteKind
}

// Shared contract types used by all interface definitions.
type CapabilityBehaviorContract {
  capability: String
  behavior: OperationBehavior
}

type CapabilityFailureContract {
  capability: String
  failures: List<FailureMode>
}

// Canonical behavior payload attached to operations and capabilities.
type OperationBehavior {
  side_effects: SideEffects
  idempotent: Bool
  idempotency_keys: List<String>?
  determinism: Determinism
  failure_modes: List<FailureMode>
  edge_cases: List<EdgeCase>
  confidence: Confidence
  prerequisites: List<Prerequisite>
  assumptions: List<String>
  unknowns: List<String>
}

# dsl/std/box_draw.dag
```
// std/box_draw.dag -- Terminal box drawing.
//
// Provides consistent box drawing for preambles, errors, and other structured
// output.  Ported from gunb.ai/tools/terminal/box.go, now modeled in DSL.
//
// Box styles:
//   Closed:    ╭─ Title ─────╮    OpenRight:  ╭─ Title ─────
//              │ content     │                │ content
//              ╰─────────────╯                ╰─────────────
//
// Tier-aware: Unicode/Emoji use rounded corners, ASCII uses +/-/|.

module std.box_draw

import std.render { SemanticColor, Span, SpanStyle, Line }
import std.symbols { Tier }
import std.unicode { string_display_width }

// --- Box style ---

type BoxStyle = Closed | OpenRight

// --- Box character set ---
//
// Character set varies by tier.  Data tables keep this declarative.

type BoxChars {
  top_left: String
  top_right: String
  bottom_left: String
  bottom_right: String
  horizontal: String
  vertical: String
}

data unicode_box_chars: BoxChars = {
  top_left: "╭", top_right: "╮",
  bottom_left: "╰", bottom_right: "╯",
  horizontal: "─", vertical: "│"
}

data ascii_box_chars: BoxChars = {
  top_left: "+", top_right: "+",
  bottom_left: "+", bottom_right: "+",
  horizontal: "-", vertical: "|"
}

fn box_chars_for_tier(tier: Tier) -> BoxChars {
  match tier {
    Ascii => ascii_box_chars
    _     => unicode_box_chars
  }
}

// --- Box configuration ---

type BoxConfig {
  title: String
  style: BoxStyle
  width: Int
  min_width: Int
  color: SemanticColor
  content_color: SemanticColor?
  tier: Tier
}

// --- Width calculation ---

fn effective_width(config: BoxConfig, title_part: String) -> Int {
  let base = string_display_width(s: title_part) + 10
  let w1 = if base < config.min_width { config.min_width } else { base }
  match config.style {
    Closed => if w1 < config.width { config.width } else { w1 }
    _      => w1
  }
}

// --- Line builders ---
//
// Each function produces a Line IR value.  The caller is responsible
// for writing them to a sink.

fn box_top_line(config: BoxConfig) -> Line {
  let chars = box_chars_for_tier(tier: config.tier)
  let title_part = chars.horizontal + " " + config.title + " "
  let eff = effective_width(config: config, title_part: title_part)
  let title_width = string_display_width(s: title_part)

  match config.style {
    Closed => {
      let padding = eff - title_width - 2
      let text = chars.top_left + title_part + repeat_char(c: chars.horizontal, n: padding) + chars.top_right
      Line { spans: [Span { text: text, style: SpanStyle { color: config.color, bold: false, italic: false, symbol: null } }], indent: 0, max_width: null }
    }
    OpenRight => {
      let padding = eff - title_width - 1
      let text = chars.top_left + title_part + repeat_char(c: chars.horizontal, n: padding)
      Line { spans: [Span { text: text, style: SpanStyle { color: config.color, bold: false, italic: false, symbol: null } }], indent: 0, max_width: null }
    }
  }
}

fn box_content_line(config: BoxConfig, content: String) -> Line {
  let chars = box_chars_for_tier(tier: config.tier)
  let border_span = Span { text: chars.vertical + " ", style: SpanStyle { color: config.color, bold: false, italic: false, symbol: null } }
  let content_style = match config.content_color {
    null => SpanStyle { color: null, bold: false, italic: false, symbol: null }
    c    => SpanStyle { color: c, bold: false, italic: false, symbol: null }
  }
  let content_span = Span { text: content, style: content_style }
  Line { spans: [border_span, content_span], indent: 0, max_width: null }
}

fn box_bottom_line(config: BoxConfig) -> Line {
  let chars = box_chars_for_tier(tier: config.tier)
  let title_part = chars.horizontal + " " + config.title + " "
  let eff = effective_width(config: config, title_part: title_part)

  match config.style {
    Closed => {
      let fill = eff - 2
      let text = chars.bottom_left + repeat_char(c: chars.horizontal, n: fill) + chars.bottom_right
      Line { spans: [Span { text: text, style: SpanStyle { color: config.color, bold: false, italic: false, symbol: null } }], indent: 0, max_width: null }
    }
    OpenRight => {
      let fill = eff - 1
      let text = chars.bottom_left + repeat_char(c: chars.horizontal, n: fill)
      Line { spans: [Span { text: text, style: SpanStyle { color: config.color, bold: false, italic: false, symbol: null } }], indent: 0, max_width: null }
    }
  }
}

// --- Convenience constructors ---

fn error_box(title: String, tier: Tier) -> BoxConfig {
  BoxConfig {
    title: title,
    style: OpenRight,
    width: 60,
    min_width: 40,
    color: Error,
    content_color: Dim,
    tier: tier
  }
}

fn preamble_box(title: String, tier: Tier) -> BoxConfig {
  BoxConfig {
    title: title,
    style: Closed,
    width: 60,
    min_width: 40,
    color: Accent,
    content_color: null,
    tier: tier
  }
}

fn info_box(title: String, tier: Tier) -> BoxConfig {
  BoxConfig {
    title: title,
    style: OpenRight,
    width: 60,
    min_width: 40,
    color: Info,
    content_color: null,
    tier: tier
  }
}

// --- Helper ---

fn repeat_char(c: String, n: Int) -> String {
  if n <= 0 { return "" }
  let result = chars(s: c) |> fold(
    init: { out: "", remaining: n },
    f: (acc, _) => {
      if acc.remaining <= 0 { acc }
      else { { out: acc.out + c, remaining: acc.remaining - 1 } }
    }
  )
  result.out
}
```

# dsl/std/fermi.dag
```
// std/fermi.dag -- Fermi estimation: order-of-magnitude reasoning.
//
// Abstract vocabulary for magnitude bucketing. Used by:
//   - Test classification (transport cost -> test tier)
//   - Timeout estimation (magnitude -> milliseconds)
//   - Scope estimation (design depth -> LOC/days)
//   - Resource budgeting (cost -> CI budget gate)
//
// Follows the state_machines.dag pattern: type + ordinal fn + comparison fns.
// No repo-specific policy here -- that lives in config/test_policy.dag.

module std.fermi

import std.types { FermiDepth, Milliseconds }

// --- Ordinal mapping (like stage_ordinal in state_machines.dag) -----

fn fermi_ordinal(depth: FermiDepth) -> Int {
  match depth {
    Xs => 0
    S  => 1
    M  => 2
    L  => 3
    Xl => 4
  }
}

// --- Comparison fns -------------------------------------------------

fn fermi_gt(lhs: FermiDepth, rhs: FermiDepth) -> Bool {
  fermi_ordinal(depth: lhs) > fermi_ordinal(depth: rhs)
}

fn fermi_gte(lhs: FermiDepth, rhs: FermiDepth) -> Bool {
  fermi_ordinal(depth: lhs) >= fermi_ordinal(depth: rhs)
}

fn fermi_eq(lhs: FermiDepth, rhs: FermiDepth) -> Bool {
  fermi_ordinal(depth: lhs) == fermi_ordinal(depth: rhs)
}

// --- Composition: max of two magnitudes (the "big-O" rule) ----------

fn fermi_max(lhs: FermiDepth, rhs: FermiDepth) -> FermiDepth {
  if fermi_gt(lhs: lhs, rhs: rhs) { lhs } else { rhs }
}

// --- Composition: max over a list (transitive dominance) ------------

fn fermi_max_of(depths: List<FermiDepth>) -> FermiDepth {
  depths |> fold(init: Xs, f: (acc, d) => fermi_max(lhs: acc, rhs: d))
}

// --- Guard: is depth within budget? ---------------------------------

fn fermi_within_budget(depth: FermiDepth, budget: FermiDepth) -> Bool {
  fermi_ordinal(depth: depth) <= fermi_ordinal(depth: budget)
}

// --- Timeout data (tautological facts, not policy) ------------------

type FermiTimeout {
  depth: FermiDepth
  timeout_ms: Milliseconds
  label: String
}

data fermi_timeouts: List<FermiTimeout> = [
  FermiTimeout { depth: Xs, timeout_ms: 30000,    label: "30 seconds" },
  FermiTimeout { depth: S,  timeout_ms: 300000,   label: "5 minutes" },
  FermiTimeout { depth: M,  timeout_ms: 600000,   label: "10 minutes" },
  FermiTimeout { depth: L,  timeout_ms: 1800000,  label: "30 minutes" },
  FermiTimeout { depth: Xl, timeout_ms: 3600000,  label: "60 minutes" },
]

fn timeout_for_depth(depth: FermiDepth) -> Int {
  match depth {
    Xs => 30000
    S  => 300000
    M  => 600000
    L  => 1800000
    Xl => 3600000
  }
}
```

# dsl/std/fidelity.dag
```
// std/fidelity.dag -- Transport fidelity: cost classification for external calls.
//
// Layers on fermi.dag. Defines transport classification as abstract
// vocabulary (like lint.dag defines lint concepts without being tool-specific).
//
// Used by:
//   - Test generation (derive tier/hermetic from graph structure)
//   - CI gating (skip expensive tests locally)
//   - Cost estimation (timeout budgets per transport class)
//
// No repo-specific policy here -- that lives in config/test_policy.dag.

module std.fidelity

import std.types { FermiDepth }
import std.fermi { fermi_max_of }

// Transport classification (mirrors ServiceTransportClass in compiler)
type TransportClass = LocalDirect | ShellLocal | FileBoundary | RestNetwork | InterfaceStub | Unknown

// Test classification
type TestClass = Unit | Hermetic | Integration

// Transport -> magnitude mapping (tautological: what each transport costs)
fn transport_depth(tc: TransportClass) -> FermiDepth {
  match tc {
    LocalDirect    => Xs
    InterfaceStub  => Xs
    ShellLocal     => S
    FileBoundary   => S
    RestNetwork    => L
    Unknown        => Xl
  }
}

// Transport -> hermetic flag (can it be mocked in DryRun?)
fn transport_hermetic(tc: TransportClass) -> Bool {
  match tc {
    LocalDirect    => true
    InterfaceStub  => true
    ShellLocal     => true
    FileBoundary   => true
    RestNetwork    => false
    Unknown        => false
  }
}

// --- Transitive derivation (the core composition) -------------------

// Given all transport classes reached transitively, derive properties.
// This is the "big-O" rule: max transport dominates.
type DerivedClassification {
  test_class: TestClass
  depth: FermiDepth
  hermetic: Bool
}

fn classify_transports(transports: List<TransportClass>) -> DerivedClassification {
  let depths = transports |> map(tc => transport_depth(tc: tc))
  let max_depth = fermi_max_of(depths: depths)
  let all_hermetic = transports |> all(tc => transport_hermetic(tc: tc))
  let n = transports |> count()
  let test_class = if n == 0 { Unit } else { if all_hermetic { Hermetic } else { Integration } }
  let depth = if n == 0 { Xs } else { max_depth }
  let hermetic = if n == 0 { true } else { all_hermetic }
  DerivedClassification { test_class: test_class, depth: depth, hermetic: hermetic }
}
```

# dsl/std/filesystem.dag
```
// std/filesystem.dag -- Filesystem model: tautological definitions.
//
// "What is a file?" -- answered compositionally from primitives.
//
// Layering:
//   Layer 0: Primitives (EntryKind, SymlinkTarget)
//   Layer 1: Categories (FileEntry -- the composed invariant)
//   Layer 2: Pure functions (is_text_readable, partition_entries)
//   Layer 3: Patterns (classify_files, read_text_files -- in patterns.dag)
//   Layer 4: Tools (gist_snapshot, etc.)

module std.filesystem

import std.types { FilePath, ContentEncoding, MimeType, EntryKind, SymlinkTarget }

// EntryKind and SymlinkTarget are defined in std.types (the lower module)
// and imported here to avoid circular dependencies.

// -- Layer 1: Categories ---------------------------------------------------

// "What is a filesystem entry?" -- the complete invariant.
// This is what Filesystem.probe returns: everything we know about a path.
//
// Parallels Language in languages.dag:
//   Language = { id, name, extensions, comment, naming, types }
//   FileEntry = { path, kind, encoding?, symlink_target?, size, mime? }
type FileEntry {
  path: FilePath
  kind: EntryKind
  encoding: ContentEncoding?     // only for RegularFile or Symlink->TargetFile
  symlink_target: SymlinkTarget? // only for kind = Symlink
  size: Int
  mime: MimeType?
}

// "What is a readable file?" -- the subset we can fs.read().
// A path is readable when it resolves to a regular text file,
// either directly or through a symlink.
//
//   [ReadableEntry] < [FileEntry]
//   [ReadableEntry] = { e in [FileEntry] | is_text_readable(e) }
type ReadableEntry = FileEntry where is_text_readable

// Partition result -- every input entry lands in exactly one list.
type PartitionResult {
  readable: List<FileEntry>      // text files (safe for fs.read)
  skipped: List<FileEntry>       // everything else (with reason)
}

// -- Layer 2: Pure functions -----------------------------------------------

// "Is this entry a text file we can read?"
// Exhaustive over EntryKind -- every branch is explicit.
fn is_text_readable(entry: FileEntry) -> Bool {
  match entry.kind {
    RegularFile => entry.encoding != Binary
    Symlink     => entry.symlink_target == TargetFile and entry.encoding != Binary
    Directory   => false
    Missing     => false
    Other       => false
  }
}

// "Split entries into readable text files vs everything else."
fn partition_entries(entries: List<FileEntry>) -> { readable: List<FileEntry>, skipped: List<FileEntry> } {
  readable = entries |> filter(e => is_text_readable(entry: e))
  skipped  = entries |> filter(e => !is_text_readable(entry: e))
  return { readable: readable, skipped: skipped }
}

// "What skip reason should we show for this entry?"
fn skip_reason(entry: FileEntry) -> String {
  match entry.kind {
    Directory   => "directory"
    Missing     => "missing"
    Other       => "special file"
    Symlink     => match entry.symlink_target {
      TargetDir => "symlink to directory"
      Broken    => "broken symlink"
      TargetFile => "binary file (via symlink)"
    }
    RegularFile => "binary file"
  }
}
```

# dsl/std/languages.dag
```
// std/languages.dag -- Language model: tautological definitions.
//
// Each type is a compositional building block. Each data declaration
// is a tautology -- "what is Rust?", "what is Markdown?" -- that the
// entire codebase inherits.
//
// Layering:
//   Layer 0: Primitives (NamingCase, CommentSyntax, TypeMapping)
//   Layer 1: Categories (TuringComplete, ConfigFormat, MarkupFormat)
//   Layer 2: Languages (Rust, Go, Markdown, HTML, Makefile, ...)
//   Layer 3: Rendering (render_heading, render_code_block, ...)
//   Layer 4: Tools (gist, docgen, etc.)
//
// Generated Rust replaces hand-written code in core/ir/src/language/.

module std.languages

// ── Layer 0: Primitives ──────────────────────────────────────────────

// "How are identifiers cased?" -- universal across all languages.
type NamingCase
  = SnakeCase
  | ScreamingSnakeCase
  | PascalCase
  | CamelCase
  | Lowercase
  | KebabCase

// "What is a comment?" -- universal across all languages.
type CommentSyntax {
  line_prefix: String?
  block_start: String?
  block_end: String?
  doc_prefix: String?
}

// "What is naming?" -- how identifiers are written.
type NamingConvention {
  type_case: NamingCase
  function_case: NamingCase
  variable_case: NamingCase
  constant_case: NamingCase
  module_case: NamingCase
}

// "What is a type system mapping?" -- abstract -> concrete types.
type TypeMapping {
  string: String
  int: String
  float: String
  bool: String
  bytes: String
  list_template: String
  optional_template: String
  map_template: String
}

// ── Layer 1: Categories ──────────────────────────────────────────────

// "What is a language?" -- the complete invariant.
type Language {
  id: String
  name: String
  extensions: List<String>
  comment: CommentSyntax
  naming: NamingConvention?
  types: TypeMapping?
}

// "What is a markup format?" -- subset for non-Turing languages.
type MarkupFormat {
  id: String
  name: String
  extensions: List<String>
  comment: CommentSyntax
  code_fence: String?
}

// "What is a config format?" -- subset for configuration files.
type ConfigFormat {
  id: String
  name: String
  extensions: List<String>
  comment: CommentSyntax
}

// ── Layer 2: Language data declarations ──────────────────────────────

// "What is Rust?"
data rust_language: Language = {
  id: "rust",
  name: "Rust",
  extensions: [".rs"],
  comment: {
    line_prefix: "//",
    block_start: "/*",
    block_end: "*/",
    doc_prefix: "///"
  },
  naming: {
    type_case: PascalCase,
    function_case: SnakeCase,
    variable_case: SnakeCase,
    constant_case: ScreamingSnakeCase,
    module_case: SnakeCase
  },
  types: {
    string: "String",
    int: "i64",
    float: "f64",
    bool: "bool",
    bytes: "Vec<u8>",
    list_template: "Vec<{0}>",
    optional_template: "Option<{0}>",
    map_template: "HashMap<{0}, {1}>"
  }
}

// "What is Go?"
data go_language: Language = {
  id: "go",
  name: "Go",
  extensions: [".go"],
  comment: {
    line_prefix: "//",
    block_start: "/*",
    block_end: "*/",
    doc_prefix: null
  },
  naming: {
    type_case: PascalCase,
    function_case: CamelCase,
    variable_case: CamelCase,
    constant_case: PascalCase,
    module_case: Lowercase
  },
  types: {
    string: "string",
    int: "int64",
    float: "float64",
    bool: "bool",
    bytes: "[]byte",
    list_template: "[]{0}",
    optional_template: "*{0}",
    map_template: "map[{0}]{1}"
  }
}

// "What is Python?"
data python_language: Language = {
  id: "python",
  name: "Python",
  extensions: [".py"],
  comment: {
    line_prefix: "#",
    block_start: null,
    block_end: null,
    doc_prefix: null
  },
  naming: {
    type_case: PascalCase,
    function_case: SnakeCase,
    variable_case: SnakeCase,
    constant_case: ScreamingSnakeCase,
    module_case: SnakeCase
  },
  types: {
    string: "str",
    int: "int",
    float: "float",
    bool: "bool",
    bytes: "bytes",
    list_template: "list[{0}]",
    optional_template: "{0} | None",
    map_template: "dict[{0}, {1}]"
  }
}

// "What is TypeScript?"
data typescript_language: Language = {
  id: "typescript",
  name: "TypeScript",
  extensions: [".ts", ".tsx"],
  comment: {
    line_prefix: "//",
    block_start: "/*",
    block_end: "*/",
    doc_prefix: "/**"
  },
  naming: {
    type_case: PascalCase,
    function_case: CamelCase,
    variable_case: CamelCase,
    constant_case: ScreamingSnakeCase,
    module_case: CamelCase
  },
  types: {
    string: "string",
    int: "number",
    float: "number",
    bool: "boolean",
    bytes: "Uint8Array",
    list_template: "{0}[]",
    optional_template: "{0} | undefined",
    map_template: "Map<{0}, {1}>"
  }
}

// ── Markup formats ───────────────────────────────────────────────────

// "What is Markdown?"
data markdown_format: MarkupFormat = {
  id: "markdown",
  name: "Markdown",
  extensions: [".md", ".markdown"],
  comment: {
    line_prefix: null,
    block_start: "<!-- ",
    block_end: " -->",
    doc_prefix: null
  },
  code_fence: "```"
}

// "What is HTML?"
data html_format: MarkupFormat = {
  id: "html",
  name: "HTML",
  extensions: [".html", ".htm"],
  comment: {
    line_prefix: null,
    block_start: "<!-- ",
    block_end: " -->",
    doc_prefix: null
  },
  code_fence: null
}

// ── Config formats ───────────────────────────────────────────────────

// "What is YAML?"
data yaml_format: ConfigFormat = {
  id: "yaml",
  name: "YAML",
  extensions: [".yml", ".yaml"],
  comment: {
    line_prefix: "#",
    block_start: null,
    block_end: null,
    doc_prefix: null
  }
}

// "What is TOML?"
data toml_format: ConfigFormat = {
  id: "toml",
  name: "TOML",
  extensions: [".toml"],
  comment: {
    line_prefix: "#",
    block_start: null,
    block_end: null,
    doc_prefix: null
  }
}

// "What is a Makefile?"
data makefile_format: ConfigFormat = {
  id: "makefile",
  name: "Makefile",
  extensions: ["Makefile", "*.mk"],
  comment: {
    line_prefix: "#",
    block_start: null,
    block_end: null,
    doc_prefix: null
  }

// "What is a .gitignore?"

  comment: {
    line_prefix: "#",
    block_start: null,
    block_end: null,
    doc_prefix: null
  }
}

// "What is CSS?"

  id: "css",
  name: "CSS",
  extensions: [".css"],
  comment: {
    line_prefix: null,

// std/lint.dag -- Abstract lint/policy concepts.
//
// Universal vocabulary for lint tools. No tool-specific data.
// See extdeps/clippy.dag for clippy-specific domain model.
// See config/arch_rules.dag for this repo's policy choices.

module std.lint

// Where a lint rule originates.
type LintSource = Compiler | ToolPlugin

// A lint rule from any source.
type LintRule {
  source: LintSource
  name: String
  category: String?
}

// What to do when a lint fires.
type LintAction = Deny | Warn | Allow

// Scope of an exemption from a policy rule.
// Uses generic package terminology (not Rust-specific crate names).
type ExemptionScope
  = WholePackage { name: String }
  | PackagePrefix { prefix: String }
  | PackageFile { package_name: String, path: String }
  | PackagePathPrefix { package_name: String, prefix: String }

// std/markdown.dag -- Markdown document model.
//
// Defines a structural representation of Markdown documents. These
// types mirror render_ir.rs::MarkupNode in core/ir -- the DSL is the
// source of truth; generated Rust will eventually replace the
// hand-written rendering layer.
//
// Types only. Rendering fns live in std.markdown_render (pure DSL)
// to avoid the lowerer injecting unconnected fn nodes into consumers.
// render_tree is the only extern func (recursive algorithm in Rust).

module std.markdown

// ── Document structure ───────────────────────────────────────────────

type MarkdownNode
  = Heading { level: Int, text: String }
  | CodeBlock { language: String?, code: String }
  | Paragraph { text: String }
  | BulletList { items: List<String> }
  | NumberedList { items: List<String> }
  | Tree { paths: List<String> }
  | ThematicBreak
  | BlockQuote { text: String }

type MarkdownDoc {
  nodes: List<MarkdownNode>
}

// ── Extern func declarations ──────────────────────────────────────────
//
// render_tree needs recursive tree algorithm (not expressible in DSL).
// Implementation: gunbc-app/src/extern_ops.rs

extern func render_tree(paths: List<String>) -> { return: String }

// Pure DSL rendering fns (including render_heading) are in
// std.markdown_render to avoid the lowerer injecting unconnected fn
// nodes into consumers that import this module.
```

# dsl/std/markdown_render.dag
```
// std/markdown_render.dag -- Markdown rendering functions.
//
// Pure DSL implementations for rendering MarkdownNode/MarkdownDoc to strings.
// Types live in std.markdown (types-only module); rendering fns live here to
// avoid the lowerer injecting unconnected fn nodes into every consumer that
// imports std.markdown.
//
// render_tree remains extern func in std.markdown (recursive tree algorithm).
// render_heading is pure DSL (repeat pipe in this module).

module std.markdown_render

import std.markdown { MarkdownNode, MarkdownDoc, render_tree }

fn render_heading(level: Int, text: String) -> String {
  let prefix = "#" |> repeat(level)
  "{prefix} {text}"
}

fn render_code_block(code: String, language: String?) -> String {
  let lang = language ?? ""
  "```{lang}\n{code}\n```"
}

fn render_bullet_list(items: List<String>) -> String {
  items |> map(item => "- {item}") |> join("\n")
}

fn render_numbered_list(items: List<String>) -> String {
  items |> map(item => "1. {item}") |> join("\n")
}

fn render_node(node: MarkdownNode) -> String {
  match node {
    Heading { level, text } => render_heading(level: level, text: text)
    CodeBlock { language, code } => render_code_block(code: code, language: language)
    Paragraph { text } => text
    BulletList { items } => render_bullet_list(items: items)
    NumberedList { items } => render_numbered_list(items: items)
    Tree { paths } => render_tree(paths: paths)
    ThematicBreak => "---"
    BlockQuote { text } => "> {text}"
  }
}

fn render_markdown(doc: MarkdownDoc) -> String {
  doc.nodes |> map(node => render_node(node: node)) |> join("\n\n")
}
```

# dsl/std/patterns.dag
```
// std/patterns.dag -- Reusable DAG shapes for the gunbc DSL.
//
// Patterns are compile-time expansion templates. Small patterns expand
// inline (no runtime SubDag boundary). Large patterns that represent
// meaningful user-facing workflows should be funcs instead.
//
// Architecture: patterns compose from fundamental steps. Each step is
// independently reusable (e.g., file_content_matches for staleness
// detection without a write). The composition patterns (upsert,
// content_upsert, transaction) add the wiring -- after/when edges --
// that gives the steps their operational meaning.
//
// See dsl-design.md 4.5 and Appendix H for the full pattern catalog.

module std.patterns

import std.resources { Filesystem, Network, AuthContext }
import std.types {
  AccessToken,
  AuthScheme,
  CloudRuntime,
  FilePath,
  Milliseconds,
  NonEmptyStr,
  ProjectId,
  ServiceAccountEmail
}
import std.filesystem { partition_entries, is_text_readable }
import services.gcp.secret_manager
import services.gcp.iam
import services.gcp.sts
import services.shell

// =====================================================================
// Fundamental Steps
// =====================================================================
// Reusable dag steps that patterns compose. Each is independently
// useful outside of any particular pattern.

// Read a file and check if its content matches an expected value.
// Useful independently for: staleness detection, dry-run reporting,
// CI verification ("has this generated file drifted?").

pattern file_content_matches(path: String, expected: String) -> { matches: Bool }
  uses fs: Filesystem(mode: Read)
{
  node read: fs.read(path: path)
  node check: eq(a: expected, b: read.content) -> { equal: Bool }
  return { matches: check.equal }
}

// Classify a list of file paths into readable and skipped partitions.
// Uses Filesystem.probe to determine entry kind and content encoding,
// then partitions using is_text_readable from std.filesystem.
//
// This is the standard pattern for safely consuming file listings
// from services that return unclassified paths (git.Core.LsFiles,
// directory listings, etc). Handles all entry kinds: regular files,
// directories, symlinks, missing paths, and special files.
//
// Every input path appears in exactly one output list.

pattern classify_files(paths: List<FilePath>) -> { readable: List<FilePath>, skipped: List<FilePath> }
  uses fs: Filesystem(mode: Read)
{
  entries = for path in paths {
    fs.probe(path: path)
  }
  partitioned = partition_entries(entries: entries)
  return {
    readable: partitioned.readable |> map(e => e.path),
    skipped: partitioned.skipped |> map(e => e.path)
  }
}

// Read all text files from a list, skipping non-readable entries.
// Composes classify_files (partition step) + parallel fs.read (content step).
//
// Returns both the successfully read files AND the skipped paths,
// so callers can report/log what was excluded. Skipped entries include
// directories, symlinks to directories, broken symlinks, binary files,
// missing paths, and special files.

pattern read_text_files(paths: List<FilePath>) -> { files: List<{ path: FilePath, content: String }>, skipped: List<FilePath> }
  uses fs: Filesystem(mode: Read)
{
  classified = classify_files(paths: paths)

  contents = for path in classified.readable {
    content = fs.read(path: path)
    { path: path, content: content.content }
  }

  return { files: contents, skipped: classified.skipped }
}

// Read all binary files from a list, skipping readable text files.
// Parallel to read_text_files but uses fs.read_bytes for binary-safe I/O.
//
// Returns both the successfully read binary files AND the skipped paths.
// Note: "skipped" here means readable text files (the inverse of
// read_text_files). Non-file entries (dirs, symlinks, missing) are
// also skipped since they can't be read as binary content.

pattern read_binary_files(paths: List<FilePath>) -> { files: List<{ path: FilePath, size: Int }>, skipped: List<FilePath> }
  uses fs: Filesystem(mode: Read)
{
  classified = classify_files(paths: paths)

  data = for path in classified.skipped {
    info = fs.stat(path: path)
    { path: path, size: info.size }
  }

  return { files: data, skipped: classified.readable }
}

// Acquire a subject token based on runtime environment.
// Useful independently for: any workflow that needs a subject token
// without the full credential chain (e.g., direct STS exchange,
// non-GCP federated auth).

pattern acquire_subject_token(
  runtime: CloudRuntime,
  audience: NonEmptyStr
) -> { token: String } {
  node token = match runtime {
    GitHubActions => github_oidc(audience: audience)
    Metadata     => metadata_oidc(audience: audience)
    LocalDev     => local_auth()
  }
  return { token: token.token }
}

// Optionally impersonate a service account.
// Passes through the original token when no SA is specified.
// Useful independently for: any workflow that needs conditional
// SA impersonation outside of the credential chain.

pattern optional_impersonation(
  access_token: String,
  service_account: ServiceAccountEmail?,
  lifetime_seconds: Int where range(min: 1, max: 3600)= 3600
) -> { token: String } {
  node result = match service_account {
    Some(sa) => {
      response = gcp.IAM.GenerateAccessToken(
        access_token: access_token,
        target_sa: sa,
        lifetime_seconds: lifetime_seconds
      )
      { token: response.access_token }
    }
    None => { token: access_token }
  }
  return { token: result.token }
}

// =====================================================================
// Composition Patterns
// =====================================================================
// Each pattern wires fundamental steps (or caller-supplied steps)
// with after/when edges. The pattern IS the wiring.

// --- Ensure (check -> conditional action) -----------------------------
// 2-step conditional: check a condition, act if it demands action.
// The lightest composition pattern. Returns whether the action ran.
//
// Generic: guard predicate is customizable via should_act parameter.
//   Default: c => !c.exists (skip action when resource already exists).
//
// Type system features used:
//   - Check.Output  (associated output type, Level 8)
//   - fn(T) -> Bool (higher-order parameter)
//
// This is the fundamental check-then-act shape that upsert extends
// (with a resolve step) and content_upsert specializes (with
// file_content_matches as the check and fs.write as the action).

pattern ensure<Check, Action>(
  should_act: fn(Check.Output) -> Bool = c => !c.exists
) -> { acted: Bool } {
  node check: Check
  node action [after check, when should_act(check)]: Action
  return { acted: should_act(check) }
}

// --- Upsert (check -> create -> resolve) ------------------------------
// 3-step conditional: check, create if needed, then resolve a result.
// Extends ensure with a resolve step that runs after both check and create.
//
// Generic: return type R is inferred from Resolve's output type.
// Guard is customizable via should_create (default: c => !c.exists).
//
// Type system features used:
//   - Resolve: -> R  (output type variable, Level 7 + Level 8)
//   - fn(T) -> Bool  (higher-order parameter)
//
// Replaces gunbc's UpsertBuilder.

pattern upsert<Check, Create, Resolve: -> R>(
  should_create: fn(Check.Output) -> Bool = c => !c.exists
) -> { value: R } {
  node check: Check
  node create [after check, when should_create(check)]: Create
  node resolve [after check, after create]: Resolve
  return { value: resolve }
}

// --- Content Upsert (check -> conditional write) ----------------------
// Specializes ensure: check = file_content_matches, action = fs.write.
// The most common pattern: ~8 of 13 tools use this.
// Replaces gunbc's add_content_upsert_chain().

pattern content_upsert(content: String, path: String) -> { written: Bool }
  uses fs: Filesystem(mode: ReadWrite)
{
  result = ensure(
    should_act: c => !c.matches,
    check: file_content_matches(path: path, expected: content),
    action: fs.write(path: path, content: content)
  )
  return { written: result.acted }
}

// --- Credential Chain -------------------------------------------------
// OIDC -> STS -> optional impersonation -> secret access -> credential.
// Composes fundamental steps (acquire_subject_token, optional_impersonation)
// with GCP service calls (STS.Exchange, SecretManager.AccessVersion).
//
// This is the largest pattern -- it expands to 8+ transport triplets
// with runtime branching. Defined as a pattern (not func) because
// it's always embedded inside a parent func's SubDag.
//
// Replaces: lib/gcp-ops/src/graph.rs (1,700+ lines)

pattern credential_chain(
  runtime: CloudRuntime,
  audience: NonEmptyStr,
  service_account: ServiceAccountEmail?,
  secret_name: NonEmptyStr,
  project_id: ProjectId,
  scheme: AuthScheme = Bearer,
  header_name: String?,
  source_id: NonEmptyStr,
  required_scopes: List<String>,
  lifetime_seconds: Int where range(min: 1, max: 3600)= 3600
) -> { token: AccessToken }
  uses net: Network
  provides auth: AuthContext
{
  // Step 1: Acquire subject token (reusable step)
  node subject: acquire_subject_token(runtime: runtime, audience: audience)

  // Step 2: Exchange for federated access token
  node access: gcp.STS.Exchange(
    subject_token: subject.token,
    audience: audience
  )

  // Step 3: Optional SA impersonation (reusable step)
  node impersonated: optional_impersonation(
    access_token: access.access_token,
    service_account: service_account,
    lifetime_seconds: lifetime_seconds
  )

  // Step 4: Access the secret (using impersonated token for auth)
  node secret: gcp.SecretManager.AccessVersion(
    access_token: impersonated.token,
    project_id: project_id,
    secret: secret_name
  )

  // Step 5: Assemble credential
  return {
    token: build_token(
      payload: secret.payload,
      scheme: scheme,
      header_name: header_name,
      source_id: source_id,
      required_scopes: required_scopes
    )
  }
}

// --- Transaction (begin -> body -> commit/rollback) --------------------
// Generic: return type R is inferred from Begin's output type.
// Success predicate is customizable (default: b => b.success).
//
// Type system features used:
//   - Begin: -> R    (output type variable)
//   - fn(T) -> Bool  (higher-order parameter)

pattern transaction<Begin: -> R, Body, Commit, Rollback>(
  succeeded: fn(Body.Output) -> Bool = b => b.success
) -> { value: R } {
  node begin: Begin
  node body: Body
  node commit [when succeeded(body)]: Commit
  node rollback [when !succeeded(body)]: Rollback
  return { value: begin }
}

// --- Retry ------------------------------------------------------------

pattern retry<Op>(max_attempts: Int = 3, backoff_ms: Milliseconds = 1000) -> {} {
  node op: Op
}

// --- Approval Yield (D18) -----------------------------------------------
// Addresses deficit D18 from domain-modeling-comprehensive.md §9.
//
// Models the approval gate protocol: when a stage requires human approval,
// the worker persists PENDING_APPROVAL in the outcome ledger, releases
// the claim, and terminates. The issue is rediscovered through normal
// H4 discovery after the approval event occurs.
//
// Key: the worker does NOT busy-wait. AwaitApproval is an async yield
// with claim release (INV-22).
//
// Protocol:
//   1. Worker persists PENDING_APPROVAL in outcome ledger
//   2. Worker releases claim
//   3. Worker terminates execution for this item
//   4. External approval event (label change, comment, webhook) sets READY
//   5. Issue is rediscovered through normal H4 discovery
//   6. New worker claims and resumes from the approval point
//
// Usage in pipeline:
//   node gate: approval_yield(
//     issue_id: id,
//     stage: "design-review",
//     run_key: rk,
//     outcomes: outcomes,
//     claims: claims,
//     owner: "pipelines.sdlc",
//     generation: claim.lease_generation
//   )
//   // Execution stops here. Pipeline is re-entered on next discovery.

// Pattern: approval_yield
//
// Approval yield for human-in-the-loop gates. This pattern will be
// compiled once the DSL supports `uses` clauses on patterns (service
// dependency injection for compile-time templates). Until then, the
// logic lives inline in pipeline stages that need it.
//
// Signature:
//   approval_yield(
//     issue_id: NonEmptyStr,
//     stage: NonEmptyStr,
//     run_key: NonEmptyStr,
//     owner: NonEmptyStr,
//     generation: Int
//   ) -> { yielded: Bool }
//   uses outcomes: OutcomeLedger
//   uses claims: ClaimStore
//
// Steps:
//   1. Persist PendingApproval in outcome ledger
//   2. Release claim (INV-22: AwaitApproval releases claim)
//   3. Signal yield — caller should terminate execution

// --- OIDC implementations (D-3a: WorkloadIdentity flow) ----------------
// Real implementations replacing stubs. Each acquires a subject token
// from the runtime environment using the appropriate protocol.

func github_oidc(audience: String) -> { token: String }
  uses net: Network
{
  url = shell.Env.Get(name: "ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL")
  auth = shell.Env.Get(name: "ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_TOKEN")

  response = github.OIDC.GetToken(
    audience: audience,
    request_url: url.value,
    request_token: auth.value
  )
  return { token: response.subject_token as String }
}

func metadata_oidc(audience: String) -> { token: String }
  uses net: Network
{
  response = gcp.Metadata.GetIdentityToken(audience: audience)
  return { token: response.subject_token as String }
}

// --- Local auth (D-3b: InteractiveAuth flow) ---------------------------
// ADC check -> OAuth2 refresh -> conditional re-auth via gcloud -> merge.
// This replaces ~725 lines of Rust in lib/gcp-ops/src/graph.rs.

func local_auth() -> { token: String }
  uses fs: Filesystem(mode: Read)
{
  adc_path = shell.Env.Get(name: "GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS")

  adc_check = if adc_path.value != None {
    adc_content = fs.read(path: adc_path.value)
    shell.OAuth2.RefreshToken(refresh_token: adc_content.content)
  }

  // If ADC check failed or no credentials, fall back to gcloud auth
  result = if adc_check?.valid != true {
    gcloud_auth = shell.GCloud.AuthPrintAccessToken()
    { token: gcloud_auth.access_token }
  } else {
    { token: adc_check.access_token }
  }

  return { token: result.token }
}

// --- IAM preflight (D-3c: Identity interface) --------------------------
// Ensure the service account has the required IAM bindings.
// Uses getIamPolicy -> check -> conditional setIamPolicy.

fn check_iam_binding(bindings: Json, service_account: String, role: String) -> { has_role: Bool } {
  return { has_role: false }
}

fn add_iam_binding(bindings: Json, service_account: String, role: String) -> { updated_bindings: Json } {
  return { updated_bindings: bindings }
}

func iam_preflight_check(
  access_token: Secret,
  project_id: ProjectId,
  service_account: ServiceAccountEmail,
  required_role: NonEmptyStr
) -> { ok: Bool }
  uses net: Network
{
  policy = gcp.ResourceManager.GetIamPolicy(access_token: access_token, project_id: project_id)

  has_binding = check_iam_binding(
    bindings: policy.bindings,
    service_account: service_account,
    role: required_role
  )

  result = if has_binding.has_role != true {
    updated = add_iam_binding(
      bindings: policy.bindings,
      service_account: service_account,
      role: required_role
    )
    gcp.ResourceManager.SetIamPolicy(
      access_token: access_token,
      project_id: project_id,
      bindings: updated.updated_bindings,
      etag: policy.etag
    )
  }

  return { ok: true }
}
```

# dsl/std/provider_config.dag
```
// std/provider_config.dag -- SR-8: Typed provider config schemas.
//
// Declares the allowed provider-specific config fields for each service
// prefix. The compiler uses these schemas to validate config blocks at
// compile time, replacing the hardcoded allowlist in the lowerer.
//
// Adding a new provider config field:
//   1. Add the field to the appropriate schema type below
//   2. Use it in your service's config block: `field: Type = default`
//   3. The compiler validates that only declared fields are used
//
// A config typo now produces a compiler error with the list of valid fields.

module std.provider_config

import std.types { NonEmptyStr, ProjectId }

// ── GCS provider config ──────────────────────────────────────────────

type GcsProviderConfig {
  bucket: NonEmptyStr
  project_id: ProjectId
}

// ── Pub/Sub provider config ──────────────────────────────────────────

type PubsubProviderConfig {
  topic: NonEmptyStr
  subscription: NonEmptyStr?
  project_id: ProjectId
}

// ── GitHub provider config ───────────────────────────────────────────

type GithubProviderConfig {
  owner: NonEmptyStr
  repo: NonEmptyStr
}

// ── GCP provider config ─────────────────────────────────────────────

type GcpProviderConfig {
  runtime: NonEmptyStr?
  project_id: ProjectId?
  audience: NonEmptyStr?
  region: NonEmptyStr?
  model: NonEmptyStr?
}

// ── File provider config ─────────────────────────────────────────────

type FileProviderConfig {
  dir: NonEmptyStr?
}

// ── LLM agent provider config ────────────────────────────────────────

type LlmAgentProviderConfig {
  provider: NonEmptyStr
  default_model: NonEmptyStr
  max_turns: Int
}

// ── GCP WIF credential provider config ───────────────────────────────

type GcpWifCredentialProviderConfig {
  runtime: NonEmptyStr
  project_id: ProjectId
  audience: NonEmptyStr
}

// ── Local credential provider config ─────────────────────────────────

type LocalCredentialProviderConfig {
  cache_dir: NonEmptyStr?
}

// ── Cloud Run deploy provider config ─────────────────────────────────

type CloudRunProviderConfig {
  project_id: ProjectId
  region: NonEmptyStr
}

// ── Schema registry ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
// Maps service name prefixes to their typed config schemas.
// The compiler uses this to validate provider-specific config fields.
//
// Schema resolution:
//   1. Match service name against prefix (e.g., "gcs." matches "gcs.ClaimStore")
//   2. Extract field names from the matched schema type
//   3. Reject any config field not in the schema → compiler error

data provider_config_schemas: List<{ prefix: String, schema: String }> = [
  { prefix: "gcs.", schema: "GcsProviderConfig" },
  { prefix: "pubsub.", schema: "PubsubProviderConfig" },
  { prefix: "github.", schema: "GithubProviderConfig" },
  { prefix: "gcp.", schema: "GcpProviderConfig" },
  { prefix: "file.", schema: "FileProviderConfig" },
  { prefix: "LlmAgentProvider", schema: "LlmAgentProviderConfig" },
  { prefix: "GcpWifCredentialProvider", schema: "GcpWifCredentialProviderConfig" },
  { prefix: "LocalCredentialProvider", schema: "LocalCredentialProviderConfig" },
  { prefix: "cloudrun.", schema: "CloudRunProviderConfig" }
]

# dsl/std/rate_limit.dag
```
// std/rate_limit.dag -- Rate limiting, retries, and propagation delay vocabulary.

module std.rate_limit

import std.types { Milliseconds, Seconds }

type ResetStrategy = FixedWindow | SlidingWindow | TokenBucket

type RateLimit {
  scope: String
  requests_per_window: Int
  window_seconds: Seconds
  burst: Int?
  reset_strategy: ResetStrategy
}

type BackoffStrategy
  = Exponential { base_ms: Milliseconds, max_ms: Milliseconds }
  | Linear { step_ms: Milliseconds }
  | JitteredExponential { base_ms: Milliseconds, max_ms: Milliseconds }

type RetryTrigger
  = RateLimit
  | Timeout
  | Http429
  | Http500
  | Http503
  | Http5xx
  | Http403Transient
  | Network
  | ApiNotEnabledYet
  | PermissionNotYetPropagated

type RetryPolicy {
  max_attempts: Int
  backoff: BackoffStrategy
  retry_on: List<RetryTrigger>
}

type PropagationDelay {
  typical_ms: Milliseconds
  max_ms: Milliseconds
  description: String
}

// Common presets reused across extdeps and service metadata.
data github_core_limit: RateLimit = {
  scope: "github.core",
  requests_per_window: 5000,
  window_seconds: 3600,
  burst: null,
  reset_strategy: FixedWindow
}

data github_search_limit: RateLimit = {
  scope: "github.search",
  requests_per_window: 30,
  window_seconds: 60,
  burst: null,
  reset_strategy: FixedWindow
}

data default_jittered_retry: RetryPolicy = {
  max_attempts: 5,
  backoff: JitteredExponential { base_ms: 200, max_ms: 8000 },
  retry_on: [RateLimit, Timeout, Http429, Http5xx, Network]
}

data conservative_retry: RetryPolicy = {
  max_attempts: 3,
  backoff: Exponential { base_ms: 500, max_ms: 5000 },
  retry_on: [Http429, Http503, Network]
}
