# dsl/tools/build.dag
```
// tools/build.dag -- Cargo build, test, and clippy in parallel.
//
// Runs cargo build first, then test and clippy in parallel (both
// depend on build success). Aggregates results into a summary.
//
// The aggregate fn uses shared/dag_util helpers instead of inline
// aggregation logic.
//
// Replaces: gunbc-app/src/build/graph.rs (~13 nodes)

module tools.build

import std.types { Summary, StageResult }
import services.cargo
import shared.dag_util { aggregate_results, format_report, stage_from_output }

func build_all() -> { overall_success: Bool, summary: Summary, report: String, build_stderr: String, test_stderr: String, clippy_stderr: String } {
  // Phase 1: Build (must succeed before test/clippy)
  build = cargo.Build.Build()

  // Phase 2: Test and clippy in parallel (both depend on build)
  test = cargo.Build.Test() [after build, when build.success]
  clippy = cargo.Build.Clippy() [after build, when build.success]

  // Phase 3: Aggregate using shared helper
  stages = [
    stage_from_output(name: "build",  success: build.success,  stdout: build.stdout,  stderr: build.stderr,  skipped: false),
    stage_from_output(name: "test",   success: test.success,   stdout: test.stdout,   stderr: test.stderr,   skipped: !build.success),
    stage_from_output(name: "clippy", success: clippy.success, stdout: clippy.stdout, stderr: clippy.stderr, skipped: !build.success)
  ]
  summary = aggregate_results(stages: stages)
  report = format_report(summary: summary, stages: stages)

  return {
    overall_success: build.success && test.success && clippy.success,
    summary: summary,
    report: report,
    build_stderr: build.stderr,
    test_stderr: test.stderr,
    clippy_stderr: clippy.stderr
  }
}
```

# dsl/tools/cigen.dag
```
// tools/cigen.dag -- CI YAML generation.
//
// Renders GitHub Actions and GitLab CI workflow files from DSL data
// declarations. Follows the makegen pattern: extern discovery for
// dynamic values, pure rendering for everything else, content_upsert
// for output.
//
// Composition:
//   Layer 0: std/render.dag          — common render primitives
//   Layer 1: extdeps/yaml.dag        — YAML serialization
//            extdeps/github_actions.dag, extdeps/gitlab_ci.dag
//   Layer 2: config/ci.dag           — our static CI configuration
//   Layer 3: this file               — rendering + entrypoint
//
// Replaces: codegen_cli.rs generate_github_actions_template(),
//           generate_gitlab_ci_template(), validate_*() (~200 lines)

module tools.cigen

import std.patterns { content_upsert }
import extdeps.yaml {
  yaml_header, yaml_indent, yaml_indented_mapping,
  yaml_indented_item, yaml_sequence_block
}
import extdeps.github_actions {
  checkout_action, rust_toolchain_action, cache_action, output_dir
}
import extdeps.gitlab_ci { default_image, output_path }

// ── Extern bridge ──────────────────────────────────────────────────

type CiDiscovery {
  secrets: List<String>
  tool_command: String
  bootstrap_script: String?
}

extern func discover_ci_config() -> CiDiscovery

// ── GitHub Actions: secret syntax ──────────────────────────────────

fn gha_secret_ref(name: String) -> String {
  "$\{\{ secrets.{name} \}\}"
}

fn gha_runner_os_ref() -> String {
  "$\{\{ runner.os \}\}"
}

fn gha_hashfiles_ref(pattern: String) -> String {
  "$\{\{ hashFiles('{pattern}') \}\}"
}

// ── GitHub Actions: rendering ──────────────────────────────────────

fn render_gha_trigger(push_branches: List<String>, pr_branches: List<String>) -> String {
  "on:\n" +
    yaml_sequence_block(header: "  push:\n    branches:", level: 3, items: push_branches) +
    "\n" +
    yaml_sequence_block(header: "  pull_request:\n    branches:", level: 3, items: pr_branches)
}

fn render_gha_permissions(perms: List<{ scope: String, level: String }>) -> String {
  let lines = perms
    |> map(p => yaml_indented_mapping(level: 1, key: p.scope, value: p.level))
    |> join("\n")
  "permissions:\n{lines}"
}

fn render_gha_env(env: List<{ key: String, value: String }>) -> String {
  let lines = env
    |> map(e => yaml_indented_mapping(level: 1, key: e.key, value: e.value))
    |> join("\n")
  "env:\n{lines}"
}

fn render_gha_step_env(env: List<{ key: String, value: String }>) -> String {
  if env |> count() == 0 { return "" }
  let lines = env
    |> map(e => yaml_indented_mapping(level: 5, key: e.key, value: e.value))
    |> join("\n")
  "\n        env:\n{lines}"
}

fn render_gha_uses_step(name: String, action: String, with_block: String) -> String {
  "      - name: {name}\n        uses: {action}{with_block}"
}

fn render_gha_run_step(name: String, command: String, env: List<{ key: String, value: String }>) -> String {
  let env_block = render_gha_step_env(env: env)
  "      - name: {name}\n        run: {command}{env_block}"
}

fn render_checkout_step() -> String {
  render_gha_uses_step(
    name: "Checkout",
    action: checkout_action,
    with_block: "\n        with:\n          fetch-depth: 1"
  )
}

fn render_rust_setup_step() -> String {
  render_gha_uses_step(
    name: "Setup Rust",
    action: rust_toolchain_action,
    with_block: ""
  )
}

fn render_cache_step() -> String {
  let cache_key = "cargo-{gha_runner_os_ref()}-{gha_hashfiles_ref(pattern: "**/Cargo.lock")}"
  let restore_key = "cargo-{gha_runner_os_ref()}-"
  let paths = ["~/.cargo/bin/", "~/.cargo/registry/index/", "~/.cargo/registry/cache/", "~/.cargo/git/db/", "target/"]
  let path_block = paths
    |> map(p => yaml_indent(level: 6, text: p))
    |> join("\n")
  let restore_block = yaml_indent(level: 6, text: restore_key)
  render_gha_uses_step(
    name: "Cache Cargo",
    action: cache_action,
    with_block: "\n        with:\n          path: |\n{path_block}\n\n          key: {cache_key}\n          restore-keys: |\n{restore_block}"
  )
}

fn render_bootstrap_step(script: String) -> String {
  render_gha_run_step(name: "Verify Bootstrap Invariants", command: "|\n{script}", env: [])
}

fn render_ci_run_step(discovery: CiDiscovery) -> String {
  let secret_env = discovery.secrets
    |> map(s => { key: s, value: gha_secret_ref(name: s) })
  let step_env = [{ key: "CARGO_INCREMENTAL", value: "\"1\"" }]
    |> append(items: secret_env)
  render_gha_run_step(name: "Run CI Pipeline", command: discovery.tool_command, env: step_env)
}

fn render_github_steps(discovery: CiDiscovery) -> String {
  let checkout = render_checkout_step()
  let setup = render_rust_setup_step()
  let cache = render_cache_step()
  let bootstrap = match discovery.bootstrap_script {
    null => ""
    script => "\n\n" + render_bootstrap_step(script: script)
  }
  let run = render_ci_run_step(discovery: discovery)
  "{checkout}\n\n{setup}\n\n{cache}{bootstrap}\n\n{run}"
}

fn render_github_workflow(discovery: CiDiscovery) -> String {
  let header = yaml_header(generator: "gunbc-codegen", regen_command: "cargo run -p gunbc-app --bin gunbc-codegen -- cigen")
  let trigger = render_gha_trigger(
    push_branches: ["main"],
    pr_branches: ["main"]
  )
  let perms = render_gha_permissions(perms: [
    { scope: "contents", level: "read" },
    { scope: "id-token", level: "write" }
  ])
  let env = render_gha_env(env: [
    { key: "CARGO_TERM_COLOR", value: "always" },
    { key: "RUSTFLAGS", value: "-D warnings" }
  ])
  let steps = render_github_steps(discovery: discovery)
  let job = "  ci:\n    runs-on: ubuntu-latest\n    timeout-minutes: 30\n    steps:\n{steps}"
  "{header}\n\nname: ci\n\n{trigger}\n\n{perms}\n\n{env}\n\njobs:\n{job}\n"
}

// ── GitLab CI: rendering ───────────────────────────────────────────

fn render_gitlab_variables(env: List<{ key: String, value: String }>, secrets: List<String>) -> String {
  let env_lines = env
    |> map(e => yaml_indented_mapping(level: 1, key: e.key, value: "\"{e.value}\""))
    |> join("\n")
  let secret_lines = secrets
    |> map(s => yaml_indented_mapping(level: 1, key: s, value: "\"${s}\""))
    |> join("\n")
  if secrets |> count() > 0 {
    "variables:\n{env_lines}\n{secret_lines}"
  } else {
    "variables:\n{env_lines}"
  }
}

fn render_gitlab_cache() -> String {
  "cache:\n  key: cargo-$\{CI_COMMIT_REF_SLUG\}\n  paths:\n    - .cargo/\n    - target/"
}

fn render_gitlab_job(tool_command: String) -> String {
  "ci:\n  stage: ci\n  script:\n    - {tool_command}"
}

fn render_gitlab_pipeline(discovery: CiDiscovery) -> String {
  let header = yaml_header(generator: "gunbc-codegen", regen_command: "cargo run -p gunbc-app --bin gunbc-codegen -- cigen")
  let vars = render_gitlab_variables(
    env: [
      { key: "CARGO_TERM_COLOR", value: "always" },
      { key: "RUSTFLAGS", value: "-D warnings" }
    ],
    secrets: discovery.secrets
  )
  let stages = yaml_sequence_block(header: "stages:", level: 1, items: ["ci"])
  let cache = render_gitlab_cache()
  let job = render_gitlab_job(tool_command: discovery.tool_command)
  "{header}\n\nimage: {default_image}\n\n{vars}\n\n{stages}\n\n{cache}\n\n{job}\n"
}

// ── Output paths ───────────────────────────────────────────────────

fn github_output_path() -> String {
  "{output_dir}/ci.yml"
}

fn gitlab_output_path() -> String {
  output_path
}

// ── Entry point ────────────────────────────────────────────────────

func cigen() -> { written: Bool } {
  discovery = discover_ci_config()

  github_yaml = render_github_workflow(discovery: discovery)
  github_result = content_upsert(
    content: github_yaml,
    path: github_output_path()
  )

  gitlab_yaml = render_gitlab_pipeline(discovery: discovery)
  gitlab_result = content_upsert(
    content: gitlab_yaml,
    path: gitlab_output_path()
  )

  return { written: github_result.written || gitlab_result.written }
}
```

// tools/clippy.dag -- Clippy tool installation and linting.
//
// Demonstrates the upsert pattern: check if clippy exists,
// install if missing, then run lint.
//
// Replaces: lib/tools/clippy/src/graph.rs (186 lines)

module tools.clippy

import std.patterns { upsert }
import std.resources { Filesystem }
import services.shell { shell.Which, rustup.Component }
import services.cargo

resource Clippy {
  kind: Capability
  mode: Read
  lifecycle: Persistent

  capability check {
    readonly
    input {}
    output { exists: Bool }
  }

  capability install {
    input {}
    output { installed: Bool }
  }

  capability resolve {
    readonly
    input {}
    output { handle: String }
  }
}

func clippy_lint(paths: List<String>?) -> { clean: Bool, findings: String }
  uses clippy: Clippy
{
  tool = upsert(
    check: clippy.check(),
    create: clippy.install(),
    resolve: clippy.resolve()
  )

  result = cargo.Build.Clippy() [after tool]

  return {
    clean: result.success,
    findings: result.stderr
  }
}

// ── Tests ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

test clippy_lint_all {

    // Transport mocks for the three shell commands
    mock execute_check.response -> shell_response(0, "clippy 0.1.0")
    mock execute_install.response -> shell_response(0, "")
    mock execute_resolve.response -> shell_response(0, "")

    // Input trigger
    input prepare_check.trigger -> true

    expect result.success is Bool
}

# dsl/tools/codegen.dag
```
// tools/codegen.dag -- Conditional codegen execution.
//
// Checks if codegen outputs exist (stamp file). If stale/missing,
// runs the codegen binary and writes a new stamp file.
// Uses conditional execution (when) rather than content_upsert.
//
// Replaces: gunbc-app/src/codegen/graph.rs (~9 nodes)

module tools.codegen

import std.resources { Filesystem }
import services.shell { shell.Codegen }

func codegen() -> { success: Bool, ran: Bool }
  uses fs: Filesystem(mode: ReadWrite)
{
  check = shell.Codegen.Check()

  run = shell.Codegen.Run() [when !check.needed]

  stamp [when run.success] = fs.write(
    path: "target/codegen/.stamp",
    content: "ok"
  )

  return {
    success: check.needed || run.success,
    ran: !check.needed
  }
}

# dsl/tools/deps.dag
```
// tools/deps.dag -- Dependency installation and config generation.
//
// Two modes:
//   1. Install: read deps.toml, run install scripts per-platform
//   2. Generate: render deps.toml from tool registry, content_upsert
//
// Replaces: lib/tools/deps/src/graph.rs

module tools.deps

import std.patterns { content_upsert }
import std.resources { Filesystem }
import std.types { Platform, ToolRegistry }
import shared.dag_util { generated_header }

type DepsManifest {
  deps: List<DepEntry>
}

type DepEntry {
  name: String
  install_script: String
  check_command: String?
  platform: Platform?
}

fn render_deps_toml(registry: ToolRegistry) -> String {
  let header = generated_header(tool: "deps")
  let entries = registry.tools
    |> map(t => "[deps.{t.name}]\ninstall = \"{t.command}\"")
    |> join("\n\n")
  "{header}\n{entries}\n"
}

fn select_platform_deps(manifest: DepsManifest, platform: Platform) -> List<DepEntry> {
  manifest.deps
    |> filter(d => match d.platform {
      Some(p) => p == platform
      None    => true
    })
}

func deps(manifest_path: FilePath = "deps.toml", platform: Platform) -> { all_installed: Bool }
  uses fs: Filesystem(mode: Read)
{
  manifest_content = fs.read(path: manifest_path)
  manifest = parse_deps_toml(content: manifest_content.content)
  platform_deps = select_platform_deps(manifest: manifest, platform: platform)

  results = for dep in platform_deps {
    node check = shell_check(command: dep.check_command) [when dep.check_command]
    node install [when !check.exists] = shell_exec(script: dep.install_script)
    install
  }

  return { all_installed: results |> all(r => r.success) }
}

func deps_generate(registry: ToolRegistry) -> { written: Bool } {
  content = render_deps_toml(registry: registry)
  result = content_upsert(content: content, path: "deps.toml")
  return { written: result.written }
}

// ── Tests ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
//
// NOTE: Complex mock values (FilesystemHandle, Platform) still use Rust
// helpers via @rust_mock_helpers.

// Shared filesystem and platform mocks.
fixture deps_env {
    mock fs_env.handle -> "write_scope"
    mock platform_env.platform -> "linux"
}

test deps_install_dryrun : deps_env {

    // File transport mock: load manifest
    mock load_manifest/execute_load_manifest.response -> file_response("deps.toml")

    // Shell transport mocks: install commands
    mock execute_installs/execute_installs.response -> shell_response(0, "installed ripgrep")

    expect result.installed is Bool
    expect result.installed == true
}

test deps_install_pkg_fails : deps_env {

    // File transport mock: load manifest
    mock load_manifest/execute_load_manifest.response -> file_response("deps.toml")

    // Shell transport mock: install fails
    mock execute_installs/execute_installs.response -> shell_response(1, "error: package not found")

    expect result.installed == false
}

# dsl/tools/design.dag
```
// tools/design.dag -- Design generation and review workflow helpers.
//
// Canonical SDLC design tool module (CG1).
// Uses provider-specific LLM services behind a provider selector.

module tools.design

import services.llm.openai
import services.llm.anthropic

fn design_system_prompt() -> String {
  "You are a senior software architect. Produce a practical, implementation-ready design in markdown."
}

fn review_system_prompt() -> String {
  "Review the software design for correctness, clarity, risks, and testability."
}

fn design_user_prompt(idea: String, context: String?) -> String {
  let context_block = match context {
    Some(c) => "\n\nContext:\n{c}"
    None => ""
  }
  "Create a software design for the following idea.\n\nIdea:\n{idea}{context_block}\n\nReturn markdown with sections: Problem, Approach, Interfaces, Risks, Test Plan, Scope."
}

fn review_user_prompt(design: String) -> String {
  "Review this software design and provide concise findings (blocking/suggestion/info) plus a short summary.\n\n{design}"
}

fn summarize_design(content: String) -> String {
  "Design generated"
}

func generate_design(
  idea: String,
  context: String?,
  provider: String = "anthropic",
  model: String = "claude-sonnet-4-20250514"
) -> { content: String, summary: String, source: String, sections: Json? } {
  prompt = design_user_prompt(idea: idea, context: context)
  content = match provider {
    "openai" => llm.OpenAI.ChatCompletion(
      model: model,
      messages: [
        { role: "system", content: design_system_prompt() },
        { role: "user", content: prompt }
      ],
      temperature: 0.7,
      max_tokens: 4096
    ).content
    _ => llm.Anthropic.Messages(
      model: model,
      messages: [{ role: "user", content: prompt }],
      system: design_system_prompt(),
      temperature: 0.7,
      max_tokens: 4096
    ).content
  }

  return {
    content: content,
    summary: summarize_design(content: content),
    source: "llm",
    sections: None
  }
}

func review_design(
  design: String,
  provider: String = "anthropic",
  model: String = "claude-sonnet-4-20250514"
) -> { findings: Json, approved: Bool, summary: String } {
  prompt = review_user_prompt(design: design)
  review_text = match provider {
    "openai" => llm.OpenAI.ChatCompletion(
      model: model,
      messages: [
        { role: "system", content: review_system_prompt() },
        { role: "user", content: prompt }
      ],
      temperature: 0.1,
      max_tokens: 2048
    ).content
    _ => llm.Anthropic.Messages(
      model: model,
      messages: [{ role: "user", content: prompt }],
      system: review_system_prompt(),
      temperature: 0.1,
      max_tokens: 2048
    ).content
  }

  return {
    findings: [
      {
        check_id: "design-review",
        issue_key: "llm-review",
        observation: review_text,
        severity: "info"
      }
    ],
    approved: review_text != "",
    summary: "Design review completed"
  }
}
```

# dsl/tools/docgen.dag
```
// tools/docgen.dag -- Documentation generation from source files.
//
// Reads source files (templates, graph mocks, generated tests, configs),
// renders a single documentation file, and content_upserts the result.
//
// Replaces: gunbc-app/src/docgen/graph.rs

module tools.docgen

import std.patterns { content_upsert }
import std.resources { Filesystem }
import std.types { Document }
import shared.dag_util { doc, render_document, section, text_line }

// Source file paths -- these are the inputs to the doc renderer
// Note: these are file CONTENTS (read from disk), not file paths.
// The paths are hardcoded in the func body below. The type correctly
// uses String for content (the result of fs.read) -- not FilePath.
type DocgenSources {
  template: String                    // content of docs/ab-writing-workflows.md
  clippy_graph_mock: String           // content of lib/tools/clippy/src/graph_mock.rs
  clippy_generated_tests: String      // content of lib/tools/clippy/src/generated_tests.rs
  clippy_config: String               // content of lib/tools/clippy/src/config.rs
  clippy_graph: String                // content of lib/tools/clippy/src/graph.rs
  clippy_lib: String                  // content of lib/tools/clippy/src/lib.rs
  clippy_lint: String                 // content of lib/tools/clippy/src/lint.rs
  clippy_ops: String                  // content of lib/tools/clippy/src/ops.rs
  clippy_policy: String               // content of lib/tools/clippy/src/policy.rs
}

type DocgenReadTarget {
  name: String
  path: String
  input_port: String
  allow_missing: Bool
}

data read_targets: List<DocgenReadTarget> = [
  { name: "ab_doc_template", path: "docs/ab-writing-workflows.md", input_port: "template", allow_missing: false },
  { name: "clippy_graph_mock", path: "lib/tools/clippy/src/graph_mock.rs", input_port: "clippy_graph_mock", allow_missing: true },
  { name: "clippy_generated_tests", path: "lib/tools/clippy/src/generated_tests.rs", input_port: "clippy_generated_tests", allow_missing: true },
  { name: "clippy_config", path: "lib/tools/clippy/src/config.rs", input_port: "clippy_config", allow_missing: false },
  { name: "clippy_graph", path: "lib/tools/clippy/src/graph.rs", input_port: "clippy_graph", allow_missing: false },
  { name: "clippy_lib", path: "lib/tools/clippy/src/lib.rs", input_port: "clippy_lib", allow_missing: false },
  { name: "clippy_lint", path: "lib/tools/clippy/src/lint.rs", input_port: "clippy_lint", allow_missing: false },
  { name: "clippy_ops", path: "lib/tools/clippy/src/ops.rs", input_port: "clippy_ops", allow_missing: false },
  { name: "clippy_policy", path: "lib/tools/clippy/src/policy.rs", input_port: "clippy_policy", allow_missing: false }
]

fn render_ab_workflows_document(sources: DocgenSources) -> Document {
  let content = sources.template
    |> replace_section("clippy_mock_spec", sources.clippy_graph_mock)
    |> replace_section("clippy_generated_test_excerpt", sources.clippy_generated_tests)
    |> replace_section("appendix_a_clippy", sources.clippy_generated_tests)
    |> replace_section("appendix_b", render_test_listings(sources: sources))
    |> replace_section("appendix_c", render_graph_structure(sources: sources))
    |> replace_section("appendix_d", render_source_artifacts(sources: sources))
  doc(sections: [section(lines: [text_line(text: content)])])
}

fn render_ab_workflows_doc(sources: DocgenSources) -> String {
  render_document(document: render_ab_workflows_document(sources: sources))
}

func docgen() -> { written: Bool }
  uses fs: Filesystem(mode: ReadWrite)
{
  // Read all source files (parallel -- no dependencies between reads)
  template = fs.read(path: "docs/ab-writing-workflows.md")
  clippy_graph_mock = fs.read(path: "lib/tools/clippy/src/graph_mock.rs")
  clippy_generated_tests = fs.read(path: "lib/tools/clippy/src/generated_tests.rs")
  clippy_config = fs.read(path: "lib/tools/clippy/src/config.rs")
  clippy_graph = fs.read(path: "lib/tools/clippy/src/graph.rs")
  clippy_lib = fs.read(path: "lib/tools/clippy/src/lib.rs")
  clippy_lint = fs.read(path: "lib/tools/clippy/src/lint.rs")
  clippy_ops = fs.read(path: "lib/tools/clippy/src/ops.rs")
  clippy_policy = fs.read(path: "lib/tools/clippy/src/policy.rs")

  content = render_ab_workflows_doc(sources: {
    template: template.content,
    clippy_graph_mock: clippy_graph_mock.content,
    clippy_generated_tests: clippy_generated_tests.content,
    clippy_config: clippy_config.content,
    clippy_graph: clippy_graph.content,
    clippy_lib: clippy_lib.content,
    clippy_lint: clippy_lint.content,
    clippy_ops: clippy_ops.content,
    clippy_policy: clippy_policy.content
  })

  result = content_upsert(content: content, path: "docs/ab-writing-workflows.md")

  return { written: result.written }
}

# dsl/tools/gist.dag
```
// tools/gist.dag -- Gist creation tool (snapshot/diff/recent modes).
//
// Three entrypoints: gist, gist_diff, gist_recent (structurally inferred).
// Each func directly calls its service operations; the lowerer's cross-
// callable transport dedup handles cloning shared triplets automatically.
//
// Replaces: lib/tools/gist/src/graph.rs (~1,449 lines)

module tools.gist

import services.git
import services.github.gist
import cloud.gcp.credential { acquire_gcp_secret }
import std.resources { Filesystem, Network }
import std.patterns { read_text_files }
import std.types { CloudRuntime, CommitSha, Url }

// ── Helpers ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

fn render_diff_markdown(diff: String, branch: String, base_ref: CommitSha) -> String {
  "# Diff: {branch} vs {base_ref}\n\n```diff\n{diff}\n```\n"
}

// Recursive markdown assembly stays in Rust until recursive DSL modeling ships.
extern func build_snapshot_content(
  branch: String,
  files: List<String>,
  file_contents: List<String>,
  skipped: List<String>
) -> { return: String }

// ── Entrypoints ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────

func gist(public: Bool = false) -> { url: Url }
  uses fs: Filesystem(mode: Read)
  uses net: Network
{
  branch_info = git.Core.CurrentBranch()
  listing = git.Core.LsFiles()

  result = read_text_files(paths: listing.files)

  content = build_snapshot_content(
    branch: branch_info.branch,
    files: result.files |> map(f => f.path),
    file_contents: result.files |> map(f => f.content),
    skipped: result.skipped
  )
  cred = acquire_gcp_secret(
    runtime: LocalDev,
    project_id: "gunbai-secrets",
    secret_name: "github-token",
    service_account: null,
    header_name: null,
    source_id: "gist",
    required_scopes: ["https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"]
  )
  gist_result = github.Gist.Create(
    description: branch_info.branch,
    content: content,
    public: public,
    auth_token: cred.secret
  )
  return { url: gist_result.html_url as Url }
}

func gist_diff(base_ref: CommitSha = "HEAD~1", public: Bool = false) -> { url: Url }
  uses fs: Filesystem(mode: Read)
  uses net: Network
{
  current = git.Core.CurrentBranch()
  changes = git.Core.Diff(base: base_ref)
  markdown = render_diff_markdown(diff: changes.diff, branch: current.branch, base_ref: base_ref)
  cred = acquire_gcp_secret(
    runtime: LocalDev,
    project_id: "gunbai-secrets",
    secret_name: "github-token",
    service_account: null,
    header_name: null,
    source_id: "gist",
    required_scopes: ["https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"]
  )
  result = github.Gist.Create(
    description: current.branch,
    content: markdown,
    public: public,
    auth_token: cred.secret
  )
  return { url: result.html_url as Url }
}

func gist_recent(since: String = "3.days.ago", public: Bool = false) -> { url: Url }
  uses fs: Filesystem(mode: Read)
  uses net: Network
{
  current = git.Core.CurrentBranch()
  base = git.Core.RevListBase(since: since)
  changes = git.Core.Diff(base: base.base_ref)
  markdown = render_diff_markdown(
    diff: changes.diff,
    branch: current.branch,
    base_ref: base.base_ref
  )
  cred = acquire_gcp_secret(
    runtime: LocalDev,
    project_id: "gunbai-secrets",
    secret_name: "github-token",
    service_account: null,
    header_name: null,
    source_id: "gist",
    required_scopes: ["https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"]
  )
  result = github.Gist.Create(
    description: current.branch,
    content: markdown,
    public: public,
    auth_token: cred.secret
  )
  return { url: result.html_url as Url }
}

# dsl/tools/infra.dag
```
// tools/infra.dag -- Infra plan/apply/reconcile orchestration contracts.
//
// CG4: express infra intent reconcile orchestration in DSL so runtime
// entrypoints can delegate flow semantics to compiled DAG execution.

module tools.infra

func infra(
  environment: String,
  runtime: String,
  spec_targets: List<String>,
  target: List<String>,
  skip: List<String>,
  execute: Bool
) -> {
  environment: String,
  runtime: String,
  mode: String,
  planned_targets: List<String>,
  target_count: Int,
  applied_count: Int,
  report: String
} {
  targeted = match target |> count() {
    0 => spec_targets,
    _ => spec_targets |> filter(item => target |> filter(t => t == item) |> count() > 0)
  }
  planned_targets = targeted |> filter(item => skip |> filter(s => s == item) |> count() == 0)
  target_count = planned_targets |> count()
  mode = match execute {
    true => "apply",
    false => "plan"
  }
  applied_count = match execute {
    true => target_count,
    false => 0
  }
  report = "infra {mode} (env={environment}, runtime={runtime}): {target_count} target(s)"

  return {
    environment: environment,
    runtime: runtime,
    mode: mode,
    planned_targets: planned_targets,
    target_count: target_count,
    applied_count: applied_count,
    report: report
  }
}

# dsl/tools/justgen.dag
```
// tools/justgen.dag -- Justfile generation.
//
// Renders a Justfile mirroring the Makefile target topology.
// Uses 4-space indentation (Just convention) instead of tabs.
// Tool discovery reuses the makegen extern fn.

module tools.justgen

import std.patterns { content_upsert }
import extdeps.make {
  CoreWorkflow, MetaTargetDef, ResourceTargetEntry,
  ResourceNeed, DiscoveredTool, ExtraTarget, EntrypointParam
}
import config.build_targets {
  core_workflows, meta_targets, resource_targets
}

// ── Shared helpers (prefixed to avoid corpus-wide name collision with ─
// makegen.dag — cross-module fn calls not supported by evaluate_fn_body)

fn just_resolve_resource_target(resource: String, mode: String, res_targets: List<ResourceTargetEntry>) -> String {
  let matches = res_targets |> filter(rt => rt.resource == resource)
  let entry = matches |> first()
  match entry {
    None => ""
    _ => if mode == "ensure" { entry.ensure_target } else { entry.verify_target }
  }
}

fn just_resolve_meta_deps(needs: List<ResourceNeed>, res_targets: List<ResourceTargetEntry>) -> List<String> {
  needs |> map(need => just_resolve_resource_target(resource: need.resource, mode: need.mode, res_targets: res_targets))
        |> filter(dep => dep != "")
}

fn just_resolve_meta_fix_deps(needs: List<ResourceNeed>, res_targets: List<ResourceTargetEntry>) -> List<String> {
  needs |> map(need => just_resolve_resource_target(resource: need.resource, mode: "ensure", res_targets: res_targets))
        |> filter(dep => dep != "")
}

fn just_apply_prefix(prefix: String?, cmd: String) -> String {
  match prefix {
    None => cmd
    _ => "@{prefix} {cmd}"
  }
}

// ── Just-specific helpers ────────────────────────────────────────────

fn normalize_for_just(cmd: String) -> String {
  // $(MAKE) references become just, @ prefix preserved
  cmd
}

fn render_recipe(name: String, deps: List<String>, body: List<String>, comment: String?) -> String {
  let dep_str = deps |> join(" ")
  let header = if dep_str != "" { "{name}: {dep_str}" } else { "{name}:" }
  let recipe = body |> map(line => "    {line}") |> join("\n")
  let comment_line = match comment {
    None => ""
    _ => "# {comment}\n"
  }
  "{comment_line}{header}\n{recipe}\n"
}

// ── Core workflow rendering ──────────────────────────────────────────

fn render_just_core_targets(workflows: List<CoreWorkflow>) -> String {
  workflows |> map(w => render_recipe(
    name: w.name,
    deps: w.deps,
    body: w.body |> map(line => normalize_for_just(cmd: line)),
    comment: w.comment ?? w.description
  )) |> join("\n")
}

// ── Meta target rendering ────────────────────────────────────────────

fn render_just_meta_base(meta: MetaTargetDef, res_targets: List<ResourceTargetEntry>) -> String {
  let deps = just_resolve_meta_deps(needs: meta.resource_needs, res_targets: res_targets)
  let cmd = just_apply_prefix(prefix: meta.command_prefix, cmd: meta.command)
  render_recipe(name: meta.name, deps: deps, body: [cmd], comment: "{meta.name}: {meta.description}")
}

fn render_just_meta_fix(meta: MetaTargetDef, res_targets: List<ResourceTargetEntry>) -> String {
  let fix_deps = meta.fix_prerequisites
  let resource_deps = just_resolve_meta_fix_deps(needs: meta.resource_needs, res_targets: res_targets)
  let all_deps = fix_deps |> append(items: resource_deps)
  let cmd = match meta.fix_command {
    None => just_apply_prefix(prefix: meta.command_prefix, cmd: meta.command)
    _ => just_apply_prefix(prefix: meta.command_prefix, cmd: meta.fix_command)
  }
  render_recipe(name: "{meta.name}-fix", deps: all_deps, body: [cmd], comment: "{meta.name}-fix: auto-fix then verify")
}

fn render_just_meta_check(meta: MetaTargetDef, res_targets: List<ResourceTargetEntry>) -> String {
  let deps = just_resolve_meta_deps(needs: meta.resource_needs, res_targets: res_targets)
  let cmd = match meta.check_command { None => "", _ => meta.check_command }
  if cmd == "" { "" } else {
    render_recipe(name: "{meta.name}-check", deps: deps, body: [cmd], comment: None)
  }
}

fn render_just_meta_target(meta: MetaTargetDef, res_targets: List<ResourceTargetEntry>) -> String {
  let base = render_just_meta_base(meta: meta, res_targets: res_targets)
  let fix = if meta.has_fix { render_just_meta_fix(meta: meta, res_targets: res_targets) } else { "" }
  let check = if meta.has_check { render_just_meta_check(meta: meta, res_targets: res_targets) } else { "" }
  "{base}{fix}{check}"
}

fn render_just_meta_targets(metas: List<MetaTargetDef>, res_targets: List<ResourceTargetEntry>) -> String {
  metas |> map(m => render_just_meta_target(meta: m, res_targets: res_targets)) |> join("\n")
}

// ── Tool target rendering ────────────────────────────────────────────

fn render_just_tool_target(tool: DiscoveredTool) -> String {
  let port_list = tool.entrypoints |> map(p => "{p.port_name} ({p.type_hint})") |> join(", ")
  let main = render_recipe(
    name: tool.short_name,
    deps: tool.deps,
    body: [tool.command],
    comment: "{tool.binary_name} entrypoints: {port_list}"
  )
  let dry = render_recipe(
    name: "{tool.short_name}-dry",
    deps: tool.deps,
    body: [tool.dry_run_command],
    comment: None
  )
  let extras = tool.extra_targets |> map(extra => render_recipe(
    name: "{tool.short_name}-{extra.suffix}",
    deps: [tool.short_name],
    body: extra.post_commands,
    comment: "{tool.short_name}-{extra.suffix}: {extra.description}"
  )) |> join("")
  "{main}\n{dry}\n{extras}"
}

fn render_just_tool_targets(tools: List<DiscoveredTool>) -> String {
  tools |> map(t => render_just_tool_target(tool: t)) |> join("\n")
}

// ── Help target ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────

fn render_just_help() -> String {
  "# Help target\nhelp:\n    @echo \"gunbc tools - generated Justfile\"\n    @echo \"Use 'just <target>' for workflow execution.\"\n"
}

// ── Main rendering ───────────────────────────────────────────────────

fn render_justfile_header() -> String {
  "# Generated by gunbc-justgen\n# DO NOT EDIT - regenerate with: cargo run -p gunbc-app --bin gunbc-justgen\nset shell := [\"bash\", \"-cu\"]\n"
}

fn render_justfile_content(workflows: List<CoreWorkflow>, metas: List<MetaTargetDef>, tools: List<DiscoveredTool>, res_targets: List<ResourceTargetEntry>) -> String {
  let header = render_justfile_header()
  let help = render_just_help()
  let core = render_just_core_targets(workflows: workflows)
  let meta = render_just_meta_targets(metas: metas, res_targets: res_targets)
  let tool = render_just_tool_targets(tools: tools)
  "{header}\n{help}\n{core}\n{meta}\n{tool}"
}

// ── Extern funcs ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────

extern func just_discover_tools() -> List<DiscoveredTool>

// ── Entry point ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────

func justgen(path: String = "Justfile") -> { written: Bool } {
  tools = just_discover_tools()
  content = render_justfile_content(workflows: core_workflows, metas: meta_targets, tools: tools, res_targets: resource_targets)
  result = content_upsert(content: content, path: path)
  return { written: result.written }
}
```

# dsl/tools/makegen.dag
```
// tools/makegen.dag -- Makefile generation.
//
// Renders the project Makefile from DSL data declarations.
// Tool discovery is the only extern fn (Rust inventory introspection).
// All rendering is pure DSL: map, join, string interpolation.

module tools.makegen

import std.patterns { content_upsert }
import extdeps.make {
  MakeTarget, ToolTarget, EntrypointParam,
  CoreWorkflow, MetaTargetDef, ResourceTargetEntry,
  ResourceNeed, DiscoveredTool, ExtraTarget
}
import config.build_targets {
  core_workflows, meta_targets, resource_targets
}

// ── Rendering helpers ──────────────────────────────────────────────

fn render_target(name: String, deps: List<String>, body: List<String>, comment: String?) -> String {
  let dep_str = deps |> join(" ")
  let header = if dep_str != "" { "{name}: {dep_str}" } else { "{name}:" }
  let recipe = body |> map(cmd => "\t{cmd}") |> join("\n")
  let comment_line = match comment {
    None => ""
    _ => "# {comment}\n"
  }
  "{comment_line}{header}\n{recipe}\n"
}

fn render_section_header(title: String) -> String {
  "# ============================================================================\n# {title}\n# ============================================================================\n"
}

fn render_phony_line(names: List<String>) -> String {
  let all_names = names |> join(" ")
  ".PHONY: {all_names}\n"
}

fn resolve_resource_target(resource: String, mode: String, res_targets: List<ResourceTargetEntry>) -> String {
  let matches = res_targets |> filter(rt => rt.resource == resource)
  let entry = matches |> first()
  match entry {
    None => ""
    _ => if mode == "ensure" { entry.ensure_target } else { entry.verify_target }
  }
}

fn resolve_meta_deps(needs: List<ResourceNeed>, res_targets: List<ResourceTargetEntry>) -> List<String> {
  needs |> map(need => resolve_resource_target(resource: need.resource, mode: need.mode, res_targets: res_targets))
        |> filter(dep => dep != "")
}

fn resolve_meta_fix_deps(needs: List<ResourceNeed>, res_targets: List<ResourceTargetEntry>) -> List<String> {
  needs |> map(need => resolve_resource_target(resource: need.resource, mode: "ensure", res_targets: res_targets))
        |> filter(dep => dep != "")
}

fn apply_prefix(prefix: String?, cmd: String) -> String {
  match prefix {
    None => cmd
    _ => "@{prefix} {cmd}"
  }
}

// ── Core workflow rendering ─────────────────────────────────────────

fn render_core_targets(workflows: List<CoreWorkflow>) -> String {
  workflows |> map(w => render_target(
    name: w.name,
    deps: w.deps,
    body: w.body,
    comment: w.comment ?? w.description
  )) |> join("\n")
}

// ── Meta target rendering ───────────────────────────────────────────

fn render_meta_base(meta: MetaTargetDef, res_targets: List<ResourceTargetEntry>) -> String {
  let deps = resolve_meta_deps(needs: meta.resource_needs, res_targets: res_targets)
  let cmd = apply_prefix(prefix: meta.command_prefix, cmd: meta.command)
  render_target(name: meta.name, deps: deps, body: [cmd], comment: "{meta.name}: {meta.description}")
}

fn render_meta_fix_variant(meta: MetaTargetDef, res_targets: List<ResourceTargetEntry>) -> String {
  let fix_deps = meta.fix_prerequisites
  let resource_deps = resolve_meta_fix_deps(needs: meta.resource_needs, res_targets: res_targets)
  let all_deps = fix_deps |> append(items: resource_deps)
  let cmd = match meta.fix_command {
    None => apply_prefix(prefix: meta.command_prefix, cmd: meta.command)
    _ => apply_prefix(prefix: meta.command_prefix, cmd: meta.fix_command)
  }
  render_target(name: "{meta.name}-fix", deps: all_deps, body: [cmd], comment: "{meta.name}-fix: auto-fix then verify")
}

fn render_meta_check_variant(meta: MetaTargetDef, res_targets: List<ResourceTargetEntry>) -> String {
  let deps = resolve_meta_deps(needs: meta.resource_needs, res_targets: res_targets)
  match meta.check_command {
    None => ""
    _ => render_target(name: "{meta.name}-check", deps: deps, body: [meta.check_command], comment: None)
  }
}

fn render_meta_target(meta: MetaTargetDef, res_targets: List<ResourceTargetEntry>) -> String {
  let base = render_meta_base(meta: meta, res_targets: res_targets)
  let fix = if meta.has_fix { render_meta_fix_variant(meta: meta, res_targets: res_targets) } else { "" }
  let check = if meta.has_check { render_meta_check_variant(meta: meta, res_targets: res_targets) } else { "" }
  "{base}{fix}{check}"
}

fn render_meta_targets(metas: List<MetaTargetDef>, res_targets: List<ResourceTargetEntry>) -> String {
  let header = render_section_header(title: "Meta Targets - Development workflow commands")
  let body = metas |> map(m => render_meta_target(meta: m, res_targets: res_targets)) |> join("\n")
  "{header}\n{body}"
}

// ── Tool target rendering ───────────────────────────────────────────

fn render_help_param(p: EntrypointParam) -> String {
  let repeat_suffix = if p.repeatable { " ..." } else { "" }
  match p.default {
    None => "[{p.make_var}=...{repeat_suffix}]"
    _ => "[{p.make_var}={p.default}{repeat_suffix}]"
  }
}

fn render_help_params(params: List<EntrypointParam>) -> String {
  params |> map(p => render_help_param(p: p)) |> join(" ")
}

fn render_tool_target(tool: DiscoveredTool) -> String {
  let port_list = tool.entrypoints |> map(p => "{p.port_name} ({p.type_hint})") |> join(", ")
  let main = render_target(
    name: tool.short_name,
    deps: tool.deps,
    body: [tool.command],
    comment: "{tool.binary_name} entrypoints: {port_list}"
  )
  let dry = render_target(
    name: "{tool.short_name}-dry",
    deps: tool.deps,
    body: [tool.dry_run_command],
    comment: None
  )
  let extras = tool.extra_targets |> map(extra => render_target(
    name: "{tool.short_name}-{extra.suffix}",
    deps: [tool.short_name],
    body: extra.post_commands,
    comment: "{tool.short_name}-{extra.suffix}: {extra.description}"
  )) |> join("")
  "{main}\n{dry}\n{extras}"
}

fn render_tool_targets(tools: List<DiscoveredTool>) -> String {
  tools |> map(t => render_tool_target(tool: t)) |> join("\n")
}

// ── Help target ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────

fn render_help_core_lines(workflows: List<CoreWorkflow>) -> String {
  workflows |> map(w => "\t@echo \"  {w.name}  - {w.comment ?? w.description}\"") |> join("\n")
}

fn fix_description(prereqs: List<String>) -> String {
  let joined = prereqs |> join(" + ")
  if joined != "" { "{joined} first" } else { "auto-fix" }
}

fn render_help_meta_line(m: MetaTargetDef) -> String {
  let base_line = "@echo \"  {m.name}  - {m.description}\""
  let fix_desc = fix_description(prereqs: m.fix_prerequisites)
  let fix_line = if m.has_fix {
    "\n\t@echo \"  {m.name}-fix  - {m.description} ({fix_desc})\""
  } else { "" }
  let check_line = if m.has_check {
    "\n\t@echo \"  {m.name}-check  - {m.description} (check only)\""
  } else { "" }
  "\t{base_line}{fix_line}{check_line}"
}

fn render_help_meta_lines(metas: List<MetaTargetDef>) -> String {
  metas |> map(m => render_help_meta_line(m: m)) |> join("\n")
}

fn render_help_tool_line(t: DiscoveredTool) -> String {
  let params = render_help_params(params: t.entrypoints)
  let main_line = "@echo \"  {t.short_name} {params}  - {t.description}\""
  let extra_lines = t.extra_targets |> map(extra =>
    "\n\t@echo \"  {t.short_name}-{extra.suffix}  - {extra.description}\""
  ) |> join("")
  "\t{main_line}{extra_lines}"
}

fn render_help_tool_lines(tools: List<DiscoveredTool>) -> String {
  tools |> map(t => render_help_tool_line(t: t)) |> join("\n")
}

fn render_help_target(workflows: List<CoreWorkflow>, metas: List<MetaTargetDef>, tools: List<DiscoveredTool>) -> String {
  let header_lines = "help:\n\t@echo \"gunbc tools - generated Makefile\"\n\t@echo \"\"\n\t@echo \"Naming convention:\"\n\t@echo \"  make <target>      - verify only (CI-safe)\"\n\t@echo \"  make <target>-fix  - auto-fix then verify (for dev)\"\n\t@echo \"\""
  let build_section = "\t@echo \"Build commands:\"\n" + render_help_core_lines(workflows: workflows) + "\n\t@echo \"\""
  let dev_section = "\t@echo \"Development:\"\n" + render_help_meta_lines(metas: metas) + "\n\t@echo \"\""
  let tool_section = "\t@echo \"Tools:\"\n" + render_help_tool_lines(tools: tools) + "\n\t@echo \"\"\n\t@echo \"Add -dry suffix for dry-run (e.g., make deps-dry)\""
  "{header_lines}\n{build_section}\n{dev_section}\n{tool_section}\n"
}

// ── Phony line collection ───────────────────────────────────────────
// Build as space-joined strings (avoids need for list concatenation).

fn collect_core_phony_str(workflows: List<CoreWorkflow>) -> String {
  workflows |> map(w => w.name) |> join(" ")
}

fn collect_meta_phony_str(metas: List<MetaTargetDef>) -> String {
  let base = metas |> map(m => m.name) |> join(" ")
  let checks = metas |> filter(m => m.has_check) |> map(m => "{m.name}-check") |> join(" ")
  let fixes = metas |> filter(m => m.has_fix) |> map(m => "{m.name}-fix") |> join(" ")
  "{base} {checks} {fixes}"
}

fn tool_phony_names(t: DiscoveredTool) -> String {
  let base = "{t.short_name} {t.short_name}-dry"
  let extras = t.extra_targets |> map(extra => "{t.short_name}-{extra.suffix}") |> join(" ")
  if extras != "" { "{base} {extras}" } else { base }
}

fn collect_tool_phony_str(tools: List<DiscoveredTool>) -> String {
  tools |> map(t => tool_phony_names(t: t)) |> join(" ")
}

// ── Naming convention header ────────────────────────────────────────

fn render_naming_convention() -> String {
  "# Naming convention:\n#   make <target>      - verify only (CI-safe, fails on issues)\n#   make <target>-fix  - auto-fix then verify (for dev)\n#\n# Dev default:     make test      (ensure generated artifacts, then test)\n# Dev workflow:    make test-fix  (fmt/lint fix + ensure generated artifacts, then test)\n# CI verification: make verify    (check generated artifacts)\n"
}

// ── Main rendering ──────────────────────────────────────────────────

fn render_makefile_body(workflows: List<CoreWorkflow>, metas: List<MetaTargetDef>, tools: List<DiscoveredTool>, res_targets: List<ResourceTargetEntry>) -> String {
  let convention = render_naming_convention()
  let default_goal = ".DEFAULT_GOAL := help\n"
  let core_phony = collect_core_phony_str(workflows: workflows)
  let meta_phony = collect_meta_phony_str(metas: metas)
  let tool_phony = collect_tool_phony_str(tools: tools)
  let phony = ".PHONY: help {core_phony} {meta_phony} {tool_phony}\n"
  let core = render_core_targets(workflows: workflows)
  let help = render_help_target(workflows: workflows, metas: metas, tools: tools)
  let meta = render_meta_targets(metas: metas, res_targets: res_targets)
  let tool = render_tool_targets(tools: tools)
  "{convention}\n{default_goal}\n{phony}\n{core}\n{help}\n{meta}\n{tool}"
}

// ── Extern funcs ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
// Tool discovery uses Rust inventory introspection (only remaining extern).

extern func discover_tools() -> List<DiscoveredTool>

// ── Makefile header ─────────────────────────────────────────────────

fn render_header() -> String {
  "# Generated by gunbc-makegen\n# DO NOT EDIT - regenerate with: cargo run -p gunbc-app --bin gunbc-makegen\n"
}

// ── Full content assembly ─────────────────────────────────────────────

fn render_makefile_content(workflows: List<CoreWorkflow>, metas: List<MetaTargetDef>, tools: List<DiscoveredTool>, res_targets: List<ResourceTargetEntry>) -> String {
  let header = render_header()
  let body = render_makefile_body(workflows: workflows, metas: metas, tools: tools, res_targets: res_targets)
  "{header}{body}"
}

// ── Entry point ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────

func makegen(path: String = "Makefile") -> { written: Bool } {
  tools = discover_tools()
  content = render_makefile_content(workflows: core_workflows, metas: meta_targets, tools: tools, res_targets: resource_targets)
  result = content_upsert(content: content, path: path)
  return { written: result.written }
}
```

# dsl/tools/pragma.dag
```
// tools/pragma.dag -- Pragma config file generation.
//
// Generates 3 config files from canonical policy derivation functions.
// Rendering is delegated to explicit extern funcs that evaluate
// config/clippy_policy.dag via Rust-side DSL evaluation.
//
//   1. clippy.toml                    -- Clippy configuration
//   2. disallowed-methods-allowlist.txt -- Method allowlist
//   3. pragma-lint-policy.txt         -- Lint policy rules
//
// Replaces: gunbc-app/src/pragma/graph.rs (~19 nodes)

module tools.pragma

import std.patterns { content_upsert }
import std.types { PragmaDirective }

extern func render_clippy_toml_content(directives: List<PragmaDirective>) -> { return: String }
extern func render_disallowed_methods_allowlist_content(directives: List<PragmaDirective>) -> { return: String }
extern func render_pragma_lint_policy_content(directives: List<PragmaDirective>) -> { return: String }

func pragma(directives: List<PragmaDirective>) -> { success: Bool, clippy_written: Bool, allowlist_written: Bool, policy_written: Bool } {
  clippy_content = render_clippy_toml_content(directives: directives)
  clippy = content_upsert(
    content: clippy_content.return,
    path: "clippy.toml"
  )

  allowlist_content = render_disallowed_methods_allowlist_content(directives: directives)
  allowlist = content_upsert(
    content: allowlist_content.return,
    path: "tools/disallowed-methods-allowlist.txt"
  )

  policy_content = render_pragma_lint_policy_content(directives: directives)
  policy = content_upsert(
    content: policy_content.return,
    path: "tools/pragma-lint-policy.txt"
  )

  return {
    success: true,
    clippy_written: clippy.written,
    allowlist_written: allowlist.written,
    policy_written: policy.written
  }
}

# dsl/tools/testgen.dag
```
// tools/testgen.dag -- Test generation for all DAG specs.
//
// Discovers all DagSpecDef targets (via inventory), generates test
// content for each, and content_upserts the results in parallel.
// This is a dynamic parallel pattern: N targets, each getting an
// independent content_upsert chain.
//
// Replaces: gunbc-app/src/testgen_dag/graph.rs (1 + N*6 nodes)

module tools.testgen

import std.patterns { content_upsert }
import std.types { CodegenTarget }

fn generate_tests(target: CodegenTarget) -> String {
  target |> generate()
}

func testgen(targets: List<CodegenTarget>) -> { success: Bool, all_fresh: Bool }
  uses fs: Filesystem(mode: ReadWrite)
{
  results = for target in targets {
    content = generate_tests(target: target)
    content_upsert(content: content, path: target.path)
  }

  return { success: true, all_fresh: results |> all(r => r.written == false) }
}

// workflows/gist.dag
//
// Replaces WF16/WF17/WF18 gist workflow specs.
//
// Supported modes:
// - gist / gist-snapshot / snapshot
// - gist-diff / diff
// - gist-recent / recent
//
// Stage topology by mode:
// snapshot: compilation_ensure -> codegen_ensure -> list_files -> read_files -> render_snapshot -> gist_create -> report
// diff:     compilation_ensure -> codegen_ensure -> diff -> render_diff -> gist_create -> report
// recent:   compilation_ensure -> codegen_ensure -> rev_list -> diff -> render_diff -> gist_create -> report
//
// Shared base edges for all modes:
// codegen_ensure -> branch_resolution -> gist_create
// codegen_ensure -> credential_resolve -> gist_create

module workflows.gist

import shared.compilation { compilation_ensure }
import shared.codegen { codegen_ensure }

pipeline gist {

  stage compilation_ensure {    _ = compilation_ensure()
  }

  stage codegen_ensure [after compilation_ensure] {
    _ = codegen_ensure()
  }

  stage branch_resolution [after codegen_ensure] {
  }

  stage credential_resolve [after codegen_ensure] {
  }

  stage list_files [after codegen_ensure, when mode == "gist" || mode == "gist-snapshot"] {
  }

  stage read_files [after list_files, when mode == "gist" || mode == "gist-snapshot"] {
  }

  stage render_snapshot [after read_files, when mode == "gist" || mode == "gist-snapshot"] {}

  stage rev_list [after codegen_ensure, when mode == "gist-recent"] {
  }

  stage diff [after codegen_ensure, after rev_list, when mode == "gist-diff" || mode == "gist-recent"] {
  }

  stage render_diff [after diff, when mode == "gist-diff" || mode == "gist-recent"] {}

  stage gist_create [
    after branch_resolution,
    after credential_resolve,
    after render_snapshot,
    after render_diff,
    when mode == "gist" || mode == "gist-snapshot"
      || mode == "gist-diff"
      || mode == "gist-recent"
  ] {
  }

  stage report [after gist_create] {}
}

# dsl/workflows/makegen.dag
```
// workflows/makegen.dag
//
// Makefile generation pipeline.
//
// Replaces the standalone `func makegen()` entry point with a staged
// pipeline that makes each phase observable and testable:
//
//   compilation_ensure -> codegen_ensure -> load_registry ->
//   render_makefile -> upsert_makefile -> report
//
// Data flow:
//   load_registry: discover tools via Rust inventory introspection
//   render_makefile: assemble Makefile content from data + tools
//   upsert_makefile: write content to disk if changed
//   report: emit success/failure result

module workflows.makegen

import shared.compilation { compilation_ensure }
import shared.codegen { codegen_ensure }
import tools.makegen {
  discover_tools,
  render_makefile_content
}
import config.build_targets {
  core_workflows, meta_targets, resource_targets
}
import std.patterns { content_upsert }

pipeline makegen {

  stage compilation_ensure {
    _ = compilation_ensure()
  }

  stage codegen_ensure [after compilation_ensure] {
    _ = codegen_ensure()
  }

  // Discover tools from Rust inventory (extern func).
  stage load_registry [after codegen_ensure] {
    tools = discover_tools()
  }

  // Render Makefile content from data declarations + discovered tools.
  stage render_makefile [after load_registry] {
    content = render_makefile_content(
      workflows: core_workflows,
      metas: meta_targets,
      tools: tools,
      res_targets: resource_targets
    )
  }

  // Write rendered Makefile to disk (idempotent: skips if unchanged).
  stage upsert_makefile [after render_makefile] {
    result = content_upsert(content: content, path: "Makefile")
  }

  stage report [after upsert_makefile] {
    success = result.written
  }
}
```

# dsl/workflows/sdlc.dag
```
// workflows/sdlc.dag
//
// Planner SDLC workflow used by gunbc-workflow.
//
// Orchestrates: prerequisites → intake → worker dispatch → report.
// The worker stage calls dispatch_sdlc() which discovers issues,
// acquires claims, dispatches per-stage handlers, and records outcomes.

module workflows.sdlc

import shared.compilation { compilation_ensure }
import shared.codegen { codegen_ensure }
import funcs.sdlc_worker { dispatch_sdlc }
import shared.dag_util { aggregate_results, format_report, stage_result }
import std.types { StageResult, Summary }

// Pipeline parameters — bound at invocation time (CLI, webhook, cron).
param sdlc_owner: String = "gunb-ai"
param sdlc_repo: String = "gunbc"
param sdlc_worker_id: String = "workflows.sdlc"
param sdlc_llm_provider: String = "anthropic"
param sdlc_llm_model: String = "claude-sonnet-4-20250514"

pipeline sdlc {

  stage compilation_ensure {
    _ = compilation_ensure()
  }

  stage codegen_ensure [after compilation_ensure] {
    _ = codegen_ensure()
  }

  // Intake: lightweight gate before worker dispatch.
  // dispatch_sdlc() handles discovery internally; this stage
  // validates that prerequisites completed and pipeline params exist.
  stage intake [after codegen_ensure] {
    intake_ok = sdlc_owner != "" && sdlc_repo != ""
  }

  // Worker: core SDLC dispatch loop.
  // Discovers SDLC-labeled issues, claims each, dispatches handlers,
  // records outcomes. One stage transition per issue per invocation.
  stage worker [after intake, when intake_ok] {
    worker_result = dispatch_sdlc(
      owner: sdlc_owner,
      repo: sdlc_repo,
      worker_id: sdlc_worker_id,
      llm_provider: sdlc_llm_provider,
      llm_model: sdlc_llm_model
    )
  }

  // Report: aggregate worker results into a summary.
  stage report [after worker] {
    summary = aggregate_results(stages: worker_result.stages)
    report_text = format_report(summary: summary, stages: worker_result.stages)
  }
}
```

# dsl/workflows/webhook.dag
```
// workflows/webhook.dag -- SP-7: Webhook-driven stage transitions.
//
// Cloud Run HTTP endpoint that receives GitHub webhook events and
// triggers SDLC pipeline stage transitions.
//
// Architecture:
//   GitHub --> webhook HTTP POST --> Cloud Run --> webhook handler
//                                      |
//                                      +--> validate signature
//                                      +--> parse event
//                                      +--> classify event type
//                                      +--> emit signal to SignalStore
//                                      +--> dispatch worker if immediate
//
// Supported webhook events:
//   - issues.labeled:    New SDLC label -> WorkReady signal
//   - issues.unlabeled:  SDLC label removed -> reconciliation check
//   - issue_comment.created: Approval comment -> ApprovalGranted signal
//   - pull_request.closed:   PR merged -> TestReady signal
//   - pull_request.review:   Review submitted -> ReviewComplete signal
//
// Security:
//   - HMAC-SHA256 signature verification (X-Hub-Signature-256 header)
//   - Webhook secret stored in Secret Manager
//   - Cloud Run IAM restricts who can invoke the endpoint
//
// Idempotency:
//   - Each webhook delivery has a unique X-GitHub-Delivery ID
//   - Signal idempotency_key includes delivery ID
//   - Duplicate deliveries produce no additional signals

module workflows.webhook

import interfaces.signal_store { SignalStore }
import interfaces.credential_provider { CredentialProvider }
import std.types {
  NonEmptyStr, Signal, SignalType, CredentialFlow, AccessToken
}
import std.state_machines { label_to_stage }

// ── Webhook event types ─────────────────────────────────────────────

type WebhookEvent
  = IssueLabeled { issue_number: Int, label: String, sender: String }
  | IssueUnlabeled { issue_number: Int, label: String, sender: String }
  | IssueCommentCreated { issue_number: Int, body: String, sender: String }
  | PullRequestClosed { pr_number: Int, merged: Bool, head_branch: String, sender: String }
  | PullRequestReview { pr_number: Int, state: String, sender: String }
  | Unknown { event_type: String }

type WebhookResponse {
  status: Int
  message: String
  signal_emitted: Bool
}

// ── Event classification ────────────────────────────────────────────

fn is_sdlc_label(label: String) -> Bool {
  label |> starts_with(prefix: "sdlc:")
}

fn is_approval_comment(body: String) -> Bool {
  body |> starts_with(prefix: "/approve") || body |> starts_with(prefix: "LGTM")
}

fn event_to_signal_type(event: WebhookEvent) -> SignalType? {
  match event {
    IssueLabeled { issue_number, label } => {
      stage = label_to_stage(label: label)
      match stage {
        Some(s) => WorkReady { issue_id: "{issue_number}", stage: s, stage_epoch: 1 }
        None => None
      }
    }
    IssueUnlabeled { issue_number, label } => if is_sdlc_label(label: label) {
      ReconcileTick { window_id: "issue-{issue_number}" }
    } else {
      None
    }
    IssueCommentCreated { issue_number, body } => if is_approval_comment(body: body) {
      ApprovalGranted { issue_id: "{issue_number}", stage: DesignReview, approval_epoch: 1 }
    } else {
      None
    }
    PullRequestClosed { pr_number, merged } => if merged {
      WorkReady { issue_id: "{pr_number}", stage: Testing, stage_epoch: 1 }
    } else {
      None
    }
    PullRequestReview { pr_number, state } => if state == "approved" {
      ApprovalGranted { issue_id: "{pr_number}", stage: CodeReview, approval_epoch: 1 }
    } else {
      None
    }
    Unknown => None
  }
}

fn event_to_issue_id(event: WebhookEvent) -> String? {
  match event {
    IssueLabeled { issue_number } => "{issue_number}"
    IssueUnlabeled { issue_number } => "{issue_number}"
    IssueCommentCreated { issue_number } => "{issue_number}"
    PullRequestClosed { pr_number } => "{pr_number}"
    PullRequestReview { pr_number } => "{pr_number}"
    Unknown => None
  }
}

fn event_to_stage(event: WebhookEvent) -> String? {
  match event {
    IssueLabeled { label } => label
    IssueUnlabeled { label } => label
    IssueCommentCreated {} => "approval"
    PullRequestClosed { merged } => if merged { "testing" } else { None }
    PullRequestReview { state } => if state == "approved" { "code-review" } else { None }
    Unknown => None
  }
}

// ── HMAC signature verification ─────────────────────────────────────

fn hmac_sha256(key: String, data: String) -> String {
  "{key}:{data}" |> hash()
}

fn verify_signature(payload: String, signature: String, secret: String) -> Bool {
  // HMAC-SHA256 verification.
  // The expected signature format is: sha256=<hex digest>
  let expected = "sha256={hmac_sha256(key: secret, data: payload)}"
  expected == signature
}

// ── Webhook handler ─────────────────────────────────────────────────

func handle_webhook(
  event: WebhookEvent,
  delivery_id: NonEmptyStr,
  signature: String,
  payload: String
) -> { response: WebhookResponse }
  uses signals: SignalStore
  uses creds: CredentialProvider
{
  // Step 1: Verify webhook signature
  webhook_secret = creds.acquire(
    secret_name: "github-webhook-secret",
    flow: Stored { secret_name: "github-webhook-secret" },
    scheme: Bearer,
    source_id: "webhook",
    required_scopes: []
  )

  valid = verify_signature(
    payload: payload,
    signature: signature,
    secret: webhook_secret.token.token
  )

  if !valid {
    return {
      response: ({
        status: 401,
        message: "Invalid webhook signature",
        signal_emitted: false
      } as WebhookResponse)
    }
  }

  // Step 2: Classify event and determine signal type
  signal_type = event_to_signal_type(event: event)

  match signal_type {
    None => {
      return {
        response: ({
          status: 200,
          message: "Event type not actionable",
          signal_emitted: false
        } as WebhookResponse)
      }
    }
    Some(signal_type_value) => {
      // Step 3: Emit signal to SignalStore (idempotent via delivery_id)
      issue_id = event_to_issue_id(event: event)
      stage = event_to_stage(event: event)

      signal_result = signals.emit(signal: {
        signal_type: signal_type_value,
        idempotency_key: "webhook::{delivery_id}",
        payload: {
          issue_id: issue_id,
          stage: stage,
          source: "github-webhook",
          delivery_id: delivery_id
        },
        produced_at: "now"
      })

      return {
        response: ({
          status: if signal_result.emitted { 200 } else { 500 },
          message: if signal_result.emitted { "Signal emitted" } else { "Failed to emit signal" },
          signal_emitted: signal_result.emitted
        } as WebhookResponse)
      }
    }
  }
}

// ── Tests ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

fixture webhook_env {
  mock creds.acquire.response -> {
    token: { token: "whsec_test_secret", scheme: "Bearer", source_id: "webhook" }

# gunbc-app/src/bin/ci.rs
```
//! gunbc-ci main entry point.
//!
//! This is a handwritten main.rs (not generated) because the CI tool is the
//! bootstrap that runs codegen for all other tools. It cannot depend on
//! generated code because it needs to run BEFORE codegen.
//!
//! The CI pipeline uses the resource acquisition pattern internally - the
//! `prep` node checks if codegen is needed and runs it if so.
//!
//! # Resource Mode
//!
//! The `--mode` flag controls how stale resources are handled:
//! - `--mode=ensure` (default): Run codegen if stale/missing
//! - `--mode=verify`: Fail if codegen is stale/missing (CI strict mode)
//!
//! # GitHub Actions Integration
//!
//! When running in GitHub Actions, this tool emits `::group::` commands
//! for each DAG node, creating collapsible sections in the Actions UI.
//! This gives visibility into each step (prep, build, test, lint, report)
//! without requiring separate workflow steps.

#![deny(dead_code)]
use gunbc_cli::{parse, CliParam, ParamType};
use gunbc_dag::build_build_graph;
use gunbc_dag::resources::MAKEFILE_OUTPUT_PATH;
use gunbc_dag::{print_tool_header, run_tool, wire_fs_env_write_mock, RunToolOptions};
use gunbc_exec::{print_attention, AttentionLevel, BoundaryMocks, CiContext, ExecutionMode};
use gunbc_ir::resource::ExecMode;
use gunbc_ir::{detect_entrypoints, Value};
use gunbc_testgen_registry::iter_dag_specs;
use std::process;

fn ci_generated_tests_path() -> Option<&'static str> {
    iter_dag_specs()
        .find(|spec| spec.name == "ci")
        .map(|spec| spec.meta.output_path)
}

fn ci_path_for_node(node_id: &str) -> Option<&'static str> {
    if node_id.contains("Find_ListDirs") {
        Some("crates")
    } else if node_id.contains("makegen") {
        Some(MAKEFILE_OUTPUT_PATH)
    } else if node_id.contains("render_and_upsert")
        || node_id == "std.patterns::content_upsert"
        || node_id == "std.patterns::file_content_matches"
    {
        ci_generated_tests_path()
    } else {
        None
    }
}

fn main() {
    let argv: Vec<String> = std::env::args().collect();
    let parsed = match parse(
        &argv,
        &[CliParam::new("mode", ParamType::Str).default("ensure")],
    ) {
        Ok(parsed) => parsed,
        Err(error) => {
            print_attention(
                AttentionLevel::Error,
                "CI argument parsing failed",
                &error.to_string(),
            );
            process::exit(1);
        }
    };
    if parsed.help {
        print_help();
        return;
    }

    let dry_run = parsed.dry_run;
    let mode = parsed
        .values
        .get("mode")
        .and_then(Value::as_str)
        .unwrap_or("ensure");
    let resource_mode = ExecMode::parse_strict(mode).unwrap_or_else(|_| {
        print_attention(
            AttentionLevel::Error,
            "Invalid --mode value",
            "expected one of: ensure, verify",
        );
        process::exit(1);
    });

    // Runtime CI path uses the concrete build/test/lint DAG.
    let dag = match build_build_graph() {
        Ok(d) => d,
        Err(e) => {
            print_attention(
                AttentionLevel::Error,
                "CI graph build failed",
                &e.to_string(),
            );
            process::exit(1);
        }
    };

    // Set up entrypoint inputs for lower-time content_upsert/service args that
    // are still injected by tool frontends.
    let mut input_mocks = BoundaryMocks::new();
    let mut unresolved_path_nodes = Vec::<String>::new();
    let entrypoints = detect_entrypoints(&dag);
    for (node_id, port_name, _) in &entrypoints.entrypoint_ports {
        match port_name.0.as_str() {
            "check_mode" => {
                input_mocks.set_input(
                    node_id.0.clone(),
                    port_name.0.clone(),
                    Value::Bool(resource_mode == ExecMode::Verify),
                );
            }
            "path" => {
                if let Some(path) = ci_path_for_node(&node_id.0) {
                    input_mocks.set_input(
                        node_id.0.clone(),
                        port_name.0.clone(),
                        Value::Str(path.to_string()),
                    );
                } else {
                    unresolved_path_nodes.push(node_id.0.clone());
                }
            }
            "max_depth" if node_id.0.contains("Find_ListDirs") => {
                input_mocks.set_input(node_id.0.clone(), port_name.0.clone(), Value::Int(1));
            }
            "min_depth" if node_id.0.contains("Find_ListDirs") => {
                input_mocks.set_input(node_id.0.clone(), port_name.0.clone(), Value::Int(1));
            }
            _ => {}
        }
    }
    if !unresolved_path_nodes.is_empty() {
        unresolved_path_nodes.sort();
        unresolved_path_nodes.dedup();
        print_attention(
            AttentionLevel::Error,
            "CI entrypoint path wiring is incomplete",
            &format!(
                "unmapped path entrypoints: {}",
                unresolved_path_nodes.join(", ")
            ),
        );
        process::exit(1);
    }

    // Set up execution mode
    let mode = if dry_run {
        let mut mocks = BoundaryMocks::new();
        wire_fs_env_write_mock(&dag, &mut mocks);
        ExecutionMode::DryRun(mocks)
    } else {
        ExecutionMode::Real
    };

    // Detect CI environment
    let ci = CiContext::detect();
    let is_ci = ci.provider_id() != "plain";

    let mut metadata = vec![
        ("exec", if dry_run { "dry-run" } else { "real" }.to_string()),
        (
            "resource_mode",
            match resource_mode {
                ExecMode::Verify => "verify (fail on stale)",
                ExecMode::Ensure => "ensure (fix stale)",
            }
            .to_string(),
        ),
    ];
    if is_ci {
        metadata.push(("ci", ci.provider_name().to_string()));
    }
    let tool_name = gunbc_ir::cargo::name("ci");
    print_tool_header(&tool_name, &metadata);

    run_tool(
        dag,
        mode,
        RunToolOptions {
            success_port: Some("success"),
            freshness: gunbc_dag::FreshnessScope::GenerationOnly,
            input_mocks: Some(&input_mocks),
        },
    );
}

fn print_help() {
    let name = gunbc_ir::cargo::name("ci");
    println!("{name} - CI orchestration tool");
    println!();
    println!("USAGE:");
    println!("    {name} [OPTIONS]");
    println!();
    println!("OPTIONS:");
    println!("    -n, --dry-run       Don't perform actual I/O");
    println!("    --mode=MODE         Resource acquisition mode:");
    println!("                          ensure - run codegen if stale/missing (default)");
    println!("                          verify - fail if codegen is stale/missing");
    println!("    -h, --help          Print this help");
    println!();
    println!("EXAMPLES:");
    println!("    {name}              # Run CI with auto-codegen if needed");
    println!("    {name} --mode=verify  # Strict mode: fail if codegen stale");
    println!("    {name} --dry-run    # Preview without I/O");
    println!();
    println!("The CI pipeline runs: SetupDeps -> Prep -> Build -> Test/Lint -> Report");
    println!();
    println!("The Prep stage uses manifest-based freshness checking.");
    println!("In 'ensure' mode, stale resources are regenerated automatically.");
    println!("In 'verify' mode, stale resources cause CI to fail immediately.");
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::ci_path_for_node;
    use gunbc_dag::resources::MAKEFILE_OUTPUT_PATH;

    #[test]
    fn maps_makegen_entrypoints_to_makefile_path() {
        assert_eq!(
            ci_path_for_node("param_source_tools_makegen_makegen_path"),
            Some(MAKEFILE_OUTPUT_PATH)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            ci_path_for_node("tools.makegen::makegen"),
            Some(MAKEFILE_OUTPUT_PATH)
        );
    }

    // NOTE: full_freshness_with_build_dag_is_rejected removed.
    // Naive overlap detection replaced by C22 (Deductive Redundancy Elimination).

    /// Validates that generation-only freshness steps compose cleanly
    /// with the build DAG (no overlap — generation steps have no subsumes).
    #[test]
    fn generation_freshness_with_build_dag_is_accepted() {
        use gunbc_exec::{compose_with_freshness, FreshnessStep};

        let dag = gunbc_dag::build_build_graph().expect("build graph should compile");

        let gen_steps = vec![
            FreshnessStep {
                id: "codegen".into(),
                command: vec!["echo".into(), "codegen".into()],
                subsumes: None,
            },
            FreshnessStep {
                id: "testgen".into(),
                command: vec!["echo".into(), "testgen".into()],
                subsumes: None,
            },
        ];

        let result = compose_with_freshness(dag, Some(gen_steps));
        assert!(
            result.is_ok(),
            "generation-only freshness steps should not overlap with build DAG: {:?}",
            result.err()
        );
    }
}
